> · **F1 — one target at a time** (atoms/stack.js `placeCopyForPerson`, the one site every copy that may take new targets goes through — `applyCopySpell` (a targeted body), `applyCopySelfSpell`, `applyCopyInstantOrSorcery` with `newTargets`, `applyCopyActivatedAbility` / `applyCopyTargetAbility` with `newTargets`, the parser setting the flag where the permission is printed; targeting.js `newTargetPositions` / `newTargetCandidates` / `advanceNewTargets`, the pw26 per-opponent pattern). Round 1 offered whole target sets from `expandCastChoices`, whose 64-row cap left most sets of a multi-target copy unreachable and never offered a mixed "keep this one, change that one" set (the review's three boards: 89 of 117, 52 of 125, 46 of 136). Now each recorded target is a position, asked in order, offering "keep" — the target as it stands, legal or not (CR 707.10c, 115.7d) — and every legal object for that slot: the pool the CR 608.2b re-check rebuilds for it (`offeredTargetSlot`; an untagged storm target the program's first targeting atom), enumerated for the copy's controller with its colours, X and context, an opponent-bound slot (Grasp of Fate's `slotPlayer`) narrowed to that opponent, never the object itself (CR 115.5). A value is offered only when the later positions can still be completed legally — distinct within one instance of "target" (CR 115.3), a pair atom's two objects distinct, an atom's joint constraints (total mana value X or less, a single graveyard, a shared creature type, cards from the chosen player's graveyard) holding whenever one of its targets changed (CR 115.7d — "must not cause any unchanged targets to become illegal") — by a keep-first search that checks them on the targets chosen so far at every position (R2-F1 below; its 20,000-step bound now a logged backstop). No product, no cap: every legal final set is reachable and nothing illegal is. **Dependent slots:** no credited copy card has them of its own — they come from what is copied (Twincast can copy any instant or sorcery): the pair atoms (fight, damage-equal-to-power), the player-and-cards atom, total-mana-value, single-graveyard and shared-type subsets; each is handled by the same completion check (`atomTargetSetOk`), witnessed here for the instance rule (Rishkar), the per-opponent binding (Grasp of Fate) and the player-and-cards and single-graveyard atoms (R2-F1). A position with one legal value is filled unasked; a copy with no real choice anywhere keeps its targets, or is removed when the house pick finds no legal target, as for every seat. The waiting copy carries `awaitingCopyTargets` (`positions`, `chosen`, `at`, the aligned house pick as `house`, `sourceName`, a storm copy's `copyNumber` / `copyCount`); the driver raises the `copy-targets` pause (one position per question, `slotNumber` / `slotCount`) before the trigger-order and trigger-target raises; `settleCopyTargetsChoice` recomputes the same list, fills the position, and with the last answer writes the targets, records their wards (every target — the copy is a new object) and runs their events (F3).
> · **F2 — the self-copy's colours** (CR 707.2, 707.10, 702.16b, 608.2b): `selfCopySource` names the copied spell's colours — `ctx.spellColors` from `resolveOptionalChoice` (the resolving spell's card, read through `resolutionSource`) or Chain of Vapor's `copyColors` (`applyChainBounce` stamps the resolving object's; `runEffectProgram` hands the chain-bounce atom `spellColors` when its source names colours); a copy of the copy reads its own source's. Before, the self-copy's source was its name and type only, so protection from blue never refused Chain of Vapor's copy — for either seat (the review's probe: Yavimaya Barbarian, Great Sable Stag, Iridescent Angel offered and bounced). > · **F3 — a copy's targets become its targets, every seat** (CR 601.2c's last sentence, 707.10c): `copyTargetEvents` runs `checkBecomesTargetTriggers` and `applyKiraTargetCounter` with the copy's own id at every site that puts a copy on the stack with targets — the house sites (storm, the self-copy, the instant or sorcery copy, "copy that spell", both ability copies), a person's copy placed unasked, and a person's last answer (learnSession `settleCopyTargets` flushes what they queued once nothing waits, as `finishTriggerTargets` does for a trigger's targets). Ward is not one of them: it stays the copy's `wardOwed`, recorded once with the targets, so it is asked exactly once per copy (wardCopies.test.js's ask lists, unchanged).
> · **F4 — a copied activated ability's controller** (CR 707.10, 603.3a, 301.5d): `applyCopyActivatedAbility` gives the copy (and its program) the copy trigger's controller (`ctx.controller`) — Illusionist's and Battlemage's Bracers: the Equipment's, not the equipped creature's — and asks that seat. Kurkesh and Rings of Brighthearth ("whenever you activate") put the copy under the original's own controller, so they are unchanged; the target-keyed arms (Strionic Resonator, Kirol, Adric, Peter Parker's Camera, Vantress Visions) copy abilities their copier controls.
> · **F6 — Deflecting Swat** (CR 115.7d): a person's Swat marks the targeted spell or ability (`awaitingCopyTargets` with `retarget` and its `chooser`) and asks them its targets one at a time — keep, or any legal object as the object's controller would target it, whoever it is aimed at; the answer changes the targets in place, records a ward and runs the becomes-the-target events only on the targets that changed (the unchanged ones were already its targets — R2-F3). The panel words it "Choose new targets for <spell>". Every AI seat keeps applyRetarget's deflection.

> · **R2-F1 — the joint constraints pruned at every target** (the round-2 recheck: FP, a person's seat; targeting.js `atomTargetSetOk` / `newTargetCandidates` / `advanceNewTargets`): an atom's joint constraints were checked only at its last position, so the completion search walked the whole product of the middle positions before it could reject anything; its 20,000-step bound then dropped legal values on ordinary graveyards, later seats first, and `advanceNewTargets` filled a position with its one surviving value unasked (the review's boards: Memory's Journey, Dwell on the Past and Stream of Consciousness lost ai2 and ai3 at the player, or never asked it; Shred Memory lost ai2's and ai3's graveyards). Each constraint is monotone — cards from the chosen player's graveyard (the player comes first), one graveyard, total mana value at most X (mana values are never negative), a shared creature type, a pair's distinct objects — so `okAt` now checks the atom's targets chosen so far at every position once one of them has changed, and a dead branch is cut where it starts: a completion takes about positions × pool steps. One candidate computation on the twenty-card boards: **0–4 ms** after; on 046b63f9, at the first question, Memory's Journey 17 ms, the Swat 159, Dwell on the Past 640, Stream of Consciousness 637, Shred Memory 477, Rapid Decay 73. The bound stays as a backstop only: `newTargetCandidates` returns `budgetHit`, the raise logs `copy-targets-search-budget` (reached on no witness board), and `advanceNewTargets` never fills such a position unasked.
> · **R2-F2 — one batch** (FP, trigger order; CR 603.3b, 101.4): `checkCopyTriggers` (magecraft, "whenever you copy") ran as a person's copy was placed, so the engine flushed those triggers right after the resolution that made the copy, before the question, and the answers' becomes-the-target triggers went on as a second batch — an active player's trigger landed above a non-active player's, and a person's own triggers from one event were split with no order question. > · **Not taken:** **Scroll Rack** (#1373) — "{1}, {T}: Exile any number of cards from your hand face down. Put that many cards from the top of your library into your hand. Then look at the exiled cards and put them on top of your library in any order." A person picks ANY number of hand cards, none included: no pending choice asks that — the hand prompts (hand-to-library-top, Brainstorm's put-back; discard; cleanup-discard) take a fixed `remaining`, one card per settle, and their panel submits only a card, never "done". The order could ride the scry-surveil reorder (Ponder's), the selection can't. A new prompt. **Glissa Sunslayer** (#1375) — its third mode, "Remove up to three counters from target permanent.": no atom removes counters from a target, and which counters — how many of each kind, chosen as it resolves (its ruling) — has no prompt a person can be asked (distribute-counters spreads one kind among permanents; edict-mode and protection-color pick a mode or a colour). A new prompt; the other two modes play. **All Will Be One** (#1393) — "Whenever you put one or more counters on a permanent or player, this enchantment deals that much damage to target opponent, creature an opponent controls, or planeswalker an opponent controls." It triggers once per placement event per object (its ruling: counters placed as a single event trigger it once), with the placer named, on permanents and players; the engine's record is the incomplete one above, and the damage target (an opponent, or a creature or planeswalker an opponent controls) has no target type. The counters-put event model is an engine slice. **Thousand-Year Storm** (#1398) — "a person's choice of new targets for spell copies: the copy-target engine slice" (the coordinator's reason: `stack.freshCopyTargets` / `newTargetsForCopy` are a house pick for every seat; not touched here). **Terastodon** (#1421) — "When this creature enters, you may destroy up to three target noncreature permanents. For each permanent put into a graveyard this way, its controller creates a 3/3 green Elephant creature token." — "up to three targets: past the 64-row cap a person can't reach most target sets; a pick-one-target-at-a-time question is the lane" (the blind review's F1, the coordinator's reason); its "put into a graveyard this way" half is built and kept.

> · **Which payers are one choice** (the coordinator's fold-in from pw29's round-2 recheck, R2-F1 — the same class in this slice's key): the counted-tap key (name, summoning sickness, counters, attachments) merged permanents a person can tell apart, then kept one member per group, so a legal choice was lost: a blocker with an idle creature, a layer-1 copy or an entered clone with the real card, a pumped or exerted creature with an untouched one, a different chosen type, colour or imprint, monstrous or renowned. One shared helper, `legalChoices.interchangeablePayerKey(state, perm)` (exported for pw29's counted sacrifice): the permanent's own id unless it equals the other apart from its id and its card's id AND nothing else on the state (the log aside) names it — combat, a continuous effect, a stack object, a pending or delayed trigger, an end-of-combat entry, a ledger; when in doubt, by id (CR 601.2h, 602.2b, 509.1h, 707.2). `payerLabels` names each payer by its printed name plus what tells it apart ("Merfolk (blocking Hill Giant)", "Clone (copy of Merfolk of the Pearl Trident, summoning sick)"), and two that key apart but would read alike carry their ids. Witnessed in baralChiefOfCompliance.test.js: seven Merfolk tokens beside the Mentor, one blocking the AI's Hill Giant, the AI's Lightning Bolt on the stack — three offers, the one that keeps the blocker untapped among them (taken: the Bolt countered, the blocker untapped and blocking, the person on 40), the blocker labelled; a Clone that entered as a copy of Merfolk of the Pearl Trident beside the real one — four offers (each of the two kept back on its own), both labelled. > · **Not taken:** **Mirage Mirror** (#1312) — "{2}: This artifact becomes a copy of target artifact, creature, enchantment, or land until end of turn." The copy is read by the activated, mana and type readers, but `liveTriggerCard`, `staticEffectsOf`, `selfPreventsUntap`, the attached bonus and Equip readers, the `effectiveTypeIdentity` seed and `applyLegendRule` read the printed card — a Mirror copying a creature with an attack trigger, an anthem or an Equipment's bonus would play half the copy (the Mycosynth Gardens precedent, parked on the same line). A copy read at every reader comes first.

(3) **Austere Command's mass mana-value filter reads the printed card** (shared.js:147 `perm.card?.cmc` — a copy's mana value is the copied card's, CR 707.2; Culling Ritual's and this slice's sets read `layers.permanentManaValue`). > · **Not taken:** **Notion Thief** (#1202) — "If an opponent would draw a card except the first one they draw in each of their draw steps, instead that player skips that draw and you draw a card." A replaced draw can need two choices from the player drawing: which applicable Notion Thief effect applies when two or more players each control one (its ruling — the answer decides which opponent ends up drawing: in a pod with two opponents' Thieves, choosing one gives the card to the other), and the order against their own draw replacements (CR 616.1; Alhammarret's Archive's, Teferi's Ageless Insight's and Bard, King of Dale's rulings: "the player drawing the card chooses the order"). Every draw runs through `gameState.drawCards` synchronously and no pending choice can pause it, so a person couldn't be asked — a new prompt, and a draw that can wait for it. **Millikin** (#1206) — "{T}, Mill a card: Add {C}." The bundled sources disagree: Millikin's ruling says the ability "is not a mana ability … A recent update to rule 605.1a has made any abilities that move cards to or from libraries no longer mana abilities", but the bundled CR 605.1a has no such clause (by it the ability IS one), and the same line's rulings on Deranged Assistant (#4656 — "If you activate it while casting a spell …") and Charmed Pendant (#22221 — "still a mana ability") treat it as a mana ability. Played as a mana ability (a mill cost the payment planner spends) Millikin contradicts its own ruling; played on the stack the same text plays Deranged Assistant against its ruling and the bundled CR. A bundled-CR refresh (or a decision which source wins) comes first. **Mount Doom** (#1209) — "{5}{B}{R}, {T}, Sacrifice Mount Doom and a legendary artifact: Choose up to two creatures, then destroy the rest. Activate only as a sorcery." Its effect's choice — up to two creatures on any battlefield to keep, made as it resolves and not targeted (its ruling: a creature with shroud may be chosen) — has no pending choice a person can be asked: sacrifice-choice asks a player for their OWN permanents to sacrifice (Promise of Loyalty's keep-one rides it as each player's own sacrifices), impulse-dig's multi-keep picks looked-at library cards, aura-entry-host one host, trigger-target a triggered ability's targets. A new prompt; the counted "a legendary artifact" cost (pw25's person-seat pattern) would be buildable, never half the card. **Amphibian Downpour** (#1230) — "Storm (When you cast this spell, copy it for each spell cast before it this turn. You may choose new targets for the copies. Copies become tokens.)" Each copy's new target is its controller's choice (CR 702.40a, 707.10c; its ruling: "You can make different choices for each copy"). `stack.applyCopySpell`'s permanent path (CR 707.10f) puts every copy of an Aura spell on the stack with the original's host, and no pending choice asks a person a copy's target: change-target (Misdirection) offers only ANOTHER legal target of a spell with a program (an Aura spell's payload has none) and the storm loop doesn't pause per copy — a new prompt. Its ability loss already plays.

(2) **Tokens stamped at the mint seam**, not a second "created this turn" ledger: one definition of "entered this turn" for every reader. (3) **A counted cost's offers for a person, not a new prompt**: the review's smallest fix (the γ1h expansion, bounded like the target cap); past the cap the combinations are a pick-N prompt's (found-not-fixed). (4) **Second Harvest moved onto the shared mint** (entry replacements, Aura hosts, copiable values) rather than a second copy-each resolver for Ocelot Pride — its behaviour changes only toward CR 707.5 / 303.4f. (5) **The Clinic's AI arm is gated on the commander restriction**, not opened for every "target creature gains lifelink" activation (that would change other cards' AI play unmeasured). (6) **PLAY_API 1.17.0** for `muldrothaSlot` and a person's counted-cost offers (`exileGyNames`) — additive MINOR, after pw24's 1.16.0. (7) **No save bump** (v14 stays): no persisted shape changed (a token's `enteredOnTurn` existed and was null; the blink sentinel's `tapped` is optional; the latch keys ride the once-latch map). (8) **Muldrotha under a Crucible**: the graveyard's plain lands are offered once, by the Crucible (the same play without the latch). (9) **The enter-tapped read at the seam**, not at each mint: every token mint of effects/atoms passes it (amass, fabricate, mobilize, manifest and the replacement extras included), the Germ at its own mint. (10) **The counted sets' bound is on the product** (R2-F1): rows × sets within 64 offers takes the full product (the coordinator's "64, or the room left" read as 64 offers beside one victim set, X and discard), past it rows + sets − 1 per X, plus one offer for each card no offer pays with — only a card the first row targets can be one (Cabal Surgeon's).

(4) **Other counted costs a person still can't choose** (the same frozen pick — queued as their own engine slice): the cast-side "discard N" and "exile N from your graveyard" additional costs (legalChoices.js:2024, legalChoices.js:2059), the graveyard-recursion discard and exile riders GR-1 / GR-2 (legalChoices.js:4100–4111), the class sacrifice "Sacrifice N <class>" (legalChoices.js:3201), the counted tap (V6 slice 2, legalChoices.js:3369) and "Sacrifice X", which takes the first X (legalChoices.js:3559). (5) Past the counted-cost cap (64 sets), and beside a target list once rows × sets passes 64, a person reaches every card, every set and every target but not every combination — the trade the target cap made for victims; a pick-N-during-activation prompt would close it. (6) A clone commander loses its designation: cloneCopy.js:729 strips `isCommander` and `commanderInstanceId` from every clone snapshot, the commander clone's own included (CR 903.3 — the designation is the card's), so Sakashima of a Thousand Faces cast as a commander and copying Grizzly Bears is no Clinic target, and its commander damage keys on nothing (the review's F4a). (7) A copy of a Role is not created when every creature already carries one of its controller's Roles (auraEntry.js:249's narrowing, now reached by copy-each), and its log reason reads "nothing it can enchant (CR 303.4g)" (tokens.js:772) though legal creatures exist — CR 303.4f lets it attach and CR 704.5y trims the older Role (the review's F4d). > · **Not taken:** **K'rrik, Son of Yawgmoth** (#1080) — "For each {B} in a cost, you may pay 2 life rather than pay that mana." An option at EVERY mana payment its controller makes (its rulings: "any cost you pay, including the mana costs of spells, activation costs, and even costs for special actions (such as morph)"; "Any time you pay mana, that's a cost"; never generic mana). The engine's life lane for a payment (manaModel.planWithPhyrexian, CR 107.4f) reads the payer's life only from `lifePaymentContext`; the payments made without it pay mana only — the dispatcher's cycling, graveyard and hand activations, the attack tax at declare, the companion, turning a permanent face up, plot and suspend (actionDispatcher.js, eleven sites), every payment a resolution asks for — the ward / "counter unless" soft counter, "you may pay", "sacrifice unless you pay" and the taxed payments, offered and auto-picked (runProgram.js, eight sites) — and ward's own check (ward.js:371): K'rrik would take life at some payments and not others. And life paid so is no mana spent, which the spent-mana readers (adamant, converge, sunburst, "if {B} was spent") would have to be taught. **Marvin, Murderous Mimic** (#1086) — "Marvin has all activated abilities of creatures you control that don't have the same name as this creature." A new mechanism: one permanent with every activated ability of others — printed and granted (Auras, Equipment, group grants), mana abilities among them, a borrowed ability that names its card reading as Marvin (its rulings) — read by every activation lane (legalChoices' activated, granted, crew and loyalty lanes; manaModel.manaSources). The ability view every ability read routes through (layers.withAbilityLoss) is consulted only on a board with an ability-loss effect, so there is no one place to add them. **Anim Pakal, Thousandth Moon** (#1097) — a new human prompt: each Gnome enters attacking a player, planeswalker or battle its controller chooses (CR 508.4; its ruling: "Each Gnome token can enter attacking a different player, planeswalker, or battle"), as the ability resolves (X is the counter count then, the last known one if it left — its ruling). The batched "you attack" event carries no defender (triggers.checkAttackTriggers — `triggeringContext: {}`), no pending choice asks one, and a token with no defender is never joined to combat (tokens.js's ATTACKING JOIN). The rest (the non-Gnome batch filter, the counter, X from its counters) reads. **Drakuseth, Maw of Flames** (#1119) — "… deals 4 damage to any target and 3 damage to each of up to two other targets." Restated on 5dabd48e (the target cap): "3 damage to each of up to two other targets" has no reader at all (it parses LOW on every tree), and its three distinct any-target slots (its ruling: no target chosen twice) would be offered as whole assignments — n·(1 + (n−1) + C(n−1, 2)), about 8,476 on a 26-target pod board. Past the 64-row cap the covering now reaches every target in every slot (the review measured 366 rows), but most whole assignments stay unoffered ("4 to ai3, 3 each to ai1 and ai2" is not among them), and the two-atom shape would need a cross-slot "other" too: a person's pick needs the slot-by-slot prompt (CR 603.3d → 601.2c) — the Decimate class. Stenn, Paranoid Partisan (#7594) reads its blink now and stays body-only on its card-type choice.

> · **Decimate (#983) stays parked.** Bundled text "Destroy target artifact, target creature, target enchantment, and target land."; its ruling (2022-12-08): a legal target is required for each, and one permanent with several card types may fill more than one. Two reasons, both its own: its comma list has no reader (arbiter-spell on both trees — the flip-diff is 0), and past the cap a person still could not aim its four targets where they like — the covering offers each target with the other three at one seat's first options, and four targets across four seats is the combination only a slot-by-slot prompt reaches.
> · **Judgment calls:** (1) **A covering, not a slot-by-slot prompt.** No existing prompt chooses a cast's targets one slot at a time — the trigger-target panel lists whole candidates, change-target moves one target of a spell already cast — and a new one is new UI (the brief's fallback); found-not-fixed (1). (2) **The old 64 rows stay first**, so the default AI's picks among them, and every `find` over the combos (the copy re-aim, the redirect onto a source, the change-target list), are unchanged; past them the order is seat-relative to the caster. (3) **One slot past 64 lists every target** — the same rule (every option of every slot), and what the legacy one-target cast path always did (one cast per legal target, uncapped). (4) **The two in-slot caps** (subsets, the player-and-cards slot) were cutting the same way and take the same fix; the subset list's own 64-row bound stays (found-not-fixed (2)). (5) **A cost choice beside the rows keeps the base's rows exactly and adds each new row once** (F1, the review's rule) — beside the least valuable choice that pays for it, a permanent by its live mana value and live power (R2-F1: round two took the first in battlefield order, the commander; R3-F1: round three's printed values put a grown Walking Ballista first), the counted sacrifice keeping its printed order; every choice × every new row would make every combination of cost and target reachable, and is what crashed. (6) **The mark is a WeakSet on the row's target array**, not a field on the action: no shape change, and a row copied away from its array reads as one of the capped offer's (the old behaviour). (7) **F2 only reads past the old rows** — the AI's picks inside them, under the cap and over it, stay byte-identical (its Lunge quirk with them, found-not-fixed (3)). (8) **The X lane (up to 10 X values), kicker, pitch costs and a repeatable-mode spell's mode sets still multiply one cast's rows by a per-card constant** (R2-F3 — acceptable for landing, the integrator's call); left as they are, found-not-fixed (7). (9) **One payment plan per action shape** (R2-F2) — keyed on everything but the action's own three target fields, never on a hand-picked list of fields, so a cost field added later can't make two different payments share a plan (R3-F2's witness pins the cost in the key). (10) **The row aimed at your own token pays with your commander before a Craw Wurm** (the round-3 recheck's pin note) — by mana value, 4 before 6, the order R3-F1's fix names; the commander's premium (+3) is the policy evaluator's (`permanentValue`), which is off by default; the pin stays.
> · ⚠️ **Found, not fixed:** (1) **A person can't pick every combination past the cap** (targeting.js `coveringVectors`): any combination of two slots each at an option that isn't its seat's first (Hungry Flames at ai2's second Bear and ai3's Jace), or, with three slots or more, the other slots at different seats (Decimate); and, beside a cost choice, a later row with any choice but the least valuable that pays (Blasting Station: an opponent's creature past the 64th target is offered only with the cheapest Squirrel token sacrificed) — it needs a slot-by-slot target prompt at cast (a pending choice the cast pauses on, and its panel in LearnView / learnDecisionPanels.jsx). (2) **A multi-count subset list keeps its 64-row bound** (targeting.js `targetSubsets` :218): every target is named now, but "up to two target creatures" among 24 offers 64 of its 301 subsets — pairs past the 63rd row are cut. (3) **The default AI's multi-slot pick takes the first row with its slot-0 target inside the old rows** (opponentAI.js:1138): from the user's seat it aims a Lunge's second 2 damage at its own face (the first player offered) — pre-existing, under the cap too, a self-play-only quirk (a person plays the user's seat). (4) **It scores slot 0 through the card's legacy single effect** (opponentAI.js:1135–1136, `spellEffects.parseSpellEffect`), which for Angrath's Fury reads the second sentence's 3 damage, so its destroy is aimed as 3 damage (the Hill Giant over the Craw Wurm). (5) **Twisted Fealty's Role takes a required target**: tokens.js:960's Role matcher accepts "up to one" and drops it, so a person can't decline the Role (a safe under-offer). (6) **The wire carries each cast's whole program** (~823 bytes a cast): a 600-Squirrel Station board's decision is 41.6 MB (base 41 MB), a 400-creature pod's 14,000 casts ~12 MB — slimming the action (the review's follow-up: rebuild `program` from `cardId` / `permanentId` + `abilityIndex`) changes `resolveChoice`'s key, a contract change for its own slice. (7) **Per-card constant multipliers past the cap** (the round-2 recheck's R2-F3): from ai2, ai1 holding 600 Squirrels, one card in hand — Mystic Confluence 193 → 14,137 casts (18.65 MB; its [1,1,1] mode set 7,996, [1,1,2] 5,524; the decision 15.5 → 86 ms), Kolaghan's Command 160 → 5,008, Blaze 640 → 6,200 (X 1–10 × 620), Burst Lightning 128 → 1,240 (kicked and not), Snapback 128 → 1,232 (2,464 plays for a person with three Brainstorms in hand): linear in the board times a per-card constant, not quadratic. A repeated targeting mode could cover its first instance only (its other instances' rows are permutations, CR 700.2e) — about 2–3× fewer rows for Mystic Confluence's [1,1,1]; not built (the integrator: acceptable for landing).

> · **The exert line and its haste rider** (Arena of Glory — manaModel `exertHasteManaLineOf` / `manualOnlyManaRecords`; CR 701.43a, 701.43b, 400.7a, 106.12). The line nets nothing over the land's own "{T}: Add {R}." (its {R} costs what that tap makes), so a payment never needs it and the planner never lists it: it is the explicit tap alone (`manualOnly`, `bundle: "exert"`), its pip paid from floating mana (the free-activation fix), tapped for mana so its own mana takes the controller's multiplier and the tap bonuses ride beside it. Its {R}{R} float as a TAGGED entry (`player.restrictedMana`, `restriction: null`, `rider: { kind: "creatureSpellHasteEot" }`): the pre-pass spends it like any entry, a remainder stays tagged, it drains with the step; the cast site reads the rider off `plan.entrySpends` (`paidHasteRider`) and stamps `hasteUntilEndOfTurn` on a creature spell's PERMANENT_ETB payload, which the resolver turns into a layer-6 haste until end of turn on the entered permanent. Exert is `doesNotUntapNext` naming the exerting player: `untapAll` skips only that player's next untap step, a permanent another player controls by then untaps in that player's step (the bundled ruling), and the exerter's step ends the flag wherever it is. Witnessed: offered only with {R} floating; exerted, the pool spends its pip, {R}{R} float tagged, the land is tapped and flagged for its controller; Hill Giant paid with it has haste and attacks, and not the next turn; the same Giant paid otherwise has none; two Goblin Raiders, one {R} each, both hasty (ruling); a Lightning Bolt takes one {R} and gains nothing, the other still hastes a creature (ruling: the mana pays for anything); Krenko's Command's Goblins don't gain haste (ruling); the tagged mana empties with the step; exerted, the land stays tapped through the next untap step and untaps in the one after; untapped by an effect first, the exert ends doing nothing (ruling); borrowed, it untaps in its owner's step and the exerter's step ends the flag (ruling).

> · **Judgment calls:** (1) **Explicit-only mana abilities stay out of `manaSources`** — fifty readers (affordability, X ceilings, the AI's mana counts) would see a phantom source; `manualManaTaps` is the one place they appear, and the runtime fingerprint (mana) is byte-identical to the base for all cards. (2) **The rider rides a tagged entry** with `restriction: null` rather than teaching the open pool a rider: the entry machinery (QUARTET Phase 4) already spends first, keeps remainders and drains with the step. (3) **Conduit of Worlds rides the free-cast window** (`paid`), so no new pending kind reaches the driver, the decision vocabulary or the AI; the decline keeps its kind with a `paid` flag for its label ("Don't cast it"). (4) **"Nonland permanent" is a structured gate** (`{ typeFilter: "permanent", nonland: true }`) in the one reanimate arm, not a parseGraveyardFilter word: two readers split that token themselves (library.js's milled pick), and a new word would reach them unread. (5) **Spinerock Knoll counts an opponent who left the game** (its ruling) — the commonest case is the opponent the 7 damage killed; `departedDamageThisTurn` is written only when the departing seat was dealt damage that turn. (6) **Tibalt's Trickery may target an uncounterable spell** through a per-atom flag (`targetsUncounterable`), not by opening every counter's enumeration; the AI's counter pick skips such a target. (7) **Reflections' snapshot rides only an exact "copy that spell" descriptor**, so no other cast trigger's context grows. (8) **Double Down's outlaw filter fixed in place** — before, the descriptor parsed and could never fire (no card was credited on it, so nothing was a live false credit). (9) **The AI's lines** (each needs the card on the battlefield, so no game without one plays differently): the exert line only for a creature cast it would make now that gains from haste and whose cost the tagged mana can pay part of; the Diamond only with an empty hand for a commander it can't otherwise cast; the reanimation precombat; Conduit after the cast picker passed; a retrace after every other cast; the hideaway play first among safe activations — and, since the review (F3), only when its own pick at the parked window would cast the hidden card. (10) **PLAY_API 1.11.0 → 1.12.0** (the review's F6 — PLAY-API-CONTRACT.md §3 / §5: additive action fields are MINOR): no decision or action kind added; the new fields (`retraceCast` / `retraceName`, `resolutionCast`, `manualOnly` / `discardsHand` / `exertHaste` / `bundle: "exert"`, the decline's `paid`) ride existing kinds; noted in gameApi.js and the contract §1. **Save format v9 → v10** (CONTRACT-MIG; `MIGRATIONS[9]` stamp-only, as S0b's and S2's): the new shapes (`state.departedDamageThisTurn`, a tagged entry's `rider`, a payload's `hasteUntilEndOfTurn`, a permanent's `leaveExiledInstead`, `doesNotUntapNext` naming a player, a paid graveyard `pendingFreeCast`, a pending trigger's `castSpellSnapshot`) are absent on every v9 save and absent reads as none; the bump makes a v9 build refuse a v10 save rather than read `doesNotUntapNext: "user"` as `true`; the round trip witnessed in learnSaveSchema.test.js.
> · ⚠️ **Found, not fixed:** (1) **The default AI casts nothing from a graveyard** except this slice's two lanes: `opponentAI.cardFromHand` (opponentAI.js:229) reads hand, command zone, exile and library, so every flashback, granted-escape, Emry, Rivaz, Raul and The Indomitable cast offered to an AI seat is dropped as "card vanished" (pickCastAction). (2) **Hall of the Bandit Lord (#3011, `land`) and Generator Servant (#6851, `native-mana`) still drop their haste rider** (the 10-16 ledger's ③ — manaModel.js:2314 `parseManaSpentRider` reads only Path of Ancestry's sentence); this slice's tagged-entry rider and `paidHasteRider` are the lane to fix them (Servant's {C}{C} surplus needs the rider kept on a planner tap's floating remainder). (3) **The explicit-tap window is its controller's own main phase with priority** (legalChoices.js:2585 `actionsTapForMana`), so Lion's Eye Diamond ("as an instant") and Arena of Glory's exert line can't be used in another window — an under-offer the engine applies to every explicit tap. (4) **The board shows only the open mana pool**: a tagged entry (Arena's {R}{R}, Klauth's restricted mana) is not displayed (LearnBoard.jsx:350 `me.manaPool`); and floating Arena's pip by hand needs the manual-mana toggle (a land tile taps only with it on). (5) **A hidden land under any hideaway land is not offered** (hideaway.js:55 — the P·10 under-offer, Spinerock Knoll included). (6) **Infect damage to a player is not on `damageTakenThisTurn`** (combatResolution.js:601, spellEffects.js:1701 — poison, not loseLife), so Spinerock Knoll and bloodthirst under-read it. (7) **A modal double-faced card found by Tibalt's Trickery (or cascade) can't be cast** — castActionsFromZone skips a combined MDFC (legalChoices.js:1383), and since the review's F2 both digs stop at a spell // land MDFC (it is a nonland card there), so its window offers only the decline (the same skip keeps Conduit of Worlds and Six from an adventurer or MDFC nonland permanent card in the graveyard — the review's F4a); and a declined found card goes after the shuffled rest (the cascade precedent), not at a random place among them. (8) **Reflections of Littjara's type is the house pick for a person too** (choicePolicy.js:60 autoPickCreatureType — the chosen-type family's precedent). (9) **Printed retrace** (Flame Jab, Worm Harvest …) is still stripped as a vacuous option; the granted-retrace lane could serve it. (10) **The tagged {R}{R} is always spent first** (the review's F4b — manaModel's restricted-first payment pre-pass, manaModel.js:4607): an auto-paid Lightning Bolt with Mountains untapped takes one of Arena's tagged {R}, so a person can't keep the haste mana for a creature unless they pay by hand — a legal payment the engine picks. (11) **Lion's Eye Diamond's five explicit activations take five of the action bar's six slots** (the review's F4c — LearnBoard.jsx:43 `BAR_ACTION_LIMIT`; tap-for-mana actions list first), pushing every other activation behind "+N more" while it is on the battlefield.
> · **Not taken:** none — every one of the eight plays its whole text. Diamond Lion (#10966, its "{T}, … Sacrifice this creature" form) stays parked; Swarm Intelligence, Thousand-Year Storm, Double Vision (their "you may choose new targets" rider), Kheru Lich Lord and Isareth the Awakener (other text) stay parked on the copy and reanimation readers.

The persona kept choosing it (R1 holds only what the seam marks; R4's position signature counts `continuousEffects.length`, and each Floodcaller trigger adds one — 41 → 57 between two dumped decisions). > · **The cost (profiled, 1 ms sampling, the stalling turn only, same seed and tick budget; this box under Omnath's load):** base, loop steps **on**, T46 2,132 s: `isHeldLoopStep` (loopStepLine.js:210) **72.2%** inclusive — `loopManaHasUse` (:187) 54.4% (its two re-offers through `legalActionsForPlayer` 30.8%, `isSpend` over both offers 30.8%), `castTriggerRemovesOwn` (gameEngine.js:2348) 37.9%; the persona seam `isTokenLoopAction` 1,461 s, the default AI's `pickAction` read 78.9 s (3.7%). Base, loop steps **off**, T45 (the Basalt pair's untap stall) 71 s: the loop-step reads **0.1%**, the engine's own offer 55%. Counted on an instrumented copy (T46's first 2,500 decisions, 680 Kinnan decisions), per Kinnan decision: **3.4 offers** beyond the engine's own 1, **4.1 cast previews**, 78.7 `loopStepOf` reads, 1.7 demand reads, 2.6 `manaValueOf`. **Omnath's inference — partly confirmed:** the read ran on every decision of the turn (`tokenLoopState` 18,382 calls for 18,385 decisions) and the "+20 mana" re-offer was the largest single piece; but the empty library was not what kept `loopStepsPossible` true (the Monolith untap-this gate and the casts that turn each do), the re-offer is cached per untap source and state (≈2 per positive-net source per decision), not run per offered action — the per-action multiplier was the cast preview, once per offered cast of a card cast this turn (Green Sun's Zenith at nine X values) in the offer and again in each re-offer; and the default AI did not pay the same: it skips the untap read, so it paid the per-X previews alone (3.7% of the turn).
> · **The fix — the combo law, not a guard (`loopStepLine.js`):** a fourth step kind, the **DRAW-BACK** — an activation whose every atom reads its controller's own library (the empty-library set) while that library holds nothing but spells that come back by themselves (each `program.selfShuffle`, every atom a library-only tutor whose filter no card of that library passes — `atoms/library.cardMatchesTutorFilter`). It is held while recasting that spell adds nothing usable: no own draw trigger fires on the draw (`checkCardDrawnTriggers` on a copy); every own cast trigger of the recast (`gameEngine.castTriggerOutcomes`, new — the `castTriggerRemovesOwn` preview reporting every own trigger's outcome through the flush's own `buildTriggerStack` + `chooseTriggerTargets`) only untaps or pumps its own permanents and adds mana, or does nothing; the mana has no use (`loopManaHasUse`, all six colours); the pump has none (`pumpHasUse` — "enough" for a pump is lethal: on its own turn before combat damage while its attack-capable power is short of the lowest opponent life; on another player's turn never). Holding the draw, not the cast, leaves the Zenith in the library, so its next draw does not lose (CR 704.5b). In the demand read a draw-back that is a play counts as a spend, so the Monolith untap that fuels a draw-back loop still taking an opponent's permanent has a use; the draw-back's own mana read counts a draw-back only by a use of its own (`recastYield`, `ownUseOnly`), so a loop is never its own use. `pickAction` holds it too (through `withoutHeldLoopSteps`). Every action stays offered (`gameApi.legalActions` untouched) and a person repeats the loop as often as they choose (CR 732.1b, 732.2a). No size or tick guard changed.
> · **The memos (the cost):** every loop-step read is a pure function of the state object, and the engine hands `pickAction` and the pilot the same object in a tick, so `loopStepLine` keeps one memo table per state object (WeakMap): each offered action's step; the cast preview per (card object, seat, zone); one `manaSources` list per (state, permanent read untapped) for both the mana value (`manaUntapLine.manaValueFromSources`, `manaValueOf`'s last step, new) and the colours; the copy with the source kept tapped; the demand read per (kept state, colours, rule). The offer as it stands is the engine's own list for that state when it built one (`legalChoices.offerMadeFor`, new — each `legalActionsForPlayer` call with no options keeps a copy per state object and player). `richUnlocks` reads the cheap side first — the same boolean as collecting both spend sets. **Proved byte-identical to the read without them:** a copy of the final code with every memo bypassed and the demand read in its eager order (`v-uncached`) gives the same picks on every decision of 106558 (4,605), every decision of the ten changed stall games, and the A/B (80 / 80 byte-identical); the memos alone (the draw-back removed, `v-cacheonly`) give base's picks on every one of 106558's 21,556 decisions with loop steps on. **Measured (quiet box, holds 1–2): 106558's uncaught T46, base 1,218.9 s with the read at 850.2 s → memos 576.3 s with the read at 215.1 s** — the same turn's non-read work 368.7 s / 361.2 s, so the read's overhead on that turn falls **3.31× → 1.60×**. Against the loop-steps-off stalling turn (T45, 43.0 s) the uncaught T46 is still **13.4×**: that turn's own engine work is 8.4× T45's (808 until-end-of-turn pumps by its end; every characteristic derivation scans them — layers.js:2126 `effectAffects`, :2444), which no read can remove. What is left of the read: the richer offer (19% of the memoized turn) and `manaSources` on a copy with a tapped untap source untapped (12%). The cost witness: one tick's reads with three or six tapped Basalts and the recast Zenith offered at several X values cost **1 offer beyond the engine's and 1 cast preview** (base: up to 12 offers and 95 previews).

> · **Judgment calls:** (1) the draw is held, not the cast — the Zenith left in the library keeps its controller's next draw alive; (2) the family is only self-shuffling library-only tutors that can find nothing (Green Sun's Zenith); (3) a pump has a use only toward lethal on the seat's own turn (attack-capable power, blockers not read) and never on another player's turn (no AI picker builds blockers through a loop); (4) other seats' cast triggers on the seat's cast are not read — they give those seats something, never this one; (5) the draw-back's mana read is over all six colours, not the colours its triggers make; (6) a draw-back is a spend in the demand read when it is a play, counted inside its own mana read only by a use of its own; (7) the library's contents are read only to see that it holds nothing but those self-returning spells, which their caster put there; (8) the engine keeps a copy of its own offer per state object for the reader of the same state.

> · **The fix (`loopStepLine.js`, new):** `loopStepOf` names an offered action as a step — an UNTAP of a mana source (its net: the mana it makes, Kinnan counted, minus its cost; minus the cost alone when it untaps an untapped permanent — paid from elsewhere or with its own untap already on the stack), an EMPTY-LIBRARY activation (every atom reads the controller's own empty library; a draw there loses, CR 704.5b), or a RECAST (a card its caster already cast this turn while one of its own cast triggers would be forced onto its own permanent and remove it — `gameEngine.castTriggerRemovesOwn`, the cast-time sibling of `entersTriggerRemovesOwn`, previewed with the flush's own routing and chooser). `isHeldLoopStep` holds the empty-library steps, the recasts (the trigger loop has nothing left to take on any opponent's side: enough), an untap that nets nothing, and an untap whose mana has no use — `loopManaHasUse` reads the engine's offer twice with the step's source kept tapped (float the mana, keep the engine), as it stands and with 20 more of each colour it makes; the mana has a use only while a cast or activation appears that was not offered at all (an X card offered at any X counts as offered — never infinite). `opponentAI.pickAction` drops the held recasts and empty-library steps from both lists right after the token loop's hold (policy `loopStep: "v1"` keeps the old pick); it leaves the untap read unread, since none of its pickers takes an untap and that read costs two offers per decision. `withLoopSteps(tokenLoopModule)` wraps the tokenLoopLine seam with every step held — the seam decide.mjs's R1 reads. > · **The fix:** (1) `manaModel.withoutOwnHandSource`: the card being cast, and every card its cost discards, is no hand source of its own payment — in `castPaymentSources`, in the offer's per-card `castSources`, and (review F1) in the discard offer itself (`payableDiscarding`): a single discard the mana needs is not offered (Thrill of Possibility + Simian Spirit Guide + one Mountain: only the other card), and a counted discard keeps its least-valuable pick unless the payment then fails, when it takes the least valuable cards the payment allows (Cathartic Reunion discards the two others while the Guide pays); the splice refuses a card that left its zone while the costs were paid (`CARD_LEFT_ZONE`) (CR 601.2a, 601.2g, 601.2h). (2) `costChoices.js` (new, pure): INSIDE the engine an alternative cost payable more than one way is ONE cast per target / mode carrying the house payment (`housePaymentIndex` — what `filterAltCastVariants` pays: the lowest mana value, then the lowest resource id, ties to the first offered) and every payment on `altCostChoices`; the AI ranks that short list. OUTSIDE it nothing changed (review F5, option A): `expandAllCostChoices` gives back every legal play key for key in the old order, and that is what `gameApi.legalActions` / `isLegalAction` (one equality, F7), a pilot's `decide`, the Academy's ask options and `applyChoice` / `resolveChoice` (a partial choice naming no payment is ambiguous again, F6) see; the trajectory row counts and ranks among every legal play (`everyPlayTally` / `everyPlayIndexOf`, no list built) and what is dispatched and logged is the cast as paid (F9). `withPayableOwedMana` judges each payment. (3) `phyrexianLifeSets`: one try per split (how many of each symbol kind are paid in life), each as its lexicographically first index set, in the order the subset walk first reached it. (4) `advanceUntilDecision` is a guard around `advanceUntilDecisionUnguarded` (review F3): any throw inside the loop is a **dispatch-error** carrying `error: { name, message, code, stack }`, the turn / phase / step and `guard: { type: "engine-error" }`, on the session as that tick began, logged with its stack; the self-play record is `dispatch-error` with `error`, `errorCode`, `errorStack` and the real `turns`; `endEngineStoppedGame` ends it; under the test-time auditor (MTG_AUDIT=1) it rethrows, so a test still goes red on engine corruption. The runner's own catch (a backstop) records `turns: null` and `errorStack`. **PLAY_API 1.9.0 → 1.10.0** (additive: a throw that escaped is now a decision with new fields; the cast surface is unchanged) — gameApi.js + PLAY-API-CONTRACT.md.

(3) **`hasKeyword` scanned the whole text twice per call** (the leveler band search and the keyword pattern) — ~750,000 calls a game. (4) **The derive split every permanent's type line** for its card types and subtypes in every game state. (5) **`parseProtectionColors` / `parseProtectionClasses` re-scanned each text** at every block, targeting and attachment check (the 10-22 attachment state-based action reads them too).
> · **The fix:** `faceUpView` keeps one entry per card object (`_faceMemo`, a WeakMap — a single-faced card maps to ITSELF, a combined card to its front-face view as before); `hasKeyword` reads a per-text entry (`_textMemo`: the band split and each keyword's pattern answer, keyed by the face-up text; the `keywords` array read live; 8,192 texts, 512 keywords per text), and `printedKeywordsOf(card, keywords)` gives `layers.printedKeywords` all eleven answers off one face read and one lowercase pass of the array; `keywordSet`'s counter loop reads the counters once with the keywords lowercased once; `teamPowerBlockGateOf` goes through `memoByCardText` (name, then face-up text) — every `deriveCharacteristics` and `creaturePower` call in the loop is where it was; `cardTypesOf` / `subtypesOf` read a per-line entry (`_typeLineWordsMemo`, 8,192 lines) and hand each caller its own copy; `parseProtectionColors` / `parseProtectionClasses` read a per-text entry (`_protectionTextMemo`, 8,192 texts; the own-clause read per name, 64 per text) and hand each caller a fresh Set in the same order. ENGINE-SCAFFOLD §3.4 names each memo's key and what invalidates it.
> · **A/B 80 seeded commander games** (base seed 7, 10 per pod, the 30 profile decks, default AI; base = the untouched 35198906 archive, same hold): **80 / 80 byte-identical** (whole record and play), 0 winner changes; user-wins 25 / ai-wins 55 on both; 0 errors, 0 unpaid-cost events; 232.6 s → 185.5 s (−20%).
> · **Per decision** (in the hold — one gated job on the box at a time; base = the 35198906 archive, after = this tree; both games' records byte-identical between the trees): main-thread CPU (`process.threadCpuUsage` around `runSelfPlayGame`, median of three alternating runs) **seed 1469368463 2.155 → 1.669 ms (−22.6%)**, July seed #0 826257776 **2.359 → 1.987 ms (−15.8%)**; the profiles' sampled CPU inside `runSelfPlayGame` per decision row 2.242 → 1.788 (−20.3%) and 2.431 → 2.089 (−14.1%), the whole process (start-up and module load included) 2.857 → 2.419 and 3.007 → 2.669. Untouched (single-run noise): `manaSources` 52.1 → 37.4, `plannerSourceRecord` 15.4 → 14.8, `parseAbilityCost` 24.3 → 28.7, `parseActivatedAbilities` 69.7 → 97.0. Inference, not measured: the same cut on the replay's v0.169.0 figure would put it at ~2.3–2.6 ms, ×1.2–1.3 over 86389b97 — a replay re-run is the measure.
> · **Witness** `textReadsOnce.test.js` (19): 35198906's `readsAsFrontFace` / `faceUpView`, `hasKeyword`, `cardTypesOf` / `subtypesOf`, the team gate (`selfOracleUncached` + the sentence) and both protection readers copied verbatim as the reference, run beside the new reads over a 136-entry sample of the bundled corpus (generated through `cardIndex.publicCard` → `learnDeckEnrich.mergeCardData`, never typed: the 25 most played, the most played card naming each of 23 keywords, the most played of each multi-face layout, and the cards each path was written for — Westvale Abbey, Delver, Lunarch Veteran and the other back-face-keyword cards, the levelers, Champion of Lambholt with Wandering Wolf, Silumgar Assassin, Bower Passage and Kraken of the Straits, every protection shape), every transform and modal card in both card shapes: 37 combined cards' views equal and stable, 5,576 keyword asks ×2 passes (114 true) equal, the derive's keyword set, types and subtypes equal on 133 one-permanent boards, the gate true for the Champion alone, protection equal cold and warm. Invalidation: the same Bog Wraith gains flying from a keyword counter and from Levitation and loses it on the next board; the same Champion bars a power-2 blocker at +2 counters, not at none, not once gone, again on return; an edited text under one name is a new key (team gate, keyword read, own-clause protection); an in-place edit of a single-faced card is read live; a caller's edit to one derive's types reaches no other. The witness imports the new `printedKeywordsOf`, so it does not run on the base; its reference IS the base's code.
> · **Judgment calls:** (1) **`faceUpView` per card OBJECT, not per text** — which face is up needs the object's own two fields either way, and a WeakMap hit is ~5× cheaper than re-reading them. It is safe because no engine code writes `layout` / `type` / `type_line` on an existing card object (grep of src/lib: the only writes are `cloneCopy.snapshotCopiedCard`'s on the copy it is building and `selfReturn` / `stack`'s on new objects; no `Object.assign`, bracket write or `delete` on a card); two tests write `.type` in place (combatDamageTrigger.test.js:63, groupTriggeredGrant.test.js:75) and neither touches " // ". A single-faced card maps to itself, so every other field is read live. (2) **No hoist in `canBlockAttacker`.** A per-state list of the Champion's sources would skip ~150,000 derive reads a game, but the derive memo fills in call order and a derive under the selector guards (`_ptPredicateInProgress` / `_selectorColorInProgress`) is not memoized, so skipping one can change what a later guarded read returns; only the text test is memoized. (3) **The `keywords` array stays out of the keyword key** — read live, so an edited array is seen at once. (4) **The memos' stored arrays are private and unfrozen** — a frozen array takes `slice()` off its fast path (the first build was slower than the unmemoized split; measured 6–12× faster unfrozen). (5) **Target 3 taken where it was a pure text read** (`permanentHasKeyword` / `hasKeyword` through the text memo, the protection readers, the counter loop); `manaSources`, `plannerSourceRecord` and `parseAbilityCost` left (found-not-fixed). (6) Procedure: the box was powered off at 01:25:10Z mid-slice; nothing was running and no output was partial. The pre-hold profiles, CPU probes and the witness file ran outside the gate as single-seed runs and one test file; every number above is the hold's.
> · ⚠️ **Found, not fixed:** (1) **`parseActivatedAbilities` has no cache** (effects/abilities.js:1257) — 16,988 calls in seed 1469368463, from `legalChoices.actionsActivateAbility` (:2662) for every permanent at every legal-actions call; now the top engine cost (487 ms inclusive of the game's 2,644, 18%). (2) **`manaSources` rebuilds a player's sources for each reader of one legal-actions call** (manaModel.js:3267 — `withPayableConsumedCosts`, `actionsActivateAbility`, `castActionsFromZone`, `manualManaTaps`): 316 ms (12%); a per-state memo needs every caller proven not to write the records. (3) **`isPlainRecord` builds a whole `plannerSourceRecord` to test `isPlainColorless`** (manaModel.js:4389). (4) **`keywords.PATTERN_CACHE` keeps a RegExp per distinct keyword string, unbounded** (keywords.js:128) — the pseudo-keywords (`cantBlockSource:<id>`) carry permanent ids.

> ## 🔧 2026-10-22 — FIX (Academy, user-facing): how a game leaves play — the stuck-game entry's found-not-fixed (1)–(4). (1) **"Abandon game" never abandoned**: `handleAbandon` (LearnView.jsx:297 at 614a5321) only reset the page and `learnSession.abandon` had no caller, so the game stayed in "Continue a game", no record was kept and "Game abandoned." was unreachable. Now `POST /api/learn/abandon` (new, beside the other learn routes) ends it — `abandon` (status `abandoned`, "You ended the game early.") → `learnPersistence.finishGame`, the one way a finished game leaves play: the record kept, the session freed, the save dropped — whether the game is in memory, only on disk (the server restarted since its last move; ended from its save) or still at its opening-hand mulligans (`abandon` now accepts status `mulligan`: start saves it, so it is listed); 404 for no such game, 409 for one already over (nothing changed), 422 for an unreadable save. The button calls it on a game in progress and is "New game" on one already over; the end card's "New game" only resets; the hook's `stateAfterAbandon` (pure) shows the end card, or goes back to the deck picker when there is nothing to end or the abandon failed (with the error there — never left on a game that can't be left). A puzzle attempt the person abandoned gets no verdict (`evaluatePuzzle` → `"abandoned"`), and the verdict's "Back to Academy" on a missed attempt still in progress ends it the same way first. (2) **The two terminal engine faults trapped like the guards did**: a step that throws (learnSession.js:2668 at 614a5321) and a seat with priority, no legal action and a fallback pass that throws (:2707, whose catch dropped the error) answered engine-stuck with no `guard`; the game stayed active, was autosaved, and every resume re-derived the same throw. Each now names itself — `guard` `{ type: "engine-error", message }` / `{ type: "no-legal-action", seat, message }` — and logs the error with its stack (`console.error` → server.err.log), and `endEngineStoppedGame` ends the game like a guard's: "The engine stopped the game: moving the game to its next step failed with an engine error — Invalid (phase=…, step=…)." / "…: You had priority with no legal action, and moving the game on failed with an engine error — …". `kind`, the `reason` text and the `active` session are unchanged, so every self-play consumer the stuck-game entry lists counts the same `engine-stuck`. The pending-choice failsafe (:2621 there, :2626 now) is left as is (it clears the choice; the game can go on). (3) **Every record's table read "—"**: `RecordsView.seatLine` read `seatNames` / `deckName` / `oppName`; the routes write `userDeckName` / `opponentNames` (start's meta, kept on the save, the record and a puzzle's snapshot). `git log -S` finds no writer of `deckName` / `oppName` ever and no Academy writer of `seatNames` (the self-play meta's shape, still read), and this box has no learn-records.json — so no older record shape to keep. The Crucible home and Teferi's rail share one result label (`recordStatusLabel`): "Abandoned (no result)". (4) **After a resume the header read "You vs Opponent"**: start, resume and resume-puzzle answer `userDeckName` / `opponentDeckNames` from the game's meta (`learnDeckNames.deckNamesOf`), the hook keeps them (`deckNamesFrom`) and the header reads them (`academyTitle`), never the deck pickers. **PLAY_API 1.8.0 → 1.9.0** (additive MINOR: the faults' `guard`; `abandon` at the mulligan) · **±0**

> · **Judgment calls:** (1) **One way out of play**: the abandon route ends the game through `learnSession.abandon` + `finishGame`, never a route-only status write, and builds its answer before `finishGame`, so a failure leaves the game as it was. (2) **A failed abandon goes back to the deck picker with the error, not back to the game**: a server that is gone would fail every abandon, and staying would leave the person on a board they can't leave; the game may still be listed, and the error says so. 404 / 409 (nothing to end) go back without one. (3) **"Abandon game" on a finished game is "New game"**, and the end card's "New game" never calls the server. (4) **The faults end the game in the Academy, not the driver** — the stuck-game slice's judgment (1): the driver change is the `guard` field (and the log line), so every harness counts the same `engine-stuck`. (5) **The no-legal-action words say "moving the game on failed"**, not "passing failed": the driver's fallback can be a decline. (6) **`abandon` accepts `mulligan`** (start saves a game at the mulligan, so it is listed). (7) **The puzzle verdict's "Back to Academy" on a missed attempt still in progress abandons it** (it is autosaved under its own id and was left listed); an abandoned attempt gets no verdict. (8) **`seatLine` drops `deckName` / `oppName`** (never written by anything) and keeps `seatNames` after the routes' fields; the result labels moved to one shared `recordStatusLabel`, so the next new ending is named once. (9) **The header reads only the game's names**, never the pickers (empty after a restart, and possibly naming other decks than a resumed game's). (10) The PLAY_API MINOR delta is owed to memory/COMMS.md (outside the repo; not written here).

> ## 🔧 2026-10-22 — FIX (rules faithfulness, four protection false positives): an attached Aura or Equipment falls off when its host GAINS protection from it, damage to a planeswalker respects protection, a triggered or loyalty ability is no longer OFFERED a permanent with protection from its source, and "combat damage can't be prevented" overrides protection, Maze of Ith and a shield counter (CR 702.16c — "Such Auras attached to the permanent or player with protection will be put into their owners' graveyards as a state-based action."; CR 702.16d — "Such Equipment or Fortifications become unattached from that permanent as a state-based action, but remain on the battlefield."; CR 704.5m, 704.5n, 702.16e, 120.3c, 702.16b, 603.3d, 601.2c, 615.12 — "Those effects won't prevent any damage, but any additional effects they have will take place."; CR 122.1c, 105.2c) — the protection-last-known-information entry's found-not-fixed (1)–(4), and the brief's fourth: `sba.sweepAttachmentLegality` (sba.js:70 at b33ae89a) read no protection, so equipping Sword of War and Peace onto a creature wearing the opponent's Pacifism left the Pacifism on and Giver of Runes' protection from colorless left Bonesplitter attached; the planeswalker hits of `applyDamageEffect` (spellEffects.js:1835, 1864, 1904) and combat's attacked-planeswalker arm checked no protection, so Storm's Wrath killed a Chandra with protection from red; the four `gameEngine` trigger offers (1656, 1745, 1796, 1899) and the loyalty offer (legalChoices.js:4385) threaded no source colours, so Flametongue Kavu's trigger was offered Silver Knight (protection from red) and fizzled on it instead of having to target the Kavu itself, and Chandra's −3 was offered it; and `combatResolution` let protection, both halves of Maze of Ith and a shield counter prevent combat damage with Frenzied Baloth on the battlefield · **±0** · snapshot native+land 15,877 unchanged

> · **The fix** — (1) ATTACHMENTS: `sba.protectionRemovesAttachment(state, hostId, attachmentId)`, read by both arms of the attachment sweep — the host's protection colours (`layers.permanentProtectionColors`, granted and the card's OWN printed clauses — colorless included) against the attachment's current colours when known (`permanentColorsIfKnown`; `protection.protectionApplies`): an Aura that matches is illegal (its owner's graveyard), an Equipment unattached and left on the battlefield; the log carries `reason: "protection"`. Two guards: a grant whose source says it doesn't remove the attachment is left out (`grantSparesAttachment`, through `permanentProtectionColors`' new optional `skipEffect`) — "This effect doesn't remove this Aura" spares that Aura alone (White Ward emits a real protection-from-white grant; without this the sweep would destroy White Ward the moment it attached), any other "doesn't remove" wording spares every attachment; and the printed part is the host's own protection only (`parseProtectionColors(card, { ownOnly })` / `permanentProtectionColors(…, ownPrintedOnly)` — `isOwnProtectionClause`: a keyword line or list, or the card itself as the subject), because the printed reader also reads "Equipped creature … has protection from red and from blue" as the Sword's own (found-not-fixed (1)) and an Aura on such a card must not fall off for it. (2) PLANESWALKERS: `spellEffects.dealDamageToPlaneswalker` — the one planeswalker hit (the single target and both planeswalker sweeps call it): protection from the dealer (`protectedFromDealer`, the creature hit's judgment) first, then the replacement, the shields and the loyalty removal as before; combat's planeswalker arm reads `protectionPrevents`. (3) OFFERS: `spellEffects.abilitySource(state, ctx, sourceId)` → `{ colors, known }`, the non-spell half of `resolutionSource` (which now calls it), read by `effects/targeting.expandTriggerChoices` — the four trigger offers' enumeration, with `sourceColorsKnown` when known — so the offer refuses exactly what the CR 608.2b re-check refuses; the loyalty offer threads the walker's colours like the activated-ability offer. (4) UNPREVENTABLE: in `resolveCombatDamage`, `protectionPrevents` answers no while `combatDamageUnpreventable`; `mazePrevents` (the receiver half) likewise; `shieldSpends` lets the damage through and still removes the counter; Maze of Ith's dealt-by half is its own stamp now (`combatDamageDealtPreventedTurn`, written by `effects/atoms/combat.applyTapEffect`), gated in `dealsThisStep`, apart from Laccolith's `noCombatDamageTurn` ("assigns no combat damage" — not prevention, unchanged). Comments in protection.js (header), spellEffects.js (canBeTargetedBy), layers.js, sba.js; docs: ENGINE-SCAFFOLD (a new protection paragraph after the last-known-information one, its "not done" list, the blocked-arm sentence), CHANGELOG (two lines).
> · **Tests changed on purpose:** `druidApprenticeSurge.test.js` "the ABILITY's source is Warstorm Surge: a creature with protection from red …" asserted the trigger was AIMED at Kor Firewalker and fizzled there (it encoded the offer's old blindness); now Kor Firewalker is never offered, the engine's pick is the AI player, and the walker is untouched — fails on the base on its assertion (`expected [ 'kf' ] to deeply equal [ 'ai' ]`). `mazeOfIth.test.js` — the dealer stamp is `combatDamageDealtPreventedTurn` (one assertion, one stale-stamp fixture, the header); the changed assertion fails on the base on its assertion.
> · **Judgment calls:** (1) **The exemption reads the granting card** (`effect.source.permanentId`'s text), not a parsed flag: White Ward's grant is a plain layer-6 effect, and "This effect doesn't remove this Aura" is the only form that emits one today; any other "doesn't remove" wording spares every attachment (FN-safe). (2) **The state-based action reads only the host's own printed protection** — a positive reading (keyword line or list, or the card as subject); audited over the bundled corpus: of the 178 card faces the printed reader gives a colour, the own reading is identical on 140 and narrower on 38, each narrowing a clause about another object or a granted / conditional one (the Swords, the Wards and other granting Auras, Akroma's Memorial, Hunted Horror's tokens, Commander's Plate, Grotesque Hybrid's "gains flying and protection …", Opal Guardian's animation …); the one card with the Protection keyword among them, Riftmarked Knight, keeps its own black and drops only its token's white. (3) **Colour qualities only** in the sweep, and only an attachment whose colours are known; **a bestowed Aura stays exempt** (CR 702.103f — it would become unattached and a creature, the bestow exit's job). (4) **The planeswalker witnesses grant protection with the resolver's own `applyGrantProtection`** — no native card grants a planeswalker protection (Angelic Intervention, Faith's Shield, Razor Barrier are Arbiter-routed; Eight-and-a-Half-Tails' grant isn't offered); the walker and the damage cards are real bundled cards cast and attacked through the engine. (5) **The trigger offer reads its source as the re-check does** (`context.sourceId ?? source.permanentId`, the id `offerSourceId` reads), so the two can't disagree, and an offer can only narrow: with colours threaded, the colour shields at the trigger offer (Thrun's "nongreen", hexproof from colours) now judge the colour instead of refusing every trigger — a wider, correct offer. (6) **A shield counter under "can't be prevented" is still removed** (CR 615.12's "additional effects … will take place"; the bundled ruling, 2022-04-29: "If a permanent with a shield counter is dealt unpreventable damage, that damage will be dealt and a shield counter will still be removed."). (7) **Maze of Ith's dealer half got its own stamp** rather than reading `noCombatDamageTurn` conditionally — that stamp is shared with Laccolith's "assigns no combat damage", which is not prevention and must hold under Frenzied Baloth; a game saved mid-turn with the old Maze stamp still reads it as "assigns no combat damage" for the rest of that turn. (8) The CHANGELOG's protection-last-known-information line (unreleased) ends "An Aura or Equipment already attached to a creature that gains the protection still stays attached." — now false; left as it is (the brief: don't edit other slices' lines) for the integrator.
> · ⚠️ **Found, not fixed:** (1) **The printed protection reader reads another object's protection as the card's own** — `protection.parseProtectionColors` (protection.js:79, read by `layers.permanentProtectionColors` :2264 at every protection site) takes "Equipped creature gets +2/+2 and has protection from red and from blue" as Sword of Fire and Ice's own protection, so a red or blue source can't target the Sword (Shatter can't; Captain America's Catch fizzled on it on the base and isn't offered it now — A/B games 21, 28, 29), and likewise the other Swords, the granting Auras (Mask of Law and Grace, the Wards), Akroma's Memorial, Commander's Plate (all five colours), Hunted Horror ("… tokens with protection from black" — Doom Blade can't target it, black creatures can't block it), Riftmarked Knight (its token's white), Grotesque Hybrid and Jodah's Avenger (a granted "gains … protection" the "gains" skip misses), Opal Guardian (conditional) — 38 faces. The `ownOnly` reading added here for the state-based action is the fix; switching every site to it is a slice of its own with its own A/B. (2) **The attach-to-self and self-attach atoms read no protection** (`effects/atoms/stack.js:274` applyAttachToSelf, `:250` applySelfAttach — CR 701.3a/b: an Equipment "can't be attached to an object … it couldn't … equip" and "doesn't move"): Captain America's Catch re-attached the red Lizard Blades to a Captain with protection from red (A/B game 24); the state-based action now unattaches it at the next check, so the end state is right, but the attach happened. (3) **Protection from everything on a player (Teferi's Protection, The One Ring) doesn't stop the rest of combat damage to that player** — `combatResolution.js` spillToDefender's player arm (:570 here, :548 at b33ae89a) records poison, commander damage, the lifelink credit, the monarch steal and the combat-damage-to-player event before :791 (:770 at b33ae89a) skips only the life loss: probed, a Teferi's Protection seat attacked by Glistener Elf and a lifelinking commander took 1 poison and 2 commander damage, and the attacker's controller gained 2. (4) A bestowed Aura whose host gains protection from it stays attached (sba.js:117 — CR 702.103f). (5) The two stack-object re-targets (`effects/atoms/stack.js:2259`, the retarget-to-me lane; `:2310`, the redirect to a source) re-enumerate with no source colours, so they can move a spell or ability onto a permanent with protection from it (it then fizzles there). (6) A cast trigger's source (the spell on the stack) and an ability of a card in a graveyard or hand read as unknown at the offer and the re-check alike (`abilitySource` — no permanent, no record). (7) The automatic protection pick (`protectionChoice.protectionColorPick`) doesn't weigh the Auras and Equipment the chosen colour would now knock off its own creature (Giver of Runes' colorless sheds the creature's colourless Equipment) — a decision-quality gap, not a rules one.

> ## 🔧 2026-10-22 — FIX (Academy, user-facing): a game one of the engine's guards stops ENDS — the runaway entry's judgment call (4). When the RUNAWAY size guard (`RUNAWAY_LIMITS`: a stack past 500, a seat past 2,000 permanents), the per-turn tick budget or the 50,000-tick safety cap fired, the person saw "⚠ The engine got stuck: runaway battlefield (2001 permanents, ai) — use “Abandon game” below to start over." and no choices; the session stayed `active`, no log line, no record, and the stuck game was AUTOSAVED (2b1c02a6 made autosave work) — "Abandon game" only resets the page, so it stayed in "Continue a game", and resuming it hit the guard at once. Now one design for all three: the driver names the guard on its decision — `guard` `{ type: "turn-stall", turn, count, limit }` / `{ type: "runaway", zone, count, limit, seat? }` / `{ type: "safety-cap", limit }` (`runawayExcess` is the size as data; `runawaySize` formats it as before; `safetyCap` is injectable like `turnTickBudget`) — and changes nothing else: `kind: "engine-stuck"`, the `reason` text and the `active` session are byte-identical, so every self-play consumer counts what it counted. The Academy ends the game: `learnSession.endEngineStoppedGame` (the `abandon` pattern — the driver never sets the status) gives status **`engine-stopped`** (terminal, not `abandoned`, whose "You ended the game early." would be false), `engineStop` `{ guard, reason, turn, detail, message }`, a game-log line with no seat as actor — "The engine stopped the game: Opponent controlled 2,001 permanents, past the engine's limit of 2,000 — a loop kept adding to the board." — an engine-log event `{ kind: "game-stopped", guard, reason }`, and answers `{ kind: "game-over", reason: "engine-stopped", guard, message, detail }` (what the driver itself answers for that session from then on). Every route that runs the engine applies it — start, step, choose, continue, mulligan, resume, resume-puzzle — and every finished game leaves through ONE path, `learnPersistence.persistAfterPlay` → `finishGame`: the record kept (`engineStop` on it), the session freed, the save dropped, the stop named in the server log. Resume finishes a game that is over when it re-derives, so a stuck save from before this fix ends the same way on its first resume and leaves the list. The end screen (`reasonToOutcome("engine-stopped", decision)`): "The engine stopped the game." + the detail + "Nobody won or lost. The game can't go on, so it is no longer offered under “Continue a game”; its record is kept." with the usual New game; a stopped puzzle attempt is `"stopped"` (no puzzle verdict); the Crucible home and Teferi's rail read "Stopped (no result)". **PLAY_API 1.7.0 → 1.8.0** (additive MINOR: the `guard` field, the `safetyCap` option, the route-only status — argued against §5's MAJOR in the contract) · **±0**

> ## 🔧 2026-10-22 — FIX (runaway): an outlet route that cannot finish never outbids enough by combat, and the outlet line never asks for a doubling past its cap — the runaway entry's found-not-fixed (1): the Squirrel-Girl-heavy batch's game 29 (seed 3964194058; Omnath, Locus of Mana / The Unbeatable Squirrel Girl / Vihaan, Goldwaker / cdh) ended engine-stuck "runaway stack (598 objects)" on turn 33 on e4e9f467 and its base alike. Root cause (replayed; probed at each doubling): Altar of the Brood ("Whenever another permanent you control enters, each opponent mills a card.") milled the Omnath seat's Kozilek, Butcher of Truth ("When Kozilek is put into a graveyard from anywhere, its owner shuffles their graveyard into their library."), and every doubling's mills reached it again — 13 "shuffle-graveyard-into-library" log lines for that seat on turns 32–33 (31, 5, 71, 11, 71, 22, 35, 75, 45, 52, 57, 26 and 61 cards) — so the mill route could never complete; yet `outlet.wantsMore` stayed true under `OUTLET_BOARD_CAP`, `holdLoop`'s `enoughNextTurn && !outlet?.wantsMore` (tokenLoopLine.js:168 at e4e9f467) let it outbid enough by combat (true from 305 permanents), and the cap was read on the board BEFORE the doubling (outletFinishLine.js:214 at e4e9f467), so at 593 permanents she doubled 576 Squirrels. > · **Judgment calls:** (1) **"Can complete" is read from the public record**: the engine logs every graveyard-into-library reshuffle with the player and the count, and one such line for a living opponent this game blocks every mill route. The line does not say whether its source comes back (Kozilek does, Finale of Revelation does not), so a one-shot reads like a repeating one — the side where enough by combat wins, the brief's stated fallback; hidden cards are never read (an unseen Kozilek in a library is not known, and the route stays open until the first reshuffle). (2) **A blocked mill route is neither live nor done**, not only "wants no more": otherwise Altar of Dementia would still be fed the Squirrels that make combat lethal, and a library the passive mill emptied after a reshuffle would read as the finish. (3) **A shot route can always complete** — life gain is not read, and there is no projection of whether a route finishes under the cap (with commander life totals and ~100-card libraries every route that is not blocked does). (4) **The cap counts the board the next activation leaves** (X and Took's Food, times the doublers), the strict `<` 600 kept; the existing cap test calls `outletState` without a yield and still pins the plain boundary — no existing test changed. (5) **Short of enough the loop still builds when the outlet cannot ask** (blocked, or at the cap) — the no-outlet rule; the cap was never a bound on the loop itself and is not now. (6) **The outlet finish's comment was made true, not the code**: reading `extra` there would fire a complete route at an opponent's end step or in response — a behavior change that wants its own slice and measurement (the 2026-10-20 windows rule). (7) The runaway builder's cap-after-the-doubling attempt held at 593 and crawled; here game 29 holds at 305 because enough by combat wins, and the cap alone still stops a completable route below 600.
> · ⚠️ **Found, not fixed:** (1) **"Enough" with no outlet that can ask, against hundreds of creatures** (tokenLoopLine.js:180–184, `enoughNextTurn`): finite — every creature she controls must beat, twice over, each opponent's life through all of that opponent's creatures (with 1/1 Squirrels, Σ(creatures + 2 × life)) — but one doubling can overshoot that by up to 2×, so a need past ~1,000 crosses the 2,000-permanent battlefield guard, and the engine slows long before (game 29: ~56 s for one opponent turn against 305 permanents). Not seen in either batch. (2) **Her own pending Altar triggers do not hold the loop**: with the route blocked and combat short, she doubles with the previous doubling's triggers still on the stack (72 + 144 = 216 in game 29); one more there would have been 504, past the 500-object stack guard. `holdLoop` waits only for her own loop activation on the stack (tokenLoopLine.js:155, :193). Not seen to fire in either batch. (3) **A milled Blightsteel Colossus goes to the graveyard**: `millCards` (gameState.js:1238) applies the exile-instead replacements but not the shuffle-instead one ("If Blightsteel Colossus would be put into a graveyard from anywhere, reveal Blightsteel Colossus and shuffle it into its owner's library instead." — Darksteel Colossus, Progenitus and Nexus of Fate as well); probed on the base archive: milled → graveyard. Fixed, it would be a second way a library cannot be milled out with no reshuffle line in the log (its event is "shuffle-instead-of-graveyard"). (4) **`moveCardToZone` from library to graveyard duplicates such a card in the library** (gameState.js:868, the recursive move to "library" from "library"): probed — library [Forest, Blightsteel, Blightsteel]; reachable from manifest.js:106.
