> · **The gaps** (ac720a90): `atoms/stack.applyRetarget` and `applyRedirectToSource` rewrote a stack object's targets without `withWardOwed`; `actionDispatcher.applyDiscardAbility` and `applyActivateGyExile` put a targeted ability on the stack with no ward raise; `groupWard.groupWardTaxForStackObject` returned null unless the object had exactly one permanent target and returned the first Diffusion source only, and was asked only at the cast, activation and loyalty paths, after the ward, through the single choice slot (`setPendingSoftCounterChoice` no-ops when occupied); `freshCopyTargets` took the first enemy-side combo and `newTargetsForCopy` kept or took the first fitting set whatever ward they carried; `learnSession.settleSoftCounterChoice` / `settleDiscardChoice` ran `gameEngine.returnPriorityAfterWard` (the `priorityAfter` the raises stamped), handing priority back to the caster after `finalizeStackResolution`'s reset to the active player.
> · **The fix** — `ward.targetTaxForStackObject(state, obj)` (new): the wards (`wardInstancesFor`, the old `wardTaxForStackObject` body) plus `groupWard.groupWardInstancesFor` (new — for each targeted permanent an opponent of the object's controller controls, each permanent once, one {N} instance per group-ward source its controller controls whose subtype it carries), combined by `combineWardCosts`, names the ward permanents' then the sources', each once. Every raise asks it: `actionDispatcher.raiseTargetTax` (new — the cast path, with the uncounterable log; the battlefield activation; the loyalty ability; and now `applyDiscardAbility` and `applyActivateGyExile`), `gameEngine.markWardOwed`, `atoms/stack.withWardOwed` (copies, `moveStackTarget`, and now `applyRetarget` and `applyRedirectToSource`); the AI's readers too (`opponentAI.wardCountersAction` / `withoutWardCounteredActions` — WARD_RAISING_KINDS gains `discard-ability` and `activate-gy-exile`, `afterOwnCosts` pays a graveyard ability's mana by the dispatcher's plan and takes a channel card out of the hand — and `gameEngine.withoutUnpaidWard`). `groupWardTaxForStackObject` stays as the Diffusion-only sum; `groupWardTaxForSpell` is gone. The copy picks: `copyKeepsTargets` (new) — no ward or Diffusion trigger on the set, or the copier can pay it (`ward.canPayWardCost`, moved from `runProgram.canAffordWardCost` so atoms/stack reads the AI's pay-if-able answer without an import cycle; runProgram now imports it), or the copy can't be countered; `freshCopyTargets` takes the first enemy-side combo that keeps, else the old pick; `newTargetsForCopy` keeps wanted-side targets that keep, re-aims kept targets only to a set that keeps, and otherwise prefers a fitting set that keeps. Priority: `returnPriorityAfterWard`, `priorityAfter` (the six dispatcher stamps, `raiseWardOwed`'s, the soft-counter setter's parameter, runProgram's two carries onto a discard pause, the driver's wire strip) are removed — the settle's `finalizeStackResolution` gives the active player priority. ENGINE-SCAFFOLD ("Ward, the leftovers"; the "Ward, finished" priority sentence; the actor-keeps-priority note; "Ward in the AI's own aim"), PLAY-API-CONTRACT's `soft-counter` row (paths, Diffusion, priority — no shape change, PLAY_API_VERSION stays 1.7.0).
> · **Judgment calls:** (1) **Priority after a ward: the active player (CR 117.3b), reversing the ward-finished slice's call (the caster, CR 117.3c).** In the rules the caster receives priority with the ward on the stack (117.3c, 117.5); when every player has passed the ward resolves — its "counter unless that player pays" is its effect — and the active player receives priority (117.3b). The engine asks the question at once, which is the ward resolving after every player passed; the only state the rules produce at that moment is the active player holding priority with the pass count at 0. Handing it to a non-active caster gives priority to a player the rules never give it to then (the forbidden direction); the active player's model withholds only the caster's chance to respond to their own ward before it resolves (an under-offer, the safe direction — THE CREED). Shipped in v0.168.0 as "paying it no longer costs you priority", so the CHANGELOG line says it is reversed and why; the caster still gets priority before the spell resolves (every player passes in succession). (2) **One question for the wards and Diffusion Sliver** — each is its own trigger, and paying some but not all of them counters the object all the same (the ward-finished slice's rule for several wards); the panel's `sourceName` names them all. (3) **Diffusion counts each targeted permanent once** (as ward does) and each source separately (CR 603.2c). (4) **The copy picks read the board as it is**, before any ward is paid: N storm copies may each pick a ward permanent the controller can pay once (found-not-fixed (4)). Kept targets on the wanted side are re-aimed only to a set the copier would keep; when no such set exists the old pick stands, so a copy is never moved to a worse target. (5) **The AI's ward read covers the two new activation kinds** (it would otherwise aim a channel ability where the new raise counters it); a channel ability's live-priced mana is not taken off, so its read errs toward "paid" — the old aim. (6) Deflecting Swat's own pick (`applyRetarget`'s first combo off the retargeter's stuff) is unchanged: the ward it now raises falls on the spell's controller.
> · ⚠️ **Found, not fixed:** (1) **The AI pays the ward on a forced trigger that only helps an opponent** (`effects/runProgram.autoPickSoftCounterPay` :1778, the driver's AI fallback, learnSession.js:2062 also feeds the person's `affordable`) — LEFT, not small and certain: an "own"-intent atom is not always a pure gift to the creature it lands on (Otherworldly Journey's `delayed-blink` also takes an opponent's creature away until the end step; an untap or a blink can help either side), so a decline needs a per-op "pure gift" reader and must stay out of the affordability flag; the 80-game census below saw no triggered ability asked a ward. (2) The two activation lanes that now raise ward still skip the other target events — becomes-the-target (Phantasmal Image), crime and Kira (`actionDispatcher.applyDiscardAbility` :1951, `applyActivateGyExile` :1487; the battlefield path runs all four). (3) Kira, Great Glass-Spinner's counter is the same collapsed trigger as a ward but leaves priority with the caster (the cast/activation paths' `applyKiraTargetCounter`, actionDispatcher.js:1183, :1879, :2075, then `priorityHolder: action.playerId`): after Kira's trigger resolves the active player should receive priority (CR 117.3b). (4) The storm picks don't reserve earlier copies' ward payments (`freshCopyTargets` :1710 — each copy reads the board before any ward is paid). (5) A copied activated or triggered ability keeps the original's targets with no re-aim (`applyCopyActivatedAbility` :2493, `applyCopyTargetAbility` :2510 — "you may choose new targets" is always declined), so it may meet a ward its controller can't pay with no alternative tried. (6) A storm copy of a permanent spell carries no target (`applyCopySpell`'s permanent branch, :1902): a storm Aura's copy (Krosan Adaptation, Amphibian Downpour, Tempest Technique) chooses its host at resolution, so no ward is ever asked for it.

> ## 🔧 2026-10-22 — FIX (deck library, user-facing): every saved deck has an `id`, so every deck can be picked — the Academy could not start a game with 6 of the owner's 8 decks, as his deck or an opponent's: their library entries had no `id`, LearnView's `<option key={d.id} value={d.id}>` rendered them with no value, the browser submitted the deck NAME, `savedDecks.find((d) => d.id === userDeckId)` missed and Start stayed disabled. /api/decks now gives every id-less deck a derived, stable id — a POST as it saves, a GET by rewriting each profile's deck file once with a backup — and the pickers never value an option by anything but an id · **±0**
> **Root cause.** The app's own creation paths always stamped an id — paste import (`Date.now()`, useDeckStore.js:347 at 2b1c02a6), URL import (`randomUUID`, :381); Karn never creates a deck (his applies go through `updateDeckById(lock.id)`). The id-less decks came in through `POST /api/decks`, which saved whatever it was sent (`body.decks.map(normalizeDeck)`; normalizeDeck never sets an id): all 28 id-less decks across the three profiles of the A/B data copy (Colton 6 of 8, Joe 11 of 11, Omnath 11 of 11) have the import preview's key order — `name, format, source, cards` (import-url/route.js's response) then `memory` — and cards carrying `oracleId` / `resolved`, which the in-app import strips; so an outside writer posted the preview with a `memory` and no id (inferred from the shape; COMMS 2026-10-03 records deck writes through that POST). In-app, the library-JSON import (`importDeckLibrary`) kept id-less decks id-less and merged them by `owner:name` — on the base, three imported decks two of which share a name saved as two — and the localStorage-cache fallback, the first-launch copy, the user-data restore and the profile migration all copy decks as they are. The same id-less decks broke every other id-keyed surface (the consumer audit, read-only, live data included): choosing any of them in the deck list made the FIRST of them active and dropped its edits (`updateActiveDeck`'s `if (!activeDeckId) return`); the × on one deleted all of them (`deleteDeck(undefined)` → `filter(deck => deck.id !== id)`), saved at once; DeckConfirmModal, Practice, deck cost, MulliganLab, DeckReport and Garfield insights were unreachable; Sim Center / Pod Balance rows ticked together and the Crucible / A/B bench couldn't select them (`selectDecksByIds`); the collection context Karn reads ("in N other decks") skipped them (collectionContext.js:99 `deck.id != null`).
> **The fix** — `lib/deck/deckIds.js` (new, isomorphic): `hasDeckId` (a non-blank string or a finite number), `derivedDeckId` = `deck_<name slug>_<8 base-36>` of a cyrb53 hash over (scope, owner, name, ordinal among the id-less decks of that owner + name), `ensureDeckIds(decks, { scope, reserved })` — an existing id is never changed, a derived id already in use takes `_2`, `_3`…, the same library always derives the same ids. `api/decks/route.js`: **POST** stamps any id-less deck (scope = the active profile id) and logs it; **GET** — `withDeckIds` — when the active library has an id-less deck, `backfillDeckIds` runs INSIDE the existing write chain (so it can't interleave with a save), re-reads the file, copies the original to `backups/decks.local.<stamp>.deck-id-backfill.json` (the existing reason-tagged `createBackup` convention, never pruned), and rewrites it once through `atomicWriteJson` with only the ids added (each deck otherwise written back as stored; a concurrent read finds nothing left to do); a failed backfill is logged and the library is still served, with the ids a later read will write. `backfillOtherProfilesOnce` does the same for every other registered profile once per server process (each with its own profile id as scope — what its own read derives), because the Sim Center, Pod Balance, the Crucible and the A/B bench pick across profiles. `useDeckStore`: the loaded library (and the localStorage fallback) through `ensureDeckIds`; `importDeckLibrary` gives an id-less imported deck a new id unique against the library and adds it (never merged by name). `LearnView`: `deckPickerOptions` (key + value = the id; a deck without a usable id, or repeating a listed id, is shown disabled with the reason) and `learnStartPicks` (the Start gate, matching by `String(id)`); the Practice handoff through the same lookup. History recorded under a deck's NAME before it had an id (toRunnerDeck's `deck.id || deck.name`) stays with the deck: `summarizeGrind` folds a name-keyed row into the one id-keyed row of that name (a name two ids share is left apart), `mineDeckHistory` reads the deck-versions registry under both keys. PROJECT-SCAFFOLD §2.1 records the deck-id contract.
> **Evidence.** Witnesses first, on an untouched `git archive` of 2b1c02a6, failing on assertions (0 thrown): deckIdBackfill.test.js 12/15 red (the owner's shape served with ids, the existing two unchanged, all distinct; one rewrite + a byte-identical backup; idempotent; the same ids after a restart and when redone from the backup; same-name decks differ; the collision suffix; a failed backup logged, the file untouched, retried with the same ids; the other profiles at the first read; POST stamps; a re-post lands on the same ids), 3 controls green on both; learnDeckPicker.test.jsx 6/7 red (SSR of LearnView with the library GET serves: every option valued by its id and found by the Start gate's lookup, Start ready for all 64 pairings; id-less / repeated-id decks disabled, no key warning), 1 control; useDeckStoreDeckIds.test.jsx 2/4 red (the hook's library import, driven through an SSR probe, POSTs ids — on the base it saved 2 of 3), 2 controls (URL import and id'd libraries stamped / kept on both); deckIdHistory.test.js 2/5 red (one standings row; the version diff across the name / id registry keys), 3 controls. After: 39/39 with deckIds.test.js (8). Suite **22,671 green (1 skipped) / 2,017 files** under the v3 gate queue (07:15–07:20Z; the rules index built in the worktree with no MTG_APP_ROOT, deleted after; sha256 over app/src + app/scripts 0ade52b5… at the hold's start and end). Lint 0 (`npm run lint` — eslint 0 warnings; CR citations: 0 of 13,382 name no rule; keyword citations: 0 of 2,759). **Mutants 6/6** on assertions, each restored byte-identical (sha256), in a copy of the final tree: GET without the backfill (12 red), the backfill without its backup (5), ensureDeckIds replacing existing ids (10), the picker valuing an id-less deck by its name (1), no sweep of the other profiles (1), no standings fold (1). In the hold the backup mutant's fifth failure was an ENOENT from the test's own `readdir`; that helper now treats a missing backups/ as empty — the file re-run alone: 15/15 green here, 12/15 red on the base (all assertions), the backup mutant 5 red, all assertions, restored byte-identical. > · **Judgment calls:** (1) **Derived ids, not random** — a retried, raced or restored backfill, and a window opened before it re-posting id-less decks, land on the same ids; client-side stamping (library import, localStorage fallback) uses an empty scope — ids are unique within a library, the contract every per-profile consumer relies on. (2) **Every profile, once per server start**, not only the active one: 22 of the 28 id-less decks are in profiles the owner may never open, and the cross-profile pickers need them. (3) **The reason-tagged backup**, one per file, not the 10-deep autobackup ring (it prunes). (4) **Raw decks written back**, not normalized — only the ids change. (5) **A failed backfill never fails the read** — logged; served with the ids the next read writes. (6) **Library import adds an id-less deck** rather than merging by name — the old merge silently dropped one of two same-named decks; re-importing an old id-less export now adds copies instead of replacing. (7) **Unpickable decks are listed, disabled, with the reason**, not hidden. (8) **History folds on read** (standings, version history); the 159,798-game grind store and deck-versions.json are not rewritten.

(2) `scripts/swap-bench.mjs:46` (`--ids=`) and `scripts/seat-fairness-gate.mjs:32` (`--deck-id=`) match runner ids, which were the deck names for these decks — a name stops matching after the backfill (no saved invocation found). (3) While a backfill write keeps failing, the derived ids served exist only in the response: routes that read the deck file directly (mulligan-lab, collection/deck-costs, self-play, pod-balance) can't find such a deck by id until a read writes it or the client saves (route.js `withDeckIds`, logged). (4) A non-active profile that gains an id-less deck while the server runs is backfilled at the next start or when opened. (5) `scripts/check-deck-library.cjs:5` still reads the pre-profiles flat `data/decks.local.json`.

> ## 🔧 2026-10-21 — FIX (runaway): the token loop's "enough" holds in every window the AI activates in — since b780b241 the standard A/B's game 16 (seed 3816266519; Zaxara, Veyran, Killer Turts, The Unbeatable Squirrel Girl) ended engine-stuck on every tree: at the end step of ai1, whose turn came right before hers, the Squirrel Girl seat activated "I LOVE Squirrels! — {1}{G}{G}{G}: Create X 1/1 green Squirrel creature tokens, where X is the number of Squirrels you control." four times (160, 320, 640, 1,280 tokens) and the runaway size guard stopped the game at 2,572 permanents. Root cause (replayed; probed at each of those decisions): `tokenLoopState` read `holdLoop: true` there — 167 creatures against one opponent at 40 with two creatures, enough twice over for next turn, the stack empty, no outlet — but only the main phase's generic picker consulted it; b780b241's end-step sink (`pickEndStepSink`) reads the activations offered outside the default windows (`extra`) and hands them to `pickSafeAbilityActivation`, which takes a token maker. Now `pickAction` reads `tokenLoopState` once, right after the window split, and while `holdLoop` the loop ability leaves both `actions` and `extra` before any picker — the end-step sink, the save in response, the pump after blocks and the generic picker read the one judgment (Colton 2026-10-03: build only to enough, then the finish); the generic picker's own copy of the filter is gone. > ## 🔧 2026-10-21 — FIX (Academy save/resume, user-facing): Academy games are kept on disk again — from v0.161.0 (7e10c186, 2026-09-29) `engineBuild()` threw in every Next-bundled server, so no Academy autosave, no "Save as puzzle" and no in-app ∞ grind worked in `npm run dev` or the exe, and the play routes' empty catches hid the autosave failure; the version is now a static JSON import, and no save failure is silent any more — each is logged and shown, none blocks play · **±0**
> **Reproduced the way a person plays** (`next dev` on 127.0.0.1:3047, MTG_APP_ROOT = a scratch copy under C:/tmp/day-autosave, browser pane): Academy → Learn to Play → Omnath, Locus of Mana vs The Unbeatable Squirrel Girl, Beginner → Start, Ship, Keep, bottom Akroma's Memorial, Play Forest, Cast Fyndhorn Elves, Pass ×2 — `/api/learn/start`, `/mulligan` ×3, `/choose`, `/step` ×4 all 200, and no `learn-sessions` folder anywhere under the root (the save threw before its mkdir). The hook's exact request sequence (useLearnSession: start → mulligan ship / keep / bottom → step) replayed over HTTP: no save after any of 8 requests; the same route handlers imported by plain Node with the same payloads: the save rewritten after every request — the report's observation exactly ("the dev server never rewrote the save; a node script driving the same routes saved fine"), and on every play route, not only after a resume. **Root cause, seen:** "Save as puzzle" in that game answered 500 with the exception the autosave catch was swallowing — `TypeError [ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE]: The "path" argument must be of type string or an instance of Buffer or URL. Received an instance of URL` at engineBuild.js:75, `readFileSync(new URL("../../../package.json", import.meta.url))`. Next's webpack (`module.parser.javascript.url: "relative"`) compiles that expression to `new __webpack_require__.U(<the package.json module>)` in dev and to `new c.U("/_next/static/media/package.<hash>.json")` in `next build` — the v0.168.0 chunk in the install folder carries exactly the latter (chunks/1374.js, as this session's MSIX view shows it; not run) — and readFileSync rejects webpack's relative-URL object; autosaveSession calls engineBuild() while it builds the save document, before the mkdir. The same throw stopped puzzleStore (Save as puzzle) and grindLoop (the Crucible's ∞ grind: bundled with Next's webpack, the base grind stops at once with that error, this tree's runs). Candidates ruled out: isSerializable / atomicWriteJson (the save never reached them), another route stepping without a save (all five play routes autosave; resume re-derives and the next move saves), a stale resume, a read/write path mismatch (one profilePath for both).
> **The fix** — engineBuild.js imports package.json `with { type: "json" }`: webpack inlines it at build time (after release.yml's version stamp), Node 22 reads it natively (no warning on 22.23); `createRequire(import.meta.url)` was tried and rejected — webpack leaves it to resolve against the build machine's path at run time. eslint's `src` ecmaVersion 2024 → 2025 (import attributes). No silent catch is left on the save path: `learnPersistence.js` (new) — `autosaveForPlay` (logs; returns `{ kind: "autosave", detail }`, also for a save written but not resumable), `recordFinishedGame` (logs; `{ kind: "game-record" }`), `dropFinishedGameSave` (logs only — cleanup: the game is over and its record kept; a leftover save at worst lingers in the resume list until pruned); start / step / choose / continue / mulligan put `saveFailure` in their response. learnSaveStore: a failed index write throws (the Resume list reads the index); deleteSave throws on anything but ENOENT (the saves/delete route already answers 500); pruning stays best-effort and logs (an AggregateError of the deletions that failed); listSaves self-heals from the save files and logs an index it can't write back. The hook keeps `saveFailure` / `saveFailureDismissed` through the pure `nextSaveNotice` in all 27 play-response handlers and start, plus `dismissSaveFailure`; LearnView's `SaveFailureNotice` (role=status, one gold line under the table strip, × to close, the detail as its tooltip) stays closed while saves keep failing and re-arms after a good save. console.error reaches server.err.log in the exe. docs/gotchas.md: never read a file through `new URL(…, import.meta.url)` in server code.
> **Evidence.** Witnesses first, on an untouched `git archive` of 3197f044, failing on assertions: engineBuild.bundled.test.js (bundles learnSaveStore + engineBuild with next/dist/compiled/webpack, dev and production mode) 4/4 red with that ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE; autosaveFailure.test.js 7/13 red (each play route with the save folder blocked: no `saveFailure`, no log; a game-over record failure unreported; an undeletable in-flight save unlogged), its 6 controls green on both; learnSaveStore.test.js 4/14 red (deleteSave, the index write, listSaves' log, the prune log), 10 green on both. Suite **22,542 green (1 skipped) / 2,007 files** under the v3 gate queue (04:50–04:54Z; the rules index built in the worktree for the run with no MTG_APP_ROOT, deleted after; sha256 of the worktree's src/ + scripts/ ec9aefc6… at the hold's start and end). Lint 0 (`npm run lint` — eslint 0 warnings; CR citations: 0 of 13,267 name no rule; keyword citations: 0 of 2,726). **Mutants 6/6** on assertions, each restored byte-identical (sha256), in a copy of the final tree: engineBuild back to the `new URL` read (4 red), autosaveForPlay swallowing (6), the step route dropping `saveFailure` (2), autosaveSession swallowing the index write (1), deleteSave swallowing every unlink failure (3), a good save not clearing the notice (2); the witness files 45/45 green after. A/B **80 seeded commander games** (base seed 7, 10 per pod, the 30 profile decks, default AI; base = the untouched 3197f044 archive; reference data from a scratch copy, MTG_APP_ROOT per command, its 18 files sha256-unchanged): **80 / 80 byte-identical, 0 winner changes** (ai-wins 54 / user-wins 25 / engine-stuck 1 — game 16, seed 3816266519, stuck at turn 31 identically on both trees); 497.3 s / 503.8 s. **Production build** (a second hold, 06:13–06:15Z: `next build` — Next 15.5.18, the build the exe ships — of the 3197f044 archive and of this tree, each standalone server on 127.0.0.1 with a scratch MTG_APP_ROOT, the hook's request sequence replayed): base — 7 requests answered 200, no save folder ever created, Save as puzzle 500 with that ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE in the server log; this tree — the save rewritten after each of the 7 (the index lists it resumable at turn 3), Save as puzzle 200.
> · **What the person sees** (`next dev`, this tree, scratch root): the same pairing played through the UI — the save rewritten after Start, each mulligan answer and each of five moves (turn 1 main → turn 3 main; Forest, Fyndhorn Elves and Boseiju on the board; engineVersion stamped); dev server stopped and restarted; Academy → "Continue a game: Omnath, Locus of Mana · Standard · turn 3 · beginner" → Resume → turn 3, your main, life 40 / 38, hand 4, the same three permanents and the same "Cast Wild Growth → Forest / Boseiju" actions. The save file made read-only: Cast Wild Growth → the game went on (Wild Growth on the stack) and "⚠ Autosave failed — your game may not survive a restart. ×" appeared under the life totals, the server log carrying `[learn] autosave failed for learn-… Error: EPERM: operation not permitted, rename …`; × closed it and it stayed closed through two more failing moves; the file writable again → the next move saved; read-only again → the notice came back.
> · **Judgment calls:** (1) **All five play routes, not only /step** — the same empty catch sat in start, choose, continue and mulligan. (2) **What a person is shown:** a failed autosave and a failed finished-game record; dropping a finished game's save and pruning old saves are cleanup and only log. (3) **A save written but not resumable** (a closure in state) counts as an autosave failure — the game would not survive a restart. (4) **A failed index write counts too** — the save file exists but the Resume list would not show it. (5) **The notice doesn't nag**: one failure shows it; closed, it stays closed until a save succeeds again.
> · ⚠️ **Found, not fixed:** (1) The /continue route ends a game without a record — step, choose and mulligan keep a finished game's record, continue does not (continue/route.js:66), so a game that ends on the move after an Arbiter ruling never reaches the Crucible's records. (2) The Learn deck pickers can't select a saved deck that has no `id` — the option value falls back to the deck's name, `savedDecks.find((d) => d.id === userDeckId)` misses and Start game stays disabled (LearnView.jsx:216–218; the `<option key={d.id} value={d.id}>` rows — React also warns of the duplicate keys); with the scratch copy of the profile, 6 of Colton's 8 decks could not be picked. (3) After a resume the header reads "You vs Opponent" and the game log "No actions yet." — the resume response carries no deck names or log tail (the header reads the pickers; useLearnSession's resume sets `decisionLogTail: []`). (4) atomicJson.js:52 still drops a failure to remove its temp file (`.catch(() => {})`) while it rethrows the real error. (5) A save file that is not valid JSON is skipped from the index without a word (learnSaveStore `indexFromFiles` → `readJsonSafe`).
> · ⚠️ **Process:** a first production-build attempt (05:13Z, inside the gate hold) ran `npx next build` in a tree copy whose node_modules junction had not been made (MSYS rewrote `mklink /J`), and npx fetched and ran next@16.4.2 from the npm registry into the npm cache (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\npm-cache\_npx\8b377f6eec906bc4` and its tarballs) — an unapproved download and a write under %LOCALAPPDATA%; the build failed before building anything and nothing else was touched. Left in place for Colton to remove; the check now refuses to build without the junction and calls the local next binary. Two two-file vitest runs also ran outside the gate queue early on.

> ## 🔧 2026-10-21 — FIX (rules faithfulness, two coupled false positives): protection judges a DEPARTED ability source by its last known information, and protection from COLORLESS is enforced (CR 608.2b — "If the source of an ability has left the zone it was in, its last known information is used during this process."; CR 113.7a; CR 105.2c — "A colorless object has no color."; CR 702.16b–f) — the protection-colour-choice entry's found-not-fixed (2) and (3): `spellEffects.resolutionSourceColors` (spellEffects.js:714 at 3197f044) read an ability's source by its CURRENT colours, so once the source had left the battlefield the layer engine derived it as colourless and the CR 608.2b re-check's empty colour list never made a target illegal — Executioner's Capsule, sacrificed to activate it, destroyed a creature that gained protection from black in response; and `protection.protectionApplies` (protection.js:106) matched colour letters only, so Giver of Runes' "protection from colorless" — on offer in the person's chooser, pickable by the AI — did nothing. COUPLED: enforcing colorless on the old read would have let protection from colorless stop that black Capsule, so the departed source's record comes first and a source's colours are now KNOWN (an empty list is colourless) or unknown (never colourless) · **±0** · snapshot native 15,877 unchanged
> Suite **22,525 green (1 skipped) / 2,004 files** under the v3 gate queue, first run, in ONE hold with every other number below (04:16–04:41Z: the base snapshot and A/B, then this tree's suite and lint, then — gated on both green — its snapshot, A/B, the mutants and the witnesses); the rules index was built in the worktree's app/data for the run with no MTG_APP_ROOT in that job, then deleted; sha256 over app/src and app/scripts c6dcde27… before the suite, after it, at the after-side start and at the hold's end; the base's 8b606fbf… at its start and end. The docs (this entry, CHANGELOG, ENGINE-SCAFFOLD) were written beside the runs; no test reads them. Lint 0 (`npm run lint` — eslint, 0 warnings; CR citations: 0 of 13,344 name no rule; keyword citations: 0 of 2,743 cite a different keyword). Flip-diff **0 / 0 / RETIERED 0** (34,620 cards; before = an untouched `git archive` of 3197f044, its src/ + scripts/ checked file-for-file against a fresh archive; native 15,877 of 34,584 snapshot names on both). **Mutants 8/8** on assertions, each restored byte-identical (per-file sha256 checked; the scratch copy's src sha 77433fc2… before and after; a scratch copy of the final tree, inside the hold): **THE COUPLING — B without A**, the re-check reading a departed source as the base did, a missing permanent's derived colourless taken as known (10 tests red — among them the coupling control, the unread-source control and the Capsule witnesses); the dispatcher freezing no record for a targeted ability whose source leaves paying its cost (2); no record stamped onto a targeted ability whose source leaves while it waits (1); the target offer and re-check ignoring a known colourless source (2); `protectionApplies` never applying colorless (8); a colourless creature allowed to block (1); the damage path reading a departed record's colours as unknown (2); a departed source never a creature (1). Witness `protectionLastKnownColorless.test.js` (20, real bundled oracle text), run in its final form on an untouched copy of 3197f044: **13 fail there, all on assertions; 7 pass on both** (controls: protected from black BEFORE the activation — White Knight, or Mother's grant — the Capsule is never offered at it, CR 601.2c before 601.2h; Neurok Replica made red bounces through protection from colorless; THE COUPLING — a black Capsule whose source has left destroys Bears with protection from colorless; a departed source with no record kept is never read as colourless; a source still on the battlefield; Terminate (black and red) against protection from black; no protection, and protection from colorless against a red Pyroclasm). The three `protectionColorChoice.test.js` tests changed on purpose fail on the base on assertions; its other 16 pass on both. A/B **80 seeded commander games** (base seed 7, 10 per pod, the 30 profile decks, default AI; base = the untouched 3197f044 archive; reference data from a scratch copy, MTG_APP_ROOT per command): **80 / 80 byte-identical**, **0 winner changes**, results unchanged (ai-wins 54 / user-wins 25 / engine-stuck 1 — game 16, seed 3816266519, Zaxara / Veyran / Killer Turts / Squirrel Girl, stuck at turn 31 identically on both trees); 507.9 s / 494.3 s. Why identical: Giver of Runes (5 casts) and Mother of Runes (4) never activated in the 80 games on either tree — 0 protection grants — so nothing was ever protected against a departed or colourless source; the change is never reached there, and its evidence is the witnesses.
> · **The fix** — (A) `gameState.departedSourceLki(state, ctx, id)`: the ONE reader, in the damage path's order (the ability's own `ctx.abilitySourceLki`, the shared `state.sacrificedSelfLki`, a self dies trigger's `ctx.dyingQualities`, the entering-creature lane's `ctx.triggeringLki`; each only for its own permanent id), read by `shared.damageSourceFor` (refactored onto it, outputs unchanged) and by `spellEffects.resolutionSource(state, obj, sourceId)` → `{ colors, known }` (replaces `resolutionSourceColors`: a spell's card / a source on the battlefield / a departed source's record — known; nothing kept — unknown), which the re-check (`targeting.resolutionTargetVerdicts`), the change-target alternatives, a copy's new targets and `protectionChoice.stackObjectProtectionColors` read. CAPTURE: the dispatcher's freeze (a source leaving as its own cost is paid) and `gameState.stampAbilitySourceLki` (a source leaving while its ability waits) now also write the record for an ability with chosen targets (`abilityHasChosenTargets`), not only one that deals damage or reads its power — so the record rides the ability, and a second sacrifice in response (which overwrites the shared stamp) no longer leaves the Capsule unread. `enumerateTargets` reads a departed source's creature-ness off the same record (`lkiRecordIsCreature` — protection from creatures; Perilous Myr's dies trigger is no longer offered Beloved Chaplain). (B) `protectionApplies(prot, colors)`: an empty array is a colourless source — "C" in the protected set applies to it; `null` is a source the caller can't read (nothing applies). `canBeTargetedBy(…, sourceColorsKnown)` / `ctx.sourceColorsKnown`, threaded only where the colours are definite (every cast offer, the activated-ability and Equip offers, the Aura host lanes, the Aura and Equip resolvers' re-checks, and the re-check / change-target / copy when `resolutionSource` says known); `damageDealer.colorsKnown` for `protectedFromDealer`; `combatEvasion.canBlockAttacker` refuses a colourless blocker; combat damage needed no edit (`combatResolution.protectionPrevents` — its sources are on the battlefield, definite; the file the sibling day-dmgfull is changing is untouched). `protectionThreats` reads colourless and departed threats; `opponentAI.pickSaveInResponse` lets colorless save from a harm whose source has no colour. Docs: ENGINE-SCAFFOLD (a new protection paragraph after the colour-choice one; the deal path's dealer; the AI-windows sentence), CHANGELOG (and the colour-choice line's now-false clause, unreleased), comments in protection.js / layers.js / choicePolicy.js / opponentAI.js.
> · **Tests changed on purpose:** `protectionColorChoice.test.js` — three tests encoded the two limits this slice removes: "control: a colourless threat is not read" (Giver vs Rod of Ruin now grants colorless; Mother, with no colorless to offer, keeps the board read), "an ability whose source has left is read only for its damage" (the AI's Mother now answers Executioner's Capsule), "a person is never told a colour stops what it won't stop here" (the Capsule's question marks black as the threat, Rod of Ruin's marks colorless); the header note updated.
> · **Judgment calls:** (1) **Known vs unknown is opt-in** (FN-safe): colorless is enforced only where the caller holds a definite reading; a path that threads no colours (trigger and loyalty offers) stays unenforced. The reverse — an empty list is colourless unless marked unknown — would turn every missed path into a false positive, the coupling's own failure. (2) **The capture covers an ability with chosen targets**, not every ability: the re-check is the reader that needed it; the damage and power readers keep their own conditions. (3) **One reader for the damage path and the re-check**, in the damage path's existing order, so the two can't disagree about a departed source. (4) **Creature-ness of a departed source is read at the offer too** (`enumerateTargets` reads `ctx.sourceId` at both): a dies trigger is offered no target with protection from creatures; the trigger offers' colours are unchanged (none threaded). (5) **The colour shields** (Thrun, Veil of Summer) still read an empty list as unknown even when the source is known colourless — unchanged, found-not-fixed (5). (6) **No PLAY_API bump**: the person's question keeps its shape; only which threats it names changes. (7) The "opponents control" shields read the ability's controller, not the departed source's last known controller — unchanged; the two are the same for every activated ability. (8) Base = 3197f044 as briefed.
> · ⚠️ **Found, not fixed:** (1) **Trigger target offers thread no source colours** — `gameEngine.js:1656, 1745, 1796, 1899` pass `[]`: protection from a colour (or colorless) is judged only at the re-check, so a trigger can be put on the stack aimed at a protected permanent and then do nothing to it. (2) The loyalty-ability offer likewise (`legalChoices.js:4385`). (3) **The attach state-based action reads no protection** — `sba.sweepAttachmentLegality` (sba.js:70): an Aura or Equipment already attached when its host gains protection from its quality stays (CR 702.16c/d, 704.5m, 704.5n), for every quality (Giver's colorless on a creature wearing Lightning Greaves leaves the Greaves on). (4) Damage to a planeswalker checks no protection (`spellEffects.js:1835, 1864, 1904`, the planeswalker hits) — Angelic Intervention's grant to a planeswalker (not native) would prevent nothing. (5) The colour shields at the offer and the re-check (`spellEffects.js:702–706`) read an empty list as "can't tell" even for a known colourless source (Veil of Summer refuses a colourless spell at the offer; Thrun's "nongreen" shield never refuses a colourless source at the re-check). (6) The lesser-power comparison against a departed source is still skipped at the re-check (`creatureRestrictions.js:139`), though a targeted ability's record now carries its power. (7) A departed source with no record stays unknown: an LTB trigger's source, a graveyard card's ability (`actionDispatcher.js:1530`, `sourceId: null`). (8) `programQueries.atomTargetIntent` (effects/programQueries.js:581, the "ambiguous" default) still has no `grant-protection` case — Midvast Protector (body-only) and Sejiri Steppe (land-partial) are not credited native, so no false credit; left as briefed.

> ## 🔧 2026-10-21 — FIX (rules faithfulness): a blocked creature assigns ALL its combat damage, and Essence Sliver reads any damage (CR 510.1c — "If exactly one creature is blocking it, it assigns all its combat damage to that creature. If two or more creatures are blocking it, it assigns its combat damage to those creatures divided as its controller chooses among them."; CR 702.19b, 702.2c, 702.15b, 120.8, 603.2c) — the dealt-by entry's found-not-fixed (1) and (2): `combatResolution`'s blocked arm gave a non-trampler's blockers exactly their lethal shares and DROPPED the rest, so a 5/5 lifelinker blocked by a 2/2 gained 2 (Vampiric Link's ruling: "If you put this on a 5/5 and it is blocked by a 1/1, you still gain 5 life.") and every reader of the damage dealt was short — lifelink, the dealt-by payoffs, the damage a surviving or damage-reactive blocker is dealt, the excess-damage ledger; and Essence Sliver (#8499, credited native) — "Whenever a Sliver deals damage, its controller gains that much life." — was the combat-damage-to-a-player event, so a Sliver's damage to a creature or outside combat gained nothing. Now the lethal shares are assigned exactly as before and the remainder goes to ONE blocker — the last in declaration order whose damage would not be fully prevented, else the last — and Essence Sliver is a dealt-by watcher of every player's Sliver · **±0** · snapshot native+land 15,877 unchanged

> · **The assignment** (combatResolution.js, the blocked arm and `combatDealPrevented`): the bundled rules have no damage assignment order and no lethal-first duty without trample (CR 510.1c's own example assigns all 4 to either blocker); that duty is trample's (CR 702.19b). The engine keeps its deterministic division: `shares` gives each live blocker, in declaration order, its lethal share (toughness less marked damage; 1 from deathtouch, CR 702.2c) — the old amounts, so who dies is unchanged — then the remainder: with trample to the player as before, without it to the LAST blocker in declaration order whose damage would not be fully prevented, else the last blocker. `combatDealPrevented` is a pure read of the walls a deal meets: protection from the attacker, a Maze of Ith stamp, a shield counter (the arm's own checks) and consultCombat's full-prevention walls (the creature's own, a Phantom's or a stocked Bloatfly's counter shield, a prevent-and-put wall, an attached "dealt to" wall, the dealer's "dealt by" walls); a partial prevent-next-N shield is not full prevention. **Why that rule:** every blocker already holds its lethal share, so the remainder decides no death, only how much is dealt — the choice that deals it is the one the attacking player would make for lifelink and the "that much" payoffs, and the one that marks a surviving blocker; "last" matches the multi-block division, which puts its remainder on the last attacker. Assignment still ignores prevention (a protected, Maze-stamped or shielded blocker takes its share, dealt as 0); each share is dealt in ONE consultCombat call (assigned un-doubled, doubled as dealt — a shield, a Phantom counter or an Ironscale Hydra counter is spent once per blocker, as before); a blocker assigned nothing is now skipped — before, a zero share still spent its shield counter (CR 120.8 — witnessed). Unchanged: trample (its excess to the player, CR 702.19b, 702.19d), the multi-block division (CR 510.1d — no drop there; it already assigned all), first strike and double strike (each step assigns its whole damage), a blocker that left combat (CR 510.1c: no blockers, no damage; a trampler all to the player).
> · **Every other place that computes blocked combat damage** (searched: app/src, app/scripts; `blockersByAttacker` and `liveBlockers` appear only in combatResolution): the AI predicts no damage to blockers — `opponentAI.combatDuel` (:1743) and `trickDuel` (:1209) read kills (a lone blocker already takes full power there), `damageRow` / `unavoidableDamage` (:3383 / :3440), `connectsAfterBlocks` (:2596), `incomingFaceFrom` (:835) and `crackBackFloor` (:3856) read the damage that reaches the player (a blocked non-trampler reaches none under either rule), `trampleStop` (:3357) is trample-only, and its only lifelink reads (`combatAsDeclared` :2624, `seatDoomedAnyway` :3910) are blockers' — power × strikes, all of it dealt to one attacker; `trapDetector.detectCounterAttackLethal` and `tokenLoopLine.unavoidableDamage` read player damage only; no Academy component previews combat (LearnBoard only abbreviates keywords); the goldfish has no combat model; Ram Through's bite already deals a non-trampler's whole power. They agree with the engine; nothing to align. Readers that inherit the full amount: lifelink, `dealtBySources` → the dealt-by triggers, the dealt-damage (enrage) totals, `creatureDamagePairs` → the damaged-by record and the to-a-creature triggers, `markCombatDamage`'s excess-damage ledger (Rith — a blocker dealt more than its toughness is dealt excess damage, CR 120.4a), `learnSession.previewFeatures` (it runs the engine).
> · **Essence Sliver** (#8499 — its whole bundled text read; its rulings: the life is gained on resolution; a Sliver that stops being a Sliver no longer triggers it; the abilities are cumulative): `detectSubtypeGlobalDamageLifegain` returns the `dealtBy` event, scope `subtypeGlobal`, `itsController`; `checkDealtByTriggers` runs an all-players scan firing only subtypeGlobal descriptors, the dealer as the triggering permanent (scopeMatches checks its subtype) and the dealer's controller as the beneficiary; the dealer's own and its attachments' paths exclude subtypeGlobal, so an Essence Sliver dealing damage fires once. Witnessed: a 3/3 Essence Sliver blocked by a Bears gains 3; a Metallic Sliver's 1 to its blocker gains 1; an opponent's Sliver blocking gains ITS controller 1; two blockers at once are one trigger for 3; a Prey Upon fight gains 3 (the Bears' 2 back gains nothing); an opponent's Sliver in a fight gains the opponent 1. Controls on both trees: an unblocked Sliver gains 3 once; two Essence Slivers each trigger; a non-Sliver's combat or fight damage gains nothing. Synapse and Brood Sliver ("… combat damage to a player") stay on the combat-damage scan. Cost: the scan visits every battlefield permanent per dealing source — 0.15 ms per 10-dealer event on a 40-permanent board against 0.035 ms (micro-benchmark); the A/B ran 500.3 s against 504.8 s.
> · **Tests changed on purpose (pins graduated):** `essenceSliver.test.js` — its five runtime tests fired Essence Sliver through `checkCombatDamageTriggers` (the event this slice moves); they now feed `checkDealtByTriggers` the same source and amount, every assertion kept. `preventDamagePutCounters.test.js` — "'that many' tracks what the engine would ACTUALLY have dealt": two attackers (3 and 5 power) each blocked by the Panther Habit host alone assign 3 + 5 = 8, not the old lethal-capped 3 + 4 = 7 (the test's own "BANKED FINDING" comment named this bug); the companion test's comment about the cap removed. `vigorGroupPreventPutCounters.test.js` — a comment only. Both graduated files fail on this tree in their 9111db80 form (6 tests).
> · **Judgment calls:** (1) **The remainder rule** above — the brief's suggested default, for the reasons given; the deterministic stand-in does not model a controller's reason to keep excess off a damage-reactive blocker (Spitemare, Boros Reckoner) when two or more block (a lone blocker gets everything anyway, CR 510.1c). (2) **The lethal-first order kept** although CR 510.1c no longer requires it without trample: any division is legal, and keeping it leaves every death unchanged. (3) **The zero-share shield fix** rides along — the restructure deals only what is assigned, and keeping the old behaviour would mean coding the bug. (4) **Essence Sliver played, not decredited** — the dealt-by machinery carries it with one scan. (5) **The multi-block division left as it is** — no drop there; it still puts its remainder on the last attacker even when that attacker's damage would be prevented (a legal, smaller choice — below).
> · ⚠️ **Found, not fixed:** (1) **"Combat damage can't be prevented" does not reach protection, Maze of Ith or shield counters** (combatResolution.js:614, :616, :619 and the blocker side :699–:705; `combatDealPrevented` mirrors them): under Frenzied Baloth those still prevent combat damage, where CR 615.12 has every prevention effect prevent nothing; only consultCombat's walls and the fog read `unpreventable`. (2) **The multi-block division's remainder ignores prevention** (combatResolution.js:681 — `gives[gives.length - 1].give += remaining`): a blocker dividing among attackers puts the rest on the last one even if that one is protected from it. (3) **A trampler's lethal check ignores other creatures' damage assigned in the same step** (the `shares` lethal need reads only marked damage; CR 702.19b counts "damage from other creatures that's being assigned during the same combat damage step"): two attackers blocked by one creature, the trampler assigns it more than it must — less tramples over. (4) **A Sliver that has left the battlefield when its damage is dealt does not trigger Essence Sliver** (triggers.js:9181 — `checkDealtByTriggers` skips a source no longer on the battlefield, right for the source's own abilities, a miss for a global watcher reading last-known information): Acidic Sliver's granted "{2}, Sacrifice this permanent: This permanent deals 2 damage to any target." would gain nothing (read, not probed). (5) **An Essence Sliver that stops being a Sliver still triggers on its own damage** (triggers.js:7350 — scope `subtypeGlobal`'s self-inclusion reads the printed card), where its ruling says it no longer does; rare (a type-changing effect on it). (6) A/B game 16's engine-stuck is the base's own (the Squirrel Girl runaway), the same on both trees.

> ## 🔧 2026-10-21 — FIX (soft-lock): a payer is tapped before its sacrifice — the dbltap entry's found-not-fixed (1): a payment plan that spends a self-sacrificing source with no {T} in its cost (Rith's / Crosis's / Dromar's / Treva's / Darigaaz's Attendant's "{1}, Sacrifice this creature: Add …", Verdant Eidolon's "{G}, Sacrifice this creature: Add three mana of any one color.", Wild Cantor's "Sacrifice this creature: Add one mana of any color.", Gold, an Eldrazi Spawn) and names that same permanent as a LATER tap's tap-other payer (Urza, Lord High Artificer's "Tap an untapped artifact you control: Add {U}.", Springleaf Drum, Loam Dryad, Supportive Parents, The Massive Zatcatl, Scene of the Crime and kin) threw "Permanent … not found" in `commitPaymentPlan`, which committed in plan order — the sacrifice first, then a tap of a permanent no longer there; in a game the dispatch error ends it. > · **The fix** — `commitPaymentPlan` passes its non-picking taps through `payersBeforeTheirSacrifice`: walking the plan in order, at a tap that removes its own permanent as it pays (`leavesAsItPays`) it first commits every later tap that taps that permanent (`permanentsItTaps` — its own {T} or a payer), then the sacrifice; nothing else moves, and a plan with no self-sacrifice comes back as the same array. The sacrifice-a-creature taps still commit after all of these. Why the order is always legal — measured on the corpus, not assumed: **no tap-other line carries a mana cost** (a read-only census of every card's parsed mana lines: 36,462 cards, 18 tap-other lines, 0 with an activation cost; a granted mana ability never carries a tap-other cost — only manaModel's own parser emits one), so a moved tap needs no mana and only makes its own sooner; the planner taps each permanent once per payment (the dbltap slice), so an earlier tap collides with no other; and **no line that removes its permanent taps another** (0 of the 18 leave; the 22 no-{T} self-sacrifice lines have no payers), so no two moves can depend on each other. A {T} self-sacrifice (Treasure, Golden Egg) is never another tap's payer in a plan (a double tap the planner refuses).
> · **Probe** (dbltap's 20,000-board harness, seed 7 — its board stream byte-for-byte, extended with a commit-state comparison, an audit of every moved tap and an independent replay of the after commit order; the SAME state read by both trees — base = the untouched c79fb91b archive, after = the final tree): **plain** payable **12,083 on both**, commit throws **2 → 0** (Darigaaz's Attendant then Supportive Parents; Crosis's Attendant then Loam Dryad — dbltap's two boards); **targeted** (1–2 tap-other and 1–2 mana-costed sources per board) payable **16,094 on both**, throws **24 → 0** (the Attendant cycle, Verdant Eidolon and Wild Cantor named later by Urza, Supportive Parents, Scene of the Crime, Loam Dryad, Saruli Caretaker, Jaspera Sentinel, Springleaf Drum, The Massive Zatcatl, Survivors' Encampment, Dragonbroods' Relic or Seton — dbltap's 24); a third mode, **selfsac** (1–2 tap-other sources and 1–2 of the 22 no-{T} self-sacrificing cards, tokens included), payable **17,189 on both**, throws **81 → 0** (the same shape; sacrificed besides those: Gold, Eldrazi Spawn, Basal Sliver, Blood Pet, Blood Vassal, Tinder Wall, Morgue Toad, Coal Golem, Composite Golem, Satyr Hedonist, Reckless Barbarian; naming them besides those: Holdout Settlement, Gene Pollinator). On all 60,000 boards: **plans differ 0** (canAfford's own plans 0), lost 0, gained 0, planPayment and canAfford agree on both trees; 0 `tap-cost-unpaid`, 0 negative pools, 0 other throw kinds; **every board that commits on both trees commits to a byte-identical state (0 differ)**; the after order moved a tap on exactly the 107 boards base threw on (0 elsewhere), and each of the 107 moved taps names payers, carries no activation cost and doesn't leave; the replay finds 0 taps of a tapped or missing permanent in the after order. Affordability moved on no board, so no board needed an illegality proof — every plan the probe met has a legal order.
> · **A/B 80 seeded commander games** (base seed 7, 10 per pod, the 30 profile decks, default AI; base = the untouched c79fb91b archive): **80 / 80 byte-identical** (whole game records), 0 winner changes, user-wins 25 / ai-wins 54 / engine-stuck 1 on both, 0 unpaid-cost events. The one error is the same game on both trees (game 16, turn 31: "runaway battlefield (2572 permanents, ai3)" after four activations of The Unbeatable Squirrel Girl's "{1}{G}{G}{G}: Create X 1/1 green Squirrel creature tokens, where X is the number of Squirrels you control.") — not this crash; no base game errored on it. **The census** (a pure hook on `commitPaymentPlan` in scratch copies of both trees, 80 / 80 play-identical to the clean runs): 12,625 commits per batch, 159 spending a self-sacrifice, 38 with a tap-other payer, **0 in the crash shape on either tree** — the 30 decks never put a no-{T} self-sacrifice and a payer naming it in one plan in these games, so no game changes.
> · **Judgment calls:** (1) **The commit moves the payer, not the sacrifice**: the later tap rises to just before the sacrifice instead of the sacrifice sinking after it — a tap-other line needs no mana, so it can commit anywhere earlier, while a sacrifice moved later could pass a costed source its mana funds (the sinking mutant is caught by the witness whose payer sits two taps later). (2) **No planner change**: the plans were right and canAfford counted them right; only the commit order was wrong, so affordability and plan contents are untouched by construction (probe: 0 / 0). (3) **The order's legality rests on two corpus facts, documented, not enforced** (no tap-other line has a mana cost; no line that removes its permanent taps another) — a census over every card, not a runtime check; found-not-fixed (1). (4) `payersBeforeTheirSacrifice` is exported through `_internals` for the order assertions; the controls read only behavior (the becomes-tapped events, in commit order), so they run on the base too. (5) The probe keeps dbltap's harness byte-for-byte on the board stream, including its targeted mode's `/\bCreature\b/`, which a heredoc wrote as backspace characters (a targeted tap-other or costed creature is never flagged a creature: 10% summoning-sick odds instead of 25%) — kept so the boards are dbltap's; the selfsac mode's test is correct. (6) Base = c79fb91b as briefed.

> · **The dealt-by event** (triggers.js `classifyCondition`:1003, `checkDealtByTriggers`:9170): "Whenever <this creature | its own name, exactly> deals [combat] damage" → `dealtBy`, scope `self`; "Whenever <equipped | enchanted> creature deals [combat] damage" → scope `equippedCreature` (the watcher is the attachment, the dealer its host); `combatOnly` for "combat damage", carried on the descriptor whitelist. Both funnels call `checkDealtByTriggers` with one `{ sourceId, amount }` per source per damage event — the amount what it DEALT after protection, replacement and prevention (CR 120.8: a fully prevented source has no entry) — and it fires, through `triggersForEvent` like any other event, the dealer's own descriptors (printed; granted by an attached Equipment's or Aura's quoted line; granted by a group or until-end-of-turn grant) and each attachment's, `combatOnly` only from the combat damage step, ctx.combatDamageAmount / ctx.dealtDamageAmount = the total. Damage to several objects at once is one event (CR 603.2c, 510.2 — the Drinker of Sorrow, Angel of Deliverance, Vessel of the All-Consuming and Captain Rex Nebula rulings), and a source dealt lethal damage in the same event still triggers (fired before the lethal pass — the Angel of Deliverance and Living Lore rulings); a source already gone has no ability to trigger (not a look-back, CR 603.10). On a self dealt-by trigger "untap it" reads "untap this creature" (Quintessential Katana's grant). `dealtByLinkOf` is gone; triggerRouting.js's two dealt-by refusals (`triggerRoutesNatively`, `isModeledGroupTriggeredBody`) are lifted — a dealt-by body routes when its effect does, like any other.

"To an opponent" carries `toOpponent`, checked in `triggersForEvent` against the ability's controller: the Aura's for its own trigger (Curiosity: "you won't draw a card when that creature deals damage to you"), the creature's for a granted one (the Snake Umbra and Helm of the Ghastlord rulings) — combat included, so an Aura on an opponent's attacker no longer fires off damage to its own controller. "… deals [combat] damage to a creature" with the destroy / exile / tap-lock "that creature" payoffs reads its subject through one shape: self → `selfDealerToCreature`, equipped / enchanted → `attachedDealerToCreature` (the dealer must be the watcher's host; the Sword of Kaldra ruling: "You exile the creature that gets damaged."), "deals damage" (no "combat") → `anyDamage`, which the non-combat funnel fires through `checkCombatDamageToCreatureTriggers(…, { isCombat: false })` — outside combat it scans only the dealer and its attachments and fires only `anyDamage` descriptors (Toxin Sliver's and Voracious Cobra's combat wording stay combat-only). The self "deals damage to a player" subject is exact now: "this creature", the card's name, a legend's short name.

A cost that taps a permanent needs it untapped (CR 107.5 — "A permanent that's already tapped can't be tapped again to pay the cost"; CR 118.3; CR 701.26a — "Only untapped permanents can be tapped"). The turn-order paths and the goad fix are not reached by these 80 games; the witnesses carry them. > · **The gaps** (b5650658): (1) Reflector Mage's name lock (`gameState.expireNameCastLocks`) ended only at its setter's own untap step, so it never ended once the setter had left. (2) A stored damage replacement whose controller left stopped applying at once (`damageReplacements.collectDamageReplacements` skipped it) and was dropped as the next turn began (`expireDamageReplacementEffects`, its comment citing CR 800.4a where 800.4m governs). (3) The goad family's hand-over (`playerLeavesGame.handOverUntilNextTurnEffects`) passed the leaver's effects to the next seat, to end as any turn of that seat's began: an extra turn of theirs taken before the leaver's would-be turn ended them early, and an extra turn already queued for the leaver — their real next turn — was missed, keeping them a round too long. The active player's departure began the next seat's turn at once (`removePlayerFromGame`), whatever extra turns were queued, keeping the leaver's `extraTurnOf` and `rotationAnchor`: another player's queued extra turn came a turn late, the next seat could take two turns in a row, and a departed rotation anchor sent the rotation on from the active player. (4) A resolved goad whose source is a permanent named that permanent's current controller as the goader (`layers.liveGoadedGrants`); CR 701.15b names the controller of the spell or ability (Jeering Homunculus's ruling: "the controller of the spell or ability that goaded it").
> · **The fix** — one moment for all three stores. `playerLeavesGame` writes the seat record `state.seatOrder` as the first player leaves (every seat in turn order, the departed included). `gameEngine.beginNextTurn` (factored out of `advanceStep`'s end of turn) names in the new turn's `turnsNotBegun` every departed player whose turn the transition reaches and does not begin (CR 800.4k): an extra turn queued for them, popped untaken, and a departed seat the rotation passes on its way from the anchor to the next seat still in the game. `layers.untilNextTurnEndsNow` is the one reading the three sweeps share (the stored continuous effects, the name locks, the damage replacements): a seated owner's effect ends as their first turn after the stamp turn begins, as before; a departed owner's ends when the untap step finds them in `turnsNotBegun`, and the step spends the list; a departed owner the seat record does not know (a state saved before it) ends as the next turn begins. The hand-over is gone, and a departed controller's damage replacement keeps applying until its end. The active player's departure runs `beginNextTurn` after the truncated turn's cleanup — a queued extra turn first, else the rotation from the anchor; a departed anchor stays the anchor, read in the seat record. A resolved goad (a `{kind: "resolution"}` source) names the controller `applyGoad` recorded; a static goad (an Aura's or Equipment's) still names the permanent's controller, read live. ENGINE-SCAFFOLD §4.6: the durations table, "A player who leaves the game", "The turn order around a departure", "The goader".
> · **Judgment calls:** (1) **The hand-over is replaced, not extended.** The brief said to give the name lock and the damage replacement the same hand-over; the hand-over cannot follow extra turns (gap 3) — it re-stamps an effect to the next seat, so that seat's extra turn ends it and the leaver's own queued extra turn is invisible to it. Naming the moment at the turn transition gives the CR 800.4m moment in every case the witness walks, and one reading serves all three stores. (2) **The active player's departure goes through the ordinary end-of-turn transition**, so the turn order around a departure follows the CR 500.7 queue and the rotation anchor (0a65c51c) like any end of turn; CR 800.4j's turn without an active player stays the documented simplification. (3) **Gap 4 confirmed and fixed** on real cards (Jeering Homunculus goads, Act of Treason takes it); the static-goad control (Coercive Impetus) passes on both trees. (4) **Taunt from the Rampart not taken**: its second sentence does not parse ("Until your next turn, those creatures can't block." → low confidence, no atom) and no group can't-block reader exists even for the "this turn" form, so it is a new reader, not a small extension. (5) Lightning's Stagger is staged in its witness: its effect sentence through the real parser and resolver (the combat-damage trigger's resolution), not Lightning's combat. (6) Citation hygiene: the name lock's comments cited CR 611.2b ("for as long as") for "until your next turn" — now 611.2a (gameState.js, gameEngine.js, effects/atoms/zones.js).
> · ⚠️ **Found, not fixed:** (1) Taunt from the Rampart's "Until your next turn, those creatures can't block." stays unread (above). (2) CR 800.4j: the active leaver's turn ends at once instead of continuing without an active player (playerLeavesGame.js:264, the existing bounded simplification), so the other seats lose that turn's remaining priority windows and end-step triggers.
> · Witness: `leaverWouldBeTurn.test.js` (19); `untilYourNextTurn.test.js` (14 — a comment and a test name edited).

(9) **No sacrifice for value in response** (a doomed creature fed to Evolutionary Leap, Blasting Station, Altar of Dementia) — each outlet's effect needs its own target reading; left for a picker of its own.

> · **The gap** (0a65c51c): `layers.expireContinuousEffects` swept `untilOwnersNextTurn` only at a cleanup — "any cleanup of a turn AFTER the stamp turn where the OWNER is the active player" (layers.js:3215, the documented one-step approximation of "as your next turn begins", written for Savage Order when no turn-begin hook existed). Every user rode it: goad (`applyGoad` — the single, bound-pronoun and mass forms, Disrupt Decorum's included), detain (`applyDetain`), Kardur's group rule (`applyOpponentsAttackOthers`), Savage Order's fetched grant (runProgram). On the owner's next turn a detained creature could not block the owner's attackers and its activated abilities stayed locked (the over-restriction play-weighted #15 measured), the goad's two requirements and Kardur's stayed on the board, and the Dinosaur stayed indestructible. A player who left the game was never the active player again, so their effects never ended — CR 800.4m's "nor last indefinitely".
> · **The fix** — the sweep takes `atTurnBegin: { playerId, turn }`, and `gameEngine.runStepActions`' untap step calls it first, before the Teferi shield, the name locks and the stored damage replacements end and before anything phases in or untaps: an `untilOwnersNextTurn` effect ends when its owner's first turn after the stamp turn begins (an extra turn of theirs counts; the stamp turn never does), and no cleanup ends it. **A player who leaves** (`playerLeavesGame.handOverUntilNextTurnEffects`, CR 800.4m — "will last until that turn would have begun. They neither expire immediately nor last indefinitely."; Azorius Arrester's and Martial Law's own rulings repeat it): their effects pass to the next seat still in the game — the turn order passes the leaver's seat just before that seat's next turn (CR 800.4k: their turn doesn't begin, that seat's does) — stamped with the current turn, or the next one when the leaver was the active player (their successor's turn begins at once, and it is not the turn the leaver would have taken). An effect with a departed owner and no hand-over (a state saved before this) ends as the next turn begins. ENGINE-SCAFFOLD §4.6 "Durations — where each one ends".
> · **The durations** (wording → where it ends, before → after): "until end of turn" / "this turn" (`endOfTurn`) → that turn's cleanup, unchanged · "until your next turn" — goad, detain, Kardur's rule, Savage Order's grant (`untilOwnersNextTurn`) → **the cleanup of the owner's next turn → as the owner's next turn begins** · the same with its owner gone → **never → as the turn the leaver would have taken would have begun** (a fallback: the next turn's beginning) · "until your next turn" — Teferi's Protection / Perch Protection / The One Ring / The Stasis Coffin (the player shield) and phasing → the owner's untap step, unchanged · Reflector Mage's name lock, Lightning, Army of One's damage replacement → the owner's untap step, unchanged · "until the end of your next turn" — Light Up the Stage, Reckless Impulse, Wrenn's Resolve and the extended impulse family (`_impulseExtended`) → the cleanup of the owner's next turn, unchanged. The census of every bundled card printing "until your next turn" or "until the end of your next turn" (reminder text included): 309, 59 native — goad 13, detain 7, Kardur, Savage Order, the shield 4, Reflector Mage, Lightning, phasing 3 (reminder text only), the impulse "until the end of your next turn" family 26, Verdant Kraken and its Forest Tentacle 2 (summoning-sickness reminder text, no duration).
> · **Tests changed on purpose (they pinned the cleanup expiry):** `detain.test.js`, `goadAtom.test.js`, `kardurDoomscourge.test.js`, `savageOrder.test.js` — each read the effect gone after the cleanup of the owner's next turn; each now reads it alive through the other players' turns (their beginnings and cleanups) and gone as the owner's next turn begins. All four fail on the untouched base in their new form.
> · **Judgment calls:** (1) **The leaver's effects follow CR 800.4m, not "end at once".** The brief said a leaver's "until your next turn" effects end and to keep the existing behaviour; 800.4m (and the detain cards' own rulings) say they last until the leaver's turn would have begun, neither ending at once nor lasting for good, and `untilOwnersNextTurn` had no leaver behaviour to keep (it never ended). The hand-over gives the exact moment in all three leave cases the witness walks (in the turn of the seat before theirs, in another seat's turn, in their own turn). The stored damage replacements keep their leaver behaviour, as asked (found-not-fixed 2). (2) **The sweep runs in the untap step's actions**, where the other "until your next turn" expiries already run — the turn has begun, nothing has untapped or phased in, and no player receives priority in the untap step (CR 502.4), so nothing can see the moment between the turn beginning and the sweep. (3) **An extra turn of the owner's ends it** — it is a turn of theirs (CR 500.7); the hand-over does not follow extra turns (found-not-fixed 3).
> · ⚠️ **Found, not fixed:** (1) **Reflector Mage's name lock never ends when its controller leaves** (gameState.js:2335 — `expireNameCastLocks` drops only the active player's locks), where CR 800.4m ends it as the turn they would have taken would have begun; the Brago Blink deck carries it. (2) **A stored damage replacement whose controller left ends as the next turn begins** (gameState.js:2348) — exact only when they left in the turn of the seat before theirs (the control in the witness), early otherwise; its comment cites CR 800.4a ("an early end rather than an outliving one") where 800.4m governs. Both would take the same hand-over. (3) The hand-over does not follow extra turns (playerLeavesGame.js:150): a successor's extra turn taken before the leaver's would-be turn ends the effect early. (4) Taunt from the Rampart's "Until your next turn, those creatures can't block." (noted unread in play-weighted #15) now has the duration it needs. > · **The fix** — `incomingFaceDamage` / `incomingFaceFrom` (new; `unblockedIncomingFace` replaced): each attacker at the seat's face with its declared blockers — unblocked, its power, twice for a double striker before the first-strike damage step (`strikesLeft`); blocked, nothing, unless it tramples (what its best blocker alone doesn't stop — `trampleStop` with the damage already marked on the blocker taken off its lethal damage, CR 702.19b; more blockers never stop less; every blocker gone, all of it) or assigns as though unblocked (all of it but what a first striker that kills it first keeps off). The fog timing reads it; the chump stage reads it when a face attacker has trample or double strike (or assigns as though unblocked) — a chump that alone ends the lethal pressure first (the smallest such blocker, then the most it saves), else the smallest spare blocker where it saves the most, until the damage is below the seat's life; without such an attacker the old stage runs byte-identically. `crackBackFloor` / `seatDoomedAnyway` (new): the board the attack finds (`gameEngine.finishCleanupActions`, then the opponent's `untapAll`); attackers that nothing may keep home or send elsewhere, each its damage amount, twice with double strike; each blocker slot keeps off at most the most it stops of one attacker it may block, and all of them never more than the blockable attackers deal; doomed when one opponent's floor reaches the seat's life plus its blockers' possible lifelink; no judgment under an attack tax on the seat, an attack cap, a damage replacement, the seat's "until your next turn" protection or a damage redirect, or a permanent of the seat's that untaps on other turns or could become a creature. Read lazily, the first time the guard would hold. `trampleStop` / `gangKill`: an indestructible attacker is killed by no blocker first (CR 702.12b). Policy keys `defendDamage: "v1"` (the old reading and stage) and `doomedHold: "v1"` (the old hold); test handles `__incomingFaceDamageForTests`, `__crackBackFloorForTests`. (3) **The new chump stage only where it reads differently** — a face attacker with trample or double strike, or one that assigns as though unblocked; elsewhere the old stage runs unchanged, so plain boards keep their exact picks. (4) **The floor's no-judgment gates** are generous on purpose — each is a reading the floor would need and doesn't have; only the rare boards they cover keep the old hold. (5) **Reused, not rebuilt:** both new readings take each blocker's stop from `trampleStop` (the floor through `damageRow`, its gang kill included); only the sum is new — the defender's blocks are declared, so it reads them attacker by attacker, and the floor needs a sum that never over-credits a blocker, which `unavoidableDamage`'s slot budget does (one strong blocker credited against every trampler; its menace greedy is no bound either). > · **The changed game, first divergence:** game 39 (Wolverine / Jurassic Ramp / Earth Bent / Believe it!), turn 41, ai2's precombat main: base cast **Preposterous Proportions** (+10/+10 to its team) into ai1 at 39 behind six untapped creatures; replayed alone to that decision, the old count read 11 attackers pumped = 65 through the best block, but the payment plan taps five of those attackers — animated Forests 3/3, 2/2, 5/5, 15/15, 17/17 (42 power) — and on the board the cast actually leaves, six pumped attackers against six blockers read **0** through. The after tree holds the card: the premise (lethal) was false, so holding is the better choice by the pump's own rule. What followed (not graded): base attacked with six, four were blocked, 26 through and four creatures died; after attacked with three (the two big Forests among them), one was blocked, 34 through, the card kept; ai2 won both (turn 43 / 45).
> · **The census** (an observing pilot on every seat — 80 / 80 play-identical to the clean run on each tree): AI decisions in their own precombat main with a pump cast offered 273 / 282 (the census predicate also took the X −X/−X wipes, Toxic Deluge and Nuclear Fallout; the +N pumps are these): precombat +N pump casts **2 → 1** — base Preposterous Proportions (game 39, its payment tapping five would-be attackers, 42 power) and Tyvar's Stand at X=10 (game 69, tapping none); after the same Tyvar's Stand only. Blink activations offered **0 / 0**, taken 0 / 0: none of the five cards is in the 30 profile decks, so the blink arm's evidence is its witnesses.
> · **The gaps** (8cc44fa6): `opponentAI.teamPumpFlipsLethal` (pickCastAction's and pickSpreeCast's team pump) and `singlePumpFlipsLethal` (pickTargetedSpell's tier-4 lethal pump, an X pump through pickXCast) read `wouldBeAttackerIds` on the board before the cast and the old rows (power once, a blocked attacker dealing nothing); `evasionConnects` read its attacker the same way. `pickTargetedActivation` skipped every blink; `pickSafeAbilityActivation` refuses targeted activations.
> · **The fix** — `pumpFlipsLethal(state, ai, action, pumpOf, pol)`: without the pump, the board as it is (already lethal → hold); with it, `boardAfterPumpCost` → `afterOwnCosts` (the ward read's preview: `offeredPaymentPlan` → `commitPaymentPlan`, the cost's other permanents gone), its would-be attackers, `pumpedSwingRows` (`damageRow` at the pumped power and toughness — trample stops recomputed), `swingIsLethalV2`; a pump that reaches no attacker there (the Druid its own payment taps) is no flip. Each X and each target is its own cast, so the X kept is one whose payment leaves the swing lethal; pickCastAction's team pump keeps only the cost variants that do. `evasionConnects` reads its attacker on the same board. Activation blink arm (before the damage arm): own nontoken creature, an owner-return only of its own card, a "returns tapped" (Displacer) only on a creature tapped already, not one back from exile this turn (`enteredFromZone` "exile" + `enteredOnTurn`), precombat only a non-attacker from a source whose tap costs no attacker, a creature source's tap held as `shotCostsBlocker`, then `blinkRebuyWorth` (extracted from the spell arm — +1/+1 counter or own attachment lost → no; `entersTriggerWorthRebuy` or an opponent's Aura shed → yes); tier 2 by `permanentValue`. Policy keys `pumpCost` (the old pre-cost count) and `blink` (the old skip) join POLICY_KEYS; `combatDamage: "v1"` now also keeps the pump on the old rows. ENGINE-SCAFFOLD §4.8 ("The precombat pump reads the swing its own cast leaves"; the targeted-activations paragraph's BLINK).
> · **Judgment calls:** (1) **The pump readers moved onto `damageRow` too** — the damage slice held them on the old rows only because of this bug; a trample grant riding on the pump (Overrun) is still not added (the safe underestimate). (2) **"Without" on the board as it is, "with" on the board after the cost**: not casting pays nothing; the after board's attackers are a subset of the board's, so the lethal side only drops. (3) **The AI picks X and targets, never sources**: which permanents pay is the planner's (battlefield order — found-not-fixed (1)); a pump the planner can only pay by tapping the needed attackers is held. (4) A "no payment plan → no swing" branch was written, survived its mutant (no witness board reaches it — an offered cast's payment is planned by the offer's own sources) and was removed. (5) **Blink worth = the spell arm's reading**, not `gameEngine.pickFlickerCandidate` (+3 for any enters trigger, a harmful one included); extracting `blinkRebuyWorth` keeps the spell arm's decisions (its tests unchanged and green; the A/B's one divergence is the pump). (6) **Once per creature per turn** is the termination bound a repeatable blink needs (Emiel the Blessed on Brood Monitor pays each {3} with the three Scions the last blink made — witnessed looping without it); it gives up a second same-turn re-buy of the same creature. (7) Eldrazi Displacer only on a creature already tapped — an untapped one would come back tapped and miss its blocks; precombat only a creature that would not attack (it returns summoning-sick, CR 302.6).
> · ⚠️ **Found, not fixed:** (1) **The payment planner pays in battlefield order** (legalChoices.offeredPaymentPlan → manaModel.planPayment): game 39's plan tapped the five animated Forests (the oldest lands) with nine plain lands untapped (Chocobo Camp and eight Forests) — paid with those, the swing read 65 into 39; the probe boards showed the same with a Paradise Druid listed before the Forests. Sparing would-be attackers precombat is a planner change, outside the AI's choice. (2) `entersTriggerWorthRebuy` (opponentAI.js:1225) counts a targeted harm aimed at an opponent without checking a legal target exists — Ravenous Chupacabra with no opposing creature is re-bought for nothing (spell and activation arms). (3) It also refuses every re-buy under `LIFE_PRUDENCE_FLOOR` even when the trigger costs no life (opponentAI.js:1244, `life - loss` with loss 0). (4) `REBUY_ENEMY_OPS` (opponentAI.js:1217) has no bounce, so Man-o'-War's re-buy is not read. (5) `pickTargetedActivation`'s precombat grants (haste, "can't be blocked") still read attackers before the activation's mana payment (opponentAI.js:2249) — unwitnessed. (6) No save lane for an activated blink: the picker runs with the stack empty; once activations are offered at instant speed (day/instab), Eldrazi Displacer and Emiel could save a creature from removal as the spell arm does (`stackHarmsToSeat`). (7) Eldrazi Displacer at an opponent's creature (a blocker tapped down precombat, a token exiled for good) is not taken. (8) The Spree team-pump call site (`pickSpreeCast`) has no witness of its own (the same reader).
> · Witnesses: `aiPumpCostAttackers.test.js` (18), `aiActivatedBlink.test.js` (18).
