> · **The gap** (6a4f3ad0): `actionsActivateAbility` returned nothing outside `mainWindow || combatWindow || stackWindow` (legalChoices.js:2630) and admitted only combat-role abilities in the combat window and stack copiers in the stack window; `actionsCrewVehicle` and `actionsCycleFromHand` required the active player in a main step; `actionsDiscardAbilityFromHand` the own main phase or a combat step for a combat-role target. The parser stripped "Activate only during your turn." with no flag (abilities.js `stripEnforcedTimingRider`), safe only while the offer's window was the own main phase; Grand Abolisher's "or activate abilities of artifacts, creatures, or enchantments" was "already enforced" by the same window (the comment in `legalActionsForPlayer`).
> · **The fix** — every lane opens on priority (`state.priorityHolder === playerId`); `activationTimingAllows` (legalChoices.js:2626) reads every timing flag in one place: `sorceryOnly` ("Activate only as a sorcery", level up, a Class level, Outlast — `canCastSorcerySpeed`), `isEquipAbility` without `anyTimeAttach` (Equip and its quality variants, Reconfigure — sorcery timing; the equip branch's old stack-only check folded in), `yourTurnOnly` (new — `abilities.abilityIsYourTurnOnly` over the same literal the strip removes), `preCombatOnly` (own turn, beginning phase or precombat main — the upkeep and draw step are new; beginning of combat left out), `combatStepOnly`. `anyTimeAttach` on the printed attaches with no timing instruction ("{cost}: Attach this Equipment to target creature you control" — the Cranial Plating cycle; "{cost}: Attach this Aura to target creature" — Detainment Spell, Stasis Cell). Transmute from hand reads `canCastSorcerySpeed` (it read the empty-stack half and leaned on the window). Grand Abolisher / Myrel: `opponentsCantActAgainst` returns `cantActivate` from the descriptor's `includeActivated`; during the lock's turn the locked player is offered no battlefield activation, crew, cycling or discard ability. The AI: `opponentAI.inDefaultAIActivationWindow` filters at the top of `pickAction` to the windows the pickers were measured in (own main; combat-role in the ④-AE steps; stack copiers while its own ability waits; Equip and the attaches in its own main with an empty stack; crew and cycling in its own main; a combat-role discard ability in a combat step). Unchanged: mana abilities, loyalty abilities, the graveyard lanes, the hand self-put lane, the pending decisions, the attack requirement and the block declaration (CR 509.1). ENGINE-SCAFFOLD §4.8 "Activation timing".
> · **The restriction readers** (census of every modelled non-mana activated ability — 4,844 over 34,620 cards — grouped by the activation-instruction sentences on its printed line): no instruction 3,804 (open whenever priority) · Equip / its quality variants 595, Reconfigure 20 → sorcery timing · printed attach 2 (+ the Plating cycle inside the 595) → `anyTimeAttach`, any time · "Activate only as a sorcery." 170 (+ 2 with a condition, 1 Exhaust) → `sorceryOnly` · level up 17 → `sorceryOnly` · "Activate only if <cond>." 74 → `condition`, evaluated live (every turn-scoped ledger it reads resets for all seats at each untap — creatures died, spells cast, life lost, tokens created, attacked) · "Activate only once each turn." 49 / "no more than twice" 5 / "three times" 2 → `activationLimit` (turn-stamped ledger) · "Activate only once." 6 / "this ability only once" 1 / Power-up and Exhaust 42 → game-scoped limit · "Activate only during your turn, before attackers are declared." 21 → `preCombatOnly` · "Activate only during your turn." 21 (one an Exhaust) → `yourTurnOnly` (NEW) · "Activate only during the end of combat step." 1 → `combatStepOnly` · Boast 11 → once each turn + the permanent attacked this turn (cleared for all seats at untap, so on an opponent's turn it is false). From hand: discard-this-card 70 (any time) + transmute 14 (`sorceryOnly`); Ghost-Lit Stalker's channel keeps "Activate only as a sorcery." in its effect text, which parses LOW, so it is never offered (parked, as before). Graveyard: GY-2 22 `sorceryOnly` / 35 open, GY-1 40 — unchanged. A rider no reader knows stays in the effect text and parks the ability; the scan of every modelled line for a timing word outside these forms found none.
> · **Tests changed on purpose (they encoded the old timing):** `attackingCreatureTarget.test.js` "the window is for combat-role abilities ONLY" — a plain pump is offered in the declare blockers step now; `bloodrush.test.js` "keeps the main phase only: Trumpeting Carnosaur" — offered in combat and on the opponent's turn now; `outletFinishLine.test.js` "UNDER-OFFER (documented)" — the outlet is offered on the opponent's turn now, and the AI still passes (its windows); `sorcerySpeedActivation.test.js` "but NOT in combat" — the plain ability is offered in combat now, which makes that file's own-combat case evidence of the sorcery rider; `activatedAbilities.test.js` "does NOT surface an ability outside the player's main phase" — surfaces in the upkeep now; `necropotence.test.js` end to end — with the discard triggers on the stack in the cleanup window the beginner is asked (Necropotence's own "Pay 1 life" is offered), so the walk passes each ask, its assertions unchanged. `activateDuringYourTurn.test.js` "NOT offered on the opponent's turn" made load-bearing: the AI held priority there, so it passed on priority alone; the user holds it now.
> · **Judgment calls:** (1) **The AI's timing is unchanged** — no new AI window. Each picker was written and measured for the windows above (pickFetchCrack would crack in the upkeep, the zero-cost crew would tap blockers on the opponent's turn, the generic picker would draw with Archivist at every window); a new window is a new picker with its own witnesses and A/B. (2) **Grand Abolisher is enforced wider than printed** — a land's ability and the from-hand abilities are legal under it, but the payment planner can't keep their mana away from the mana abilities of artifacts and creatures the lock forbids, so they are withheld (an under-offer); the hand self-put lane keeps its pre-existing window. (3) **"Before attackers are declared"** opens in the beginning phase and the precombat main only — the beginning of combat step is left out (an additional combat phase has one after attackers were declared; Capricious Sorcerer's ruling names the first combat), and the bare form's opponent's-turn window is not offered. (4) **The printed attaches** open at instant speed (Cranial Plating's and Detainment Spell's rulings say so); Equip and Reconfigure keep sorcery timing. (5) **The Academy** — Beginner asks at every window where a non-mana activation is offered (the same rule it already applies to castable instants); Intermediate is unchanged.
> · ⚠️ **Found, not fixed:** (1) Mother of Runes / Giver of Runes choose their colour by `choicePolicy.autoPickProtectionColor` (choicePolicy.js:216) — the most common colour among the opponents' nonland permanents, not the spell on the stack — and the person cannot choose it: in response to a Lightning Bolt from an opponent with no red permanent the protection is the wrong colour. Much more reachable now. (2) Intermediate difficulty auto-passes whenever no cast, attack or block is offered (decisionGate.js:205), so an Intermediate player is never asked about an activation, main phase included. (3) City of Solitude ("Players can cast spells and activate abilities only during their own turns") and Yuriko, Blade of the Mighty ("During combat, players can't … activate abilities that aren't mana abilities") are body-only and unenforced; the old window happened to honour part of their activation half. (4) The hand self-put lane under Grand Abolisher may be paid with mana abilities the lock forbids (legalChoices.js:4925, pre-existing). (5) The graveyard lanes sit inside the cast lock's block (legalChoices.js:4868 — Rule of Law, Voice of Victory and split second withhold them; split second rightly, the others not) and GY-1 has no priority check (legalChoices.js:3719). (6) AI windows now possible, each a picker of its own with an A/B: a pump after blocks that wins a combat, a sacrifice or Mother of Runes in response to removal, the E7.2 outlet finish at any window (outletFinishLine was written for it), crew to block, end-of-turn draws. (7) The AI's combat-role picker has no first-strike damage step in its window (opponentAI.js:2008).

Copies: `atoms/stack.withWardOwed` — the redirect path's recorder, now shared — stamps `wardOwed` on every copy put onto the stack with targets (instant/sorcery copy re-aimed or kept, each storm copy, the self-copy, a copied activated or triggered ability); `gameEngine.raiseWardOwed` asks it before anyone receives priority, as for a redirect. > · **Judgment calls:** (1) **Dropped, not down-ranked**: an action a ward will counter does nothing (CR 701.6a — it is removed from the stack), so it is removed from the AI's choice before the choosers rank; a ward the AI can pay stays a choice and the chooser's own value order decides (the best target is still taken and paid for — no "prefer the cheaper target" rule was added). (2) **"Beneficial regardless"**: a countered spell or ability has no effect, and nothing in the AI values its cast triggers (prowess, storm count, magecraft), so no doomed action is kept for its own sake; an empty choice falls back to the unfiltered actions so a window with no pass is never left empty (none arose). (3) **After its own costs**: the read pays the action's mana by the dispatcher's own plan first — the reason four Swamps hold Murder at a Lightbringer; a life payment beside the mana (an alternative, an additional cost, a target's life tax) is not taken off — the AI pays an alternative cost's life only at LIFE_PRUDENCE_FLOOR or more, above every printed life ward but a power-sized one — so a missed one reads as paid, the old aim. (4) **A copy keeping its target raises the ward too**: the copy is a new spell or ability put onto the stack with that target (CR 707.10, 707.10c), not only a re-aimed one (the brief named new targets; the rule doesn't distinguish). (5) The copy's ward is asked like a redirect's — recorded on the copy, asked by the driver once no choice is pending, priority returned to its holder (CR 117.5). (6) Diffusion Sliver is read by the AI (the dispatcher asks it) but a copy records ward only (as the redirect path does; Diffusion's own gaps unchanged).

Crack-back calls with an opposing trampler or double striker: held 42 / passed 97 → 14 / 83; on the after tree's states the new reading holds where the old passed in 8 calls (all game 10, turn 25), the reverse 0. > · **The gap** (opponentAI.unavoidableDamage, 5f0936b0): the defender spent its blocker count chumping the biggest blockable attackers, each blocked attacker dealing nothing and each attacker dealing its power once; `planWalkerAttacks` admitted an attacker only when no blocker of the walker's controller killed it "for nothing" (`blockKillsForNothing`, its deathtouch clause included), at no charge.
> · **The fix** — `damageRow` (new) reads each attacker: power, block size, eligible blockers, `strikes`, and for a trampler `stops` (`trampleStop`, new: what each eligible blocker alone keeps off the player — lethal damage first, 1 from deathtouch; a first striker that kills it first stops all; a double striker's regular step tramples past a blocker its first step killed, and a survivor — toughness above the power, or indestructible — needs the rest of its lethal damage again, at least 1, as combatResolution assigns it) and `gangKill` (first strikers that kill it only together). `unavoidableDamage` keeps the slot budget and reads each block as a piece: a non-trampler all its damage for its block size, a trampler what its best blockers stop, then one slot per further blocker (a gang), taken biggest first — with block size 1 the greedy is the best over the pieces, and a gang never stops more than its members alone, summed, except a first-strike gang kill, which reads as fully stopped. The crack-back (`over`, new) gives each trampler its own blocker — the strongest free, biggest trampler first — and no gang. Rows without trample or double strike read byte-identically as before (200 random boards pinned). Callers: the racer's lethal call and group damage, `faceSwingIsLethal` and `cheapestReach` (a trampler's excess reaches a planeswalker, CR 702.19b), `crackBackReader`. `planWalkerAttacks`: no gate; the cost is the face damage given up (power, twice for double strike) plus the marginal of `tradeLossPrefixes` over the walker controller's blocker slots for the attackers the plan newly sends at that controller (those already attacking it — declared, the racer's face attackers when it is the focused player, those sent at its other walkers — face its blocks wherever they attack); `cheapestReach` takes the cost as a function; a land creature keeps the old gate (its value reads 0). Policy keys `combatDamage: "v1"` (the old reading) and `walkerTrade: "v1"` (the old gate at no charge); test handle `__combatDamageForTests`. ENGINE-SCAFFOLD §4.8 describes both.
> · **Judgment calls:** (1) The first-strike gang kill: the first engine-pinned random run found Knuckles the Echidna into three Halberdiers read 1 where the engine deals 0 — two Halberdiers kill it in the first-strike step though neither alone does; such a trampler now reads as one slot stops all of it (valid, loose only on that board shape). (2) The crack-back side was first "each trampler's weakest eligible blocker"; replaced by a feasible distinct assignment (strongest free blocker, biggest trampler first) — still never below a real block's damage, half the slack on the probe (1,461 → 707 over 1,233 boards; seed 777). (3) The pump readers (`teamPumpFlipsLethal`, `singlePumpFlipsLethal`) were moved onto `damageRow` in the first A/B run and moved back: game 61 then cast Tyvar's Stand at X=7 on Thrun because its trample made the swing look lethal — counting Birds of Paradise and Fanatic of Rhonas as attackers though paying X taps them — so Thrun swung alone for 9 at a user on 10. Their reading is unchanged from 5f0936b0; found-not-fixed (2). (4) Walker attackers already attacking the walker's controller are charged no trade loss for moving to its walker (the same blockers face them either way); attackers moved from another player are charged in full, the risk they leave behind not credited — conservative. (5) Damage already marked on a blocker is not subtracted from its lethal damage (the larger figure: the safe side of a lethal call).
> · ⚠️ **Found, not fixed:** (1) The crack-back guard has no baseline (opponentAI.js:3186, `outnumberingAttackers`): it holds a group even when the crack-back is lethal with the group home (A/B game 10); deciding "dead whatever it holds" needs a valid lower bound on the crack-back — the lethal side's slot budget credits one strong blocker against every trampler, so it can't; a per-blocker bound (each blocker stops at most its best stop, counted once) would. (2) The pump readers count as attackers the creatures their pump's own cost taps (`wouldBeAttackerIds` read by `teamPumpFlipsLethal` / `singlePumpFlipsLethal`, opponentAI.js:750, :768, :1134) — the cast's payment plan (legalChoices.offeredPaymentPlan, unexported) would say which; until then they keep the old damage reading. (3) The AI as defender still ignores both keywords: `pickBlockers`' chump-under-lethal sum and the fog timing (`unblockedIncomingFace`, opponentAI.js:734) add each unblocked attacker's power once and count a chump-blocked trampler as stopped. (4) `boardEval.permanentValue` reads 0 for an animated artifact as for an animated land (the printed-type creature bonus, boardEval.js:65): the walker policy charged nothing for risking two Treasure creatures (game 74). (5) Protection, prevention, damage doublers and damage already marked are not read; a "≥N" block size is still spent greedily (not exact, as before).

> · **The gap** (gameEngine.orderTriggersAPNAP, 5f0936b0:1441): first in, first out within each controller, for every seat — the stale doc above it still called the person's order "an Arbiter case". The trigger-target slice (660c7639) asked a person's targets in that fixed order.
> · **The fix** — the batch is placed as before, and the person's part of it waits for its order. At a live flush, after the batch's target events (becomes-the-target, crime, Kira, ward), `markTriggerOrder` stamps the abilities a `state.humanSeats` seat put on the stack in that batch (flushTriggers' `asking`, collected as `personAbilities`) with `awaitingOrder: { batch, abilityText }` when two or more are still there and they are not all identical copies. The session driver raises the question BEFORE the trigger-target raise (`raiseTriggerOrderChoice` → `setPendingTriggerOrderChoice`, the new `trigger-order` kind) — unless an ability of an earlier batch still waits for its targets (it went on the stack first). `candidates` list the abilities top first (`{ id: stack id, sourceName, abilityText, targets, targetsNext? }`); the answer `resolveOrder` names every one once, the first to resolve first. `settleTriggerOrderChoice` permutes them among the batch's own stack positions (bottom-up = the reverse of `resolveOrder`) and strips the stamp; anything else decides nothing and the question is asked again. The trigger-target questions then follow in the order chosen (the lowest waiting object first). Contract: `PENDING_CHOICE_KINDS` + fixture (auto path `autoPickTriggerOrder` — the standing order), `PLAY_API_VERSION` 1.6.0 (PLAY-API-CONTRACT.md row), no new wire field (the abilities ride `candidates`; `batch` never reaches the wire). UI: `TriggerOrderPanel` (learnDecisionPanels.jsx — the abilities as a list in the order they will resolve, each row "Resolves first" … "Resolves last", its source, text and targets or "You choose its targets after the order", ▲▼ like the scry panel, one Done; it opens in the standing order, so Done alone keeps it), `useLearnSession.applyTriggerOrderChoice`, the LearnView sheet and router. The stale `orderTriggersAPNAP` doc rewritten and moved onto the function. ENGINE-SCAFFOLD §4.4 names it.
> · **Two existing tests changed on purpose:** `triggerTargetChoice.test.js` "two of your enters triggers at once" and `wardTriggeredAbility.test.js` "two of your triggers at once" — two Ravenous Chupacabras are two sources, so their order is asked first now; each answers it with the standing order, then runs its unchanged assertions.
> · **Judgment calls:** (1) **The order before the targets.** CR 603.3d — each ability's targets are chosen as it is put on the stack, so the order decides whose targets are announced first; asking the whole order up front and then the targets in stack order (the first put on, first) matches that sequence. Only a later ability targeting an earlier one of the same batch on the stack could tell the difference, and the engine's candidates are enumerated at the flush either way (as in the trigger-target slice). (2) **When to ask — the identity rule.** Interchangeable = the stack object minus its id, plus the printed sentence, is the same JSON: the same ability of the same source for the same trigger event, with the same auto-taken targets or the same candidates (Panharmonicon's extra instance). Copies resolve the same in any order. Anything else is asked: asking is always legal, so the rule can only add a question nobody needed, never skip one that mattered. Two sources with the same text (two Chupacabras, a board of identical tokens) are asked — found-not-fixed (1). (3) **Recorded at the flush, asked by the driver**, like the trigger-target and ward questions: every flush site's own follow-up is unchanged, the choice slot stays single, and a flush inside a resolution never sets a choice. (4) **One answer, the whole order** — not one pick per question: one pause per batch, one settle, one save point; the panel builds it locally. (5) **Permuted among the batch's own positions**, so an AI's abilities of the same batch keep their APNAP places whatever the person answers (CR 101.4). (6) `resolveTopOfStack` does not refuse an `awaitingOrder` object (unlike `awaitingTargets`): it is complete, and the driver asks before anyone receives priority. (7) A pilot (the contract's auto path, unreachable at a real table — only `humanSeats` are asked) is offered one order per ability resolving first with the rest as they stand, not all n! orders.
> · ⚠️ **Found, not fixed:** (1) **Same text, different sources are asked** — two copies of a card, or a board of identical tokens dying together, ask an order; one Done keeps it. Treating them as interchangeable needs a reading that the effect never refers to its source (gameEngine.markTriggerOrder's key). (2) **CR 603.3b's two parts are one pass** — "each triggered ability … with a trigger condition that isn't another ability triggering" goes on first, the rest second; `orderTriggersAPNAP` (gameEngine.js:1434) places every trigger of the batch in one APNAP pass. (3) The AI's abilities later in APNAP order chose their targets at the flush, before the person orders and targets theirs (the trigger-target entry's judgment (3), unchanged). (4) Unrelated, seen live: React's duplicate-key warning from the Academy's deck `select` (LearnView.jsx:523 / 540, `key={d.id}`) in the scratch profile — not investigated.
> · Witness: `triggerOrderChoice.test.js` (12), `triggerOrderPanel.test.jsx` (5).

A keyword with no readable ward line keeps the first mana ward its text names (Emerin, Catch of the Day, Squishy Sphinx Ninja — the old read), else unpayable. runProgram: `canAffordWardCost` / `settleSoftCounterCost` grew `discard-random` (the seeded `pitchRandomDiscard`), `all` (all-or-nothing, checked whole then paid life → mana → random discard; the chosen discard handed to `advanceDiscardChain` as before) and `any` (`wardCostOption` — the payer's `option`, else the house pick: an affordable alternative that discards nothing first); `unpayable` is never affordable. actionDispatcher: the loyalty path raises the ward and Diffusion's tax like the ability path; every ward / Diffusion raise stamps `priorityAfter` (the caster / activator; `raiseWardOwed` the holder at its raise), carried onto a discard payment's pause; `learnSession.settleSoftCounterChoice` and `settleDiscardChoice` run `gameEngine.returnPriorityAfterWard` after the finalize (no holder / holder gone / no-priority step → unchanged; a soft counterspell carries none and keeps CR 117.3b). `moveStackTarget` records `wardOwed` on the redirected object (not for an uncounterable spell), asked by `raiseWardOwed`. The driver's soft-counter decision carries `objectKind` and, for `any`, `optionsAffordable` (both added to decisionWire's whitelist; `priorityAfter` stripped); `SoftCounterPanel` reads "<card>’s ability will be countered", one button per alternative, and "This game can’t take that payment yet" for unpayable; `wardCostLabel` names `all` / `any` / `unpayable`; the hook sends `option`. PLAY_API_VERSION 1.4.0 → **1.5.0** (additive MINOR; PLAY-API-CONTRACT).
> · **Judgment calls:** (1) **Priority after a ward**: in the rules the caster holds priority with the ward on the stack (117.3c, 117.5), and after the ward resolves the active player gets it (117.3b); the engine collapses the ward into an immediate question, so it can keep one of the two — it keeps the caster's (the one 117.3c guarantees for every cast; with the active player's, a non-active caster could never act before the active player after casting at a ward permanent). (2) **One question for all the wards**, not one per ward: every answer to separate questions is one of these outcomes except paying some and declining others, which counters the spell all the same; the AI's pay-if-able therefore never pays a part it can't finish. (3) **Unreadable → unpayable, not free** (per the slice's charter: never a free ward) — Vein Ripper, Evin, Ulamog, Emrakul, Sauron, Ygra, Valgavoth (sacrifice), The Serpent Society, That Which Was Compleated (poison), Axebane Ferox, The Unagi, Auntie Ool, Saruman of Many Colors: a spell or ability aimed at one is now always countered — the payer is denied a legal payment (an under-offer), never handed an outcome the rules forbid. (4) Life = power and Minthara's X are read when asked (their rulings: as the ward resolves — the same moment in the collapsed model); Minthara with no counters asks {0}. (5) The house pick for an alternative cost prefers one that discards no card. (6) Within one payment, a random discard is taken before a chosen one (no corpus card combines them on one spell). (7) Diffusion Sliver got the loyalty raise and the priority return too (the same trigger shape); its own single-target limit and its overlap with a ward on one spell are unchanged. (8) Catch of the Day and Squishy Sphinx Ninja keep their old (unconditional) mana ward — their conditions aren't read; Emerin's "ward 2" grant to itself now reads as {2}. (9) Hag of Mage's Doom: her own grant's quoted "Ward—Pay 2 life" used to be read as a printed ward AND counted as the grant (4 life); it is one instance now (2).
> · ⚠️ **Found, not fixed:** (1) **Copies** — a copy of a spell or ability with targets raises no ward (the copied object's targets become its targets — the Best in Show ruling's chain): effects/atoms/stack.js applyCopySelfSpell :1780, applyCopySpell :1826, applyCopyInstantOrSorcery :2044, applyCopyCreatureSpell :2073, applyCopyActivatedAbility :2447, applyCopyTargetAbility :2464, and storm. (2) `autoPickSoftCounterPay` (effects/runProgram.js:1777) still pays whenever able, including for a forced beneficial trigger aimed at an opponent's ward creature. (3) The AI's spell targeting ignores ward — it may now aim removal at an unpayable-ward permanent (Vein Ripper) and lose the spell; the trigger chooser already avoids it (`withoutUnpaidWard`). (4) Sacrifice wards could be paid through the sac-unless-pay lane's pool predicate (`sacrificePoolMatchNow`) once a person can pick the victim. (5) Diffusion Sliver (groupWard.js:79) still taxes a single target only, isn't raised for triggered abilities, and is dropped when a ward on the same spell takes the choice slot. (6) Stale comments: coverage.js:1126–1131 ("parseWardCost returns null for them"), spellEffects.js:654–656.
> · Witnesses: `wardCompleteness.test.js` (35), `softCounterPanelWording.test.jsx` (5).

> ## 🔧 2026-10-20 — FIX (AI decision quality): a deathtouch blocker that kills a bigger attacker dies too — the racer's group judgment counted such a block as a free kill (`blockKillsForNothing`'s clause: a mutual kill is "for nothing" when the attacker's power plus toughness is above the deathtouch blocker's), so a lone Typhoid Rats kept two Zombie tokens home and a single untapped Atraxa, Praetors' Voice kept Old Gnawbone, Avenger of Zendikar and Apex Devastator home (the racer entry's found-not-fixed (1)); the loss the group judgment weighs is now the TRADE VALUATION — each block an edge worth the attacker it kills less the blocker it loses, the defender's best a maximum-weight matching of its blocker slots to the attackers (one blocker takes one attacker; CR 509.1a, 510.2, 702.2b), so a trade counts the difference between the two creatures, a trade the defender would lose by counts nothing, and a deathtouch blocker can take only one of the group · **±0** · snapshot native+land 15,765 unchanged
> Suite **21,736 green (1 skipped) / 1,940 files** under the gate queue, first run of the final code (with the rules index built for the run inside the worktree, then deleted); sha256 of the changed code and test file identical before and after the run — the docs (this entry, CHANGELOG, ENGINE-SCAFFOLD) were written beside it, and no test reads them. Witness `aiRacerDeathtouchTrade.test.js`: **16 tests — the 11 board tests written before the engine change and run on an untouched copy of 221d4fb4: 7 fail there on assertions, the 4 controls pass on both**; the 5 matching tests (the Hungarian against an exhaustive search on 300 seeded random boards, every prefix; one blocker one attacker; menace; the cap) call the new test handle and were written with the change. A/B **80 seeded commander games** (base seed 7, 10 per pod, the 30 profile decks, default AI; base = the untouched 221d4fb4 archive; reference data from a scratch copy, MTG_APP_ROOT per command): **76 byte-identical, 4 change picks, 1 winner change** (game 71: user → ai3), 0 errors on either tree; ai-wins 53 → 54, user-wins 27 → 26; attacks declared 3,412 → 3,415; combat damage to players 10,219 → 10,236; turns 2,740 → 2,731; 199.7 s / 236.7 s. Committed on `day/dttrade`, not pushed; the release-batch line and the WAKE-REPORT are the integrator's.
> · **The four changed games, first divergence each (every one a held attacker now declared):** game 77 (turn 35) — the user seat's Solphim, Mayhem Dominus (5/4) and Sheoldred, the Apocalypse (4/5 deathtouch) attack ai1 at 35, whose one untapped creature is its commander Atraxa (4/4 deathtouch); base: no attack (both "eaten for nothing" by the clause). Atraxa blocked Solphim, both died, Sheoldred connected for 4 — the deathtouch commander traded down. Better. Game 42 (turn 20) — Trophy Mage (2/2) joins Bruce Banner against the user at 5 life, whose only blocker is Roadkill Rodney (2/1 deathtouch): Rodney blocking it is a near-even trade (5.2 against 3.9 value), not a free kill. Rodney blocked it, Tamiyo's Safekeeping saved it, Rodney died. Better. Game 50 (turn 23) and game 71 (turn 31) — a lone 3/3 Elephant token against a group whose safe attacker it can trade with up (Solitude 3/2; Vihaan, Goldwaker 3/3, the commander): its best block is that trade, so the small attackers it could otherwise eat (Bloom Tender and Generous Pup; Zulaport Cutthroat) cost nothing more — one blocker, one block. Both times the Elephant blocked that attacker and the extras connected (3 and 1 more damage). Better under the model, and the engine's defender behaved as it predicts. Game 71's winner change comes 12 turns later (the game is 10 turns shorter), not attributable to the one point.
> · **The census** (every AI declaration through a pure hook in scratch copies of both trees — 80 / 80 byte-identical to the clean runs on each): declarations into an untapped deathtouch creature that can block the attacker **35 → 37**; of them, attackers bigger (power plus toughness) than every such blocker — the boards the clause called free kills — **2 → 5** (power 10 → 21: + Trophy Mage, Solphim, Sheoldred). Deathtouch blockers are rare in this batch: 16 combats (base) offer an attacker one can block — Atraxa in 29 of the 35 declarations — so the batch exercises the fix only lightly; the witnesses carry it.
> · **The gap** (opponentAI.outnumberingAttackers, 221d4fb4): `worstCaseLoss` matched blocker slots only to "killers" — blockers that kill the attacker for nothing by `blockKillsForNothing`, whose deathtouch clause counts a mutual kill as free when the attacker is bigger — and credited nothing for the blocker that dies; a non-deathtouch trade counted nothing at all.
> · **The fix** — `opponentAI.tradeLossPrefixes` (new; `tradeEdgeValue` the edge, `combatDuel` decides who dies): the loss of each cheapest-first prefix of the attackers (those that go anyway first) is the defender's maximum-weight matching of slots to attackers under edges worth LIFE_PER_VALUE × (the attacker's value if it dies − the blocker's value if it dies), floored at 0. Exact: the Hungarian method adds one row at a time and keeps the matching of the rows so far optimal (dual feasible, tight on matched edges, unmatched columns at potential 0), so one pass gives every prefix, O(R²·(S+R)); the bound — up to 64 matching rows, beyond which the base (the attackers that go anyway) is bounded from below by a greedy matching and every longer prefix from above (the smaller of each slot's best edge and each row's best edge summed), so the gain is never overstated. A menace / "≥N" attacker is N rows of 1/N its best single-blocker trade (worstCaseLoss's reading). The damage side is unchanged (`unavoidableDamage`, every slot chumping the biggest), both worst cases at once. Policy `racerTrade: "v1"` keeps `worstCaseLoss` (POLICY_KEYS); test handle `__tradeLossPrefixesForTests`. ENGINE-SCAFFOLD §4.8 describes it.
> · **Judgment calls:** (1) The damage stays off the edges. A single assignment whose edges also carry the damage a block stops would charge a chump its blocker and so assume the defender chumps; then a small attacker it would eat for free looks cheap — `opponentAI.test.js` "drops unprofitable attackers" (a 5/5 and a 1/1 into a 3/3 wall at 10 life) went red that way, sending the 1/1 to die. Kept: damage and loss at the defender's best, both at once, as the racer already judged. (2) First draft valued a menace attacker's gang block (the N strongest blockers together killing it, no blocker loss charged) — an upper bound that, on an attacker going anyway, inflated the base and made the group look free: run 1 of the A/B changed a fifth game (48: Tempestra, Big Mother Mouser and Tokka & Rahzar sent beside Heroes in a Half Shell into Bruce Banner and Abomination, both of which eat them for free) for that reason alone. Revised to worstCaseLoss's single-blocker reading, and the over-cap bound made one-sided; game 48 is byte-identical in the run of record. (3) Trades are valued by `boardEval.permanentValue` (mana value heavy): Old Gnawbone (13.2) for a commander Atraxa (9.4) is a 15.2-life loss, so Gnawbone joins a wide attack into Atraxa only when what else Atraxa could block is worth more than that (the witness: four Grizzly Bears beside it, Atraxa's controller at 9), and stays home at 40 (a control). (4) A trade with a non-deathtouch blocker now counts when the attacker is worth more (it counted nothing): the effect seen in games 50 and 71.
> · ⚠️ **Found, not fixed:** (1) `unavoidableDamage` (opponentAI.js:2621) ignores trample and double strike — the racer's lethality, the group's damage, the walker policy's reach and the crack-back all read it; separable, but it moves lethal calls everywhere and needs its own A/B. (2) The per-attacker hold still uses the clause (`blockKillsForNothing`, opponentAI.js:2595): the racer's safe set and the planeswalker policy's `safe` filter (opponentAI.js:3268) still treat a bigger attacker into a smaller deathtouch blocker as eaten for nothing — the group judgment now rescues the racer's, the walker policy's is not. (3) Gang blocks (two blockers on one attacker) are modelled on neither side, menace included (opponentAI.js:2867). (4) A blocker with lifelink gains its controller life on the block (Atraxa: 4), not valued. (5) A blocker that can block several attackers is read as independent slots, each charged its death (blockSlots' reading), so blocking two attackers it is charged twice.
> · Witness: `aiRacerDeathtouchTrade.test.js` (16).

> ## 🔧 2026-10-20 — FIX (AI decision quality + soft-lock): the session driver's anti-loop latch no longer throws away an action that changed the game — it read only `progressSignature` (turn, step, distinct attackers / blockers, stack depth, the active player's hand and pool, battlefield count, the free-cast / cascade / discover windows) and passed from the state before any auto-decided non-pass action that moved none of those, so every AI crew while crew took effect at once (22 of 22 in the 80-game A/B), a turn-face-up paid by tapping lands (CR 701.40b), a second block by a creature that can block more than one (CR 509.1a — Palace Guard) and "done" in Etali, Primal Storm's cast-from-among window (CR 608.2g — the window never closed and the game wedged) were undone; now `antiLoopLatch.actionChangedGame` reads the signature first and then the whole state outside the bookkeeping fields, with exact repeats folded, so PR 10.3's re-declared-attacker loop and a true no-op are still passed on · **±0** · snapshot native+land 15,769 unchanged
> Suite **21,795 green (1 skipped) / 1,945 files** under the gate queue, first run (with the rules index built for the run inside the worktree, then deleted); it ran on the final code and test bytes (sha256 of the four changed code and test files checked before and after the run) — the docs (this entry, CHANGELOG, ENGINE-SCAFFOLD) were written beside it, and no test reads them. Lint 0 (CR citations: 0 of 12,493 name no rule; keyword citations: 0 of 2,504 cite a different keyword). Flip-diff **0 / 0 / RETIERED 0** (34,620 cards; before = an untouched `git archive` of 660c7639; native-* + land 15,769 of 34,584 snapshot names on both). **Mutants 6/6** on assertions, each restored byte-identical (sha256): the whole-state read removed (5 tests red — the four witnesses and the predicate's change cases), repeats not folded (2 — PR 10.3's loop control), the log compared (2 — the no-op control), the priority holder and pass count compared (1), an undefined-valued key counted (1), a rebuilt object counted as a change (3). Witness `antiLoopLatch.test.js` (6) run on the untouched 660c7639 archive: **the 4 witnesses fail there on assertions, the 2 controls pass on both**; it was written beside the engine change, not before it. `antiLoopLatchProgress.test.js` (2) pins the predicate. A/B **80 seeded commander games** (base seed 7, 10 per pod, the 30 profile decks, default AI; base = the untouched 660c7639 archive): **74 byte-identical**; **6 change play** — games 60, 63, 64, 65, 66, 69, the Shorikai Vehicles pod — and **every first divergence is an AI crew the base threw away** (Prodigy's Prototype, Imposter Mech as a copy of Thrun, Breaker of Silence, Shorikai, Nautiloid Ship, Mechtitan Core, Smuggler's Copter); crew-vehicle log lines 0 → 12; **1 winner changes** (game 69, ai2 → ai3); turns move in 4 (60: 36 → 32, 64: 33 → 35, 65: 47 → 32, 69: 57 → 51); 0 errors, 0 engine-stuck, 0 turn-cap games on either tree (longest game 62 turns / 3,197 ticks on both); results unchanged (ai-wins 53 / user-wins 27); **196.2 s / 193.1 s (24.46 / 24.86 games per minute)**. The predicate's cost, timed as an observer over the 80 games: 9,747 calls, 70.1 ms in all (about 7 µs a call); the whole-state read ran 12 times. Committed on `day/latch`, not pushed; the release-batch line and the WAKE-REPORT are the integrator's.
> · **The latch and its history.** PR 10.4 (5972d3da, 2026-06-05) added it behind PR 10.3's fix (b9570788): a Vigilance attacker stayed untapped after its declaration, was offered again, and each re-declaration appended another copy of the same attacker entry — the signature counted DISTINCT attackers for exactly that. 1beabb4a (2026-07-01) added the pending-window bits after the latch rolled a free-cast decline back to a force-pass on the pre-decline state and wedged the window — the same failure as this one, fixed then for three flags only.
> · **The census** (observer hooks in a copy of the base tree, the 80-game batch byte-identical to the plain base run): 9,811 auto-decided non-pass actions; **22 left the signature unchanged, all `crew-vehicle`, all real changes** (the crew taps, `becameTappedThisTurn`, `pendingTapEvents`, a layer-4 continuous effect, a summoning-sick stamp) — Prodigy's Prototype ×3, Shorikai ×7 (Shimmer Myr, Kotori, Ironsoul Enforcer crewing), Imposter Mech-as-Thrun ×2, Nautiloid Ship ×2, Mechtitan Core ×4, Smuggler's Copter ×4, in games 60, 63–66, 69; **no true no-op**. On the fixed tree the same census found **0 of 9,747** non-pass actions with an unchanged state. Outside the batch, a static read of the dispatcher's 23 handlers found three more signature-blind actions, each reproduced on the base through the driver: turn-face-up paid by tapping lands (no stack, nothing enters or leaves, the pool 0 → 0), a multi-blocker's second block (same `blockerId`), and `cast-from-among-done` (clears `pendingCastFromAmong`, a flag the signature never read — on the base the AI's Etali exiled only a Day of Judgment it holds, the window stayed open, and no seat was offered anything but the window until the user's turn-19 cleanup). The signature also reads only the ACTIVE player's hand and pool, so a non-active seat's tap-for-mana or instant-speed suspend was invisible to it.
> · **The fix** (`antiLoopLatch.js`, a new zero-import leaf; `learnSession.js` imports it and drops its private copy of `progressSignature`). `actionChangedGame(before, after)`: identical objects → no change; a different signature → change (the common case, unchanged cost); otherwise the whole state is compared, skipping `LATCH_BOOKKEEPING_KEYS` (`log`, `priorityHolder`, `consecutivePasses`, `idSeq`, `timestampCounter`, `rngSeed` — every action restates the priority fields, CR 117.3c, and the counters move only beside a change seen elsewhere), treating an undefined-valued key as absent, and comparing arrays with exact repeats removed (first occurrences, order kept): a duplicated attacker entry and the duplicated defender in the attacker's `attackedPlayersThisTurn` memo are PR 10.3's loop and stay "no change"; a new, removed, changed or reordered element is a change. The latch site is otherwise as it was: a no-change action is replaced by a pass from the state before it.
> · **On master 39b8a81a** (crew on the stack): `learnSession.js` is byte-identical on 660c7639 and 39b8a81a, and the change applies cleanly there. Crew now pushes a stack object, so the signature already sees it — the latch keeps it with or without this fix, and the whole-state read never runs for a crew. On a 39b8a81a archive with this change: `antiLoopLatch`, `antiLoopLatchProgress`, `activationPriority`, `crewVehicles`, `mobilizerMech`, `termination`, `freeCast` — 7 files, 62 tests green; on pure 39b8a81a the crew witness passes and the turn-face-up, multi-block and Etali witnesses fail.
> · **Judgment calls:** (1) the signature stays as the fast path — a different signature is always a different state, so it changes no outcome, and it keeps the whole-state read off ~99.9% of actions. (2) Repeats fold at every array, not only `combat.attackers`: the re-declaration also grows the attacker's per-turn defender memo, so a combat-only dedupe would have kept PR 10.3's loop alive to the tick budget. (3) The two control loops are reconstructed with module mocks (the pre-PR-10.3 attacker offer; a dispatcher that answers the AI's land drop with a rebuilt state and a log line), since neither loop can occur on the current engine. (4) No true no-op turned up in either census, so none is named as latched; the controls stand in for the class.
> · ⚠️ **Found, not fixed:** (1) The decision-trajectory row for an auto-decided action is recorded before the dispatch (`resolveDecideAction`, learnSession.js:2612 → the row write at :1145), so a latched no-op still leaves a row whose action never happened — 0 such rows in the 80 games after the fix, 22 (the crews) before. (2) While a cast-from-among / free-cast / cascade / discover window is open, every other seat is offered nothing (legalChoices.js:4765 and its siblings) — correct mid-resolution, but it is why a window that never closes wedges the whole table rather than one seat.
> · Witness: `antiLoopLatch.test.js` (6), `antiLoopLatchProgress.test.js` (2).

> ## 🔧 2026-10-20 — FIX (rules faithfulness, false positive): ward triggers on a TRIGGERED ability an opponent controls (CR 702.21a — "Whenever this permanent becomes the target of a spell or ability an opponent controls, counter that spell or ability unless that player pays [cost]") — the trigger-target entry's found-not-fixed (2): ward was raised for spells and activated abilities only, so an opponent's triggered ability aimed at a ward permanent resolved without the ward cost ever being demanded (Ravenous Chupacabra destroyed a Leonin Lightbringer for free); now the flush and the person's trigger-target answer record it on the ability and the session driver asks it — the existing soft-counter pay-or-be-countered question — before anyone receives priority; the AI's trigger chooser passes over a ward it won't pay while another correct-side target is free of it · **±0** · snapshot native+land 15,769 unchanged
> Suite **21,801 green (1 skipped) / 1,944 files** under the gate queue, first run (the rules index built in the worktree's app/data for the run, then deleted; no MTG_APP_ROOT in that job); it ran on the final code and test bytes (sha256 of src/lib/learn, src/components/mtg and src/hooks, aeb407ce…, checked before and after the run and again before the commit) — the docs (this entry, CHANGELOG, ENGINE-SCAFFOLD, PLAY-API-CONTRACT) were written beside it, and no test reads them. Lint 0 (CR citations: 0 of 12,500 name no rule; keyword citations: 0 of 2,510 cite a different keyword). Flip-diff **0 / 0 / RETIERED 0** (34,620 cards; before = an untouched `git archive` of 660c7639; native+land 15,769 of 34,584 snapshot names on both). **Mutants 7/7** on assertions, each restored byte-identical (sha256; run in a scratch copy of the tree): the flush records no ward (7 tests red), the person's answer records none (2), the driver never asks (9), the record not cleared as it is asked (5), the ward asked before the trigger-target question (1), the chooser ignoring a ward it won't pay (1), ward.js taxing the controller's own permanent (2 — the controls). Witness `wardTriggeredAbility.test.js` written before the engine change and run on the untouched 660c7639 archive in its final form: **14 tests — 10 fail there on assertions, the 4 controls pass on both** (your Bond Beetle's counter on your own Lightbringer, chosen by you; the AI's Bond Beetle on its own Lightbringer; Murder at the opponent's Lightbringer asks the ward exactly as before; the AI's Chupacabra at a creature without ward). A/B **80 seeded commander games** (base seed 7, 10 per pod, the 30 profile decks, default AI; base = the untouched 660c7639 archive): **80 / 80 byte-identical** (the sha256 of every game record — each decision row, the log, result, winner, turns, ticks), 0 errors on either tree, results unchanged (ai-wins 53 / user-wins 27), 198.5 s / 195.3 s. **Census** (scratch copies of both trees instrumented with one log line per new triggered ability aimed at an opponent's ward permanent, evaluated where the after tree records the ward; each instrumented batch equals its uninstrumented twin once those lines are dropped, 80 / 80 on both; the instrumentation seen to fire on a Chupacabra-at-Lightbringer probe on both trees): **0 on base, 0 after** — 19 ward cards in the 30 decks (printed or granted: Innkeeper's Talent, Sheltered by Ghosts, Chains of Custody, Brotherhood Regalia), 14 of them entered the battlefield, 42 (card, game) pairs, and spells were asked a ward 8 times in the base batch (Swords to Plowshares at a ward-granted Walking Ballista, Path to Exile at Ghyrson Starn, Valorous Stance at Hexing Squelcher …), but no triggered ability in the batch aimed at one. (An 8-game smoke run of the A/B script — one game per pod, meant as a zero-game load check — ran ungated before the gated runs; its output was discarded.) Committed on `day/wardtrig`, not pushed; the release-batch line and the WAKE-REPORT are the integrator's.
> · **The gap** (660c7639): `actionDispatcher` raised ward at the cast path (wardTaxForSpell → setPendingSoftCounterChoice, :1155) and the activated-ability path (:1864); `gameEngine.flushTriggers`' target-event loop (:2351) and `settleTriggerTargetChoice` ran becomes-the-target, crime and Kira only. ward.js's header already claimed "an opponent's ABILITY targeting a ward permanent now raises the ward tax too" for triggered abilities.
> · **The fix** — reuse, not a second ward: `markWardOwed` (after Kira, in the flush loop and in the settle) asks `ward.wardTaxForStackObject` — the cast and ability paths' detector (one ward target; the mana, life and discard costs; an opponent's permanent only) — and stamps `wardOwed: { cost, wardName }` on the triggered ability; `raiseWardOwed` (the session driver, right after the trigger-target raise, before the pendingChoice block) turns the lowest owed ability into the existing `soft-counter` pause (`setPendingSoftCounterChoice` → `resolveSoftCounterChoice`, `autoPickSoftCounterPay` for an AI, the SoftCounterPanel for a person) and clears the record. `chooseTriggerTargets` gains `withoutUnpaidWard` (ahead of the loop backstop, the fight restraint and the flicker pick): a correct-side candidate whose ward its controller wouldn't pay (the same answer the driver will give) is dropped while another candidate is free of it; all such → unchanged. The stack view (boardSnapshot.stackView) whitelists fields, so `wardOwed` never reaches the board. PLAY-API-CONTRACT's `soft-counter` row now says spell or ability (no new kind, no shape change, PLAY_API_VERSION unchanged). ENGINE-SCAFFOLD §4.4 names it.
> · **Judgment calls:** (1) RECORDED at the flush and ASKED by the driver, not raised in the flush: the choice slot is single (setPendingSoftCounterChoice no-ops when occupied) — raising in the flush would have dropped a second ward in one batch and, on the cast path, the spell's own ward (raised after its cast-trigger flush; witnessed: Murder + Weaver of Lightning's ping at one Lightbringer ask {2} twice), and a flush inside a resolution never sets a choice. (2) The ward is asked as an immediate pay-or-counter, as the spell and ability paths model it — no ward object on the stack that players could respond to. (3) Order: the spell's ward before its cast trigger's; within one batch the lowest owed ability first. In the rules a cast trigger's ward goes on the stack after the spell's and resolves first — only a payer short of mana for both sees a difference. (4) The ward is asked only after every ability of its batch has its targets (the driver raises the trigger-target question first — CR 603.3: the batch goes on the stack before the wards that trigger on it); an explicit gate in raiseWardOwed was removed as dead code (its mutant survived — the driver order already guarantees it; the mutant swapping that order is the one kept). (5) The chooser preference is small and ranking-only (never a wrong-side target); it shares the AI's pay-if-able answer, so the AI never aims where it will then decline. (6) A caller that resolves the stack without the session driver skips an owed ward (as every ward did before for triggers); resolveTopOfStack does not refuse it, unlike `awaitingTargets`, since AI previews resolve copies without the driver.
> · ⚠️ **Found, not fixed:** (1) **Loyalty abilities raise no ward** — `applyActivateLoyalty` (actionDispatcher.js:2011–2091) runs becomes-the-target, crime and Kira but never `wardTaxForStackObject` (Chandra, Torch of Defiance's −3 at a ward creature is free). (2) Every ward settle resets priority to the active player (learnSession.settleSoftCounterChoice :754 → gameEngine.finalizeStackResolution :1308 → resetPriorityLoop :222), so a non-active caster loses the priority it keeps after casting (CR 117.3c) — spells and activated abilities before this slice, now triggers too. (3) `autoPickSoftCounterPay` (effects/runProgram.js:1718) pays whenever able — including for a forced trigger that harms its own controller's side (a mandatory buff forced onto an opponent's ward creature). > · **The gap** (gameEngine.buildTriggerStack / chooseTriggerTargets, 31d97587:1620–1646): one chooser picked the targets of every seat's triggered abilities; a person's "destroy target creature an opponent controls" or "2 damage to any target" was aimed by the AI's heuristic, an "up to one" could not be declined, and a modal trigger's mode was the AI's. Both earlier ledger entries named it found-not-fixed (the trigger-target restraint entry, (2); the reflexive-trigger entry, Faebloom Trick's tap).
> · **The fix** — the ability goes on the stack WAITING for its controller (CR 601.2a: an object is on the stack while its choices are made). At a live flush (`flushTriggers` with the automatic chooser) a trigger of a seat in `state.humanSeats` (createLearnSession stamps the user seat below Expert) is routed with `askControllerChooser`: with two or more legal candidates, or a modal "choose up to one" with any, it answers the private `ASK_CONTROLLER` sentinel at each of `buildTriggerStack`'s four choose sites (intervening-if, non-modal, modal, reflexive), and the ability is put on the stack in its APNAP place with its payload, no target yet, and `awaitingTargets: { candidates, abilityText, allowNone? }` — the engine's own `expandCastChoices` candidates, legality never re-derived. Its target events (becomes-the-target, crime, Kira) are skipped there. The session driver, before the pendingChoice block, raises the question for the LOWEST waiting object (`raiseTriggerTargetChoice` → `setPendingTriggerTargetChoice`, the new `trigger-target` kind — the order the batch went on the stack, CR 603.3b). `settleTriggerTargetChoice` writes the pick where the chooser writes it (`targets`, `payload.params.targets` / `.chosenMode`), runs the target events, and once no object of the batch waits flushes what they enqueued (together, APNAP). "none" removes a modal "choose up to one" ability (CR 603.3c, 700.2b); an answer that is no candidate decides nothing and is asked again. `resolveTopOfStack` throws on a waiting object — the driver asks before anyone receives priority. A single legal choice is taken unasked, as before. Contract: `PENDING_CHOICE_KINDS` + fixture (auto path `autoPickTriggerTarget` — the chooser's pick among the waiting object's choices, mapped to its index), `PLAY_API_VERSION` 1.4.0 (PLAY-API-CONTRACT.md row), the wire whitelist gains `abilityText` and `allowNone`; the board snapshot never shows `awaitingTargets`. UI: `TriggerTargetPanel` (learnDecisionPanels.jsx — one button per legal choice: a target by name and whose, a player by seat, "No target" for the decline, a mode by its text, "Choose no mode" for allowNone), `useLearnSession.applyTriggerTargetChoice`, the LearnView sheet and router. ENGINE-SCAFFOLD §4.4 names it.
> · **One existing test changed:** `auraEntryHostChoice.test.js` — its Displacer Kitten and Brago triggers are the person's, so the person now answers their targets first (`aimTrigger`, the same permanents the automatic chooser took) before the Aura's host question; the "AI flicker read" case now asserts that the automatic answer to the person's Brago question is the set a table without a person blinks (brago, rancor, vis). 23/23 green.
> · **Judgment calls:** (1) waiting on the stack, not pausing the flush mid-batch: every flush site's own follow-up (hold in declare blockers when the stack grew, the cleanup window, the attack-declaration hold, a resolution already paused on another choice) stays exactly as it is, and the settle is local to one object. (2) Modal triggers are in: their candidates are (mode × targets) already, so the person chooses the mode too (CR 603.3c) — Knight of Autumn's three modes, each labelled. (3) The AI's triggers later in APNAP order choose their targets at the flush, before the person answers — the rules have them choose after the person's are on the stack; only a "target an ability on the stack" choice could differ. (4) The ask fires only at a live flush (`chooseTargets === chooseTriggerTargets`), so a caller passing its own chooser — tests, the AI's cast-time preview (`entersTriggerRemovesOwn`, which calls `buildTriggerStack` directly) — is untouched. (5) An answer that names no candidate re-asks rather than picking for the person.
> · ⚠️ **Found, not fixed:** (1) **No order choice for a person's simultaneous triggers** — CR 603.3b lets each player put theirs on the stack "in any order they choose"; `orderTriggersAPNAP` (gameEngine.js:1398) keeps FIFO within a controller, for every seat. (2) **Ward never triggers on a triggered ability's target** — `flushTriggers`' target-event loop (gameEngine.js:2351, and now the settle) runs becomes-the-target, crime and Kira only; ward's pay-or-be-countered is raised for spells and activated abilities in the dispatcher (actionDispatcher.js:1864), never for a triggered ability, for any seat. (3) The expander's 64-candidate cap (targeting.js:91; the "up to one" decline appended last at :462) drops a person's decline past 63 legal targets and limits "any number" (Brago) to 64 subsets — with 7+ nonland permanents a person can't pick every subset. (4) A person's single-candidate OPTIONAL ability whose one target is on the wrong side still becomes the Arbiter no-op (askControllerChooser gameEngine.js:1439 → chooseTriggerTargets → `pickForcedTriggerCandidate` returns null for an optional atom, :1962) instead of going on the stack with that target and asking "you may" at resolution — false-negative safe. (5) A trigger the α1 allowlist sends to the Arbiter no-op (an atom whose target side can't be read — gameEngine.js:1774) is never offered to a person either.

(3) **The fixed-mana and {0} alternatives are hand-only** — a commander cast from the command zone (Dracogenesis with a Dragon commander: {0} + the commander tax), a graveyard or exile cast, and any {X} spell are not offered them; As Foretold's ruling "If a spell has no mana cost, its mana value is 0. You can cast it with As Foretold's alternative cost" (Ancestral Vision, Living End) is not offered — the CR 202.1a gate refuses a costless card before the variants are built. (4) **AI quality:** the default AI pays the printed cost for a Dragon when Dracogenesis offers {0} (A/B game 26: Goldspan Dragon for {R}{R}) — `opponentAI.filterAltCastVariants` prefers a FREE `altCost` twin, but a fixed-mana variant (`altManaCost`) is never preferred; a non-latched {0} variant strictly dominates its printed twin. (5) Not taken, same family: Tlincalli Hunter, Charred Foyer, Dragon's Smile ("a spell you cast from exile"), Grenzo, Crooked Jailer ("that you don't own with mana value 3 or less"), Runeforge Champion ("{1} … Rune spells"), Etched Oracle Avatar (the five pips for "spells that you cast"), Kentaro, the Smiling Cat ("{X} … where X is that spell's mana value").

> ## 🔧 2026-10-18 — FIX (rules faithfulness): the attacking player gets priority after blockers are declared — the declare blockers step's first lap of passes was both the defending players' block declaration and the step's last round of priority, so its passes ended the step: the attacker never held priority on the declared blocks (a trick after blocks was reachable only when another player acted first), in a pod the players seated before the defender never saw the blocks, the active player could cast spells before any block existed and a defender in the middle of its own declaration; now the declaration is open from the step's start until every player has passed once, only blocks and the pass are offered while it is open, and when it closes the block triggers go on the stack, the active player receives priority with the pass count reset, no block is offered any more, and the step ends only when the stack is empty and all players pass again (CR 509.1, 509.2, 509.2a, 117.4, 500.2) · **±0** · snapshot native+land 15,728 unchanged

> · **The bug (reproduced on 32865c89, the engine's own entry points).** Two seats, the user's Grizzly Bears attacking the AI's Hill Giant, the
>   user holding Giant Growth: in declare blockers the user held priority with no block (Giant Growth offered), passed; the AI declared its
>   block and passed — and the step ended (`first-strike-damage` next). In a pod (the user attacking ai2) the order was user (no block) → ai1 →
>   ai2 blocks → ai3 → step over: neither the attacker nor ai1 ever saw the block in the step. The phantom first-strike damage step (found,
>   not fixed (2)) was the only window where a human attacker could still pump; the AI's block-trick reader (`trickGain`) asks for the declare
>   blockers step, so the AI attacker never did.
> · **The fix** (`gameEngine.js`, `gameState.js`, `legalChoices.js`). Entering declare blockers marks `combat.blockDeclarationOpen`
>   (`runStepActions`; `gameState.blockDeclarationOpen` is the one predicate). While it is open `legalActionsForPlayer` offers only
>   `declare-blocker` and the pass — no spell, ability, special action or mana ability (CR 509.1: no player has priority during the turn-based
>   action). `passPriority`: when the lap completes with the declaration open it calls `closeBlockDeclaration` instead of resolving or
>   advancing — the block triggers fire (`fireBlockTriggers`, shared with `nextStep`'s forced advance; the mark goes, `_blockTriggersFired`
>   set) and the active player gets priority, passes 0 (CR 509.2, 509.2a). The close happens once, so the next full lap with an empty stack
>   ends the step — no loop. `actionsDeclareBlocker` returns nothing once `_blockTriggersFired` is set: before this gate the fixed tree offered a
>   block in 463 post-close windows of the 80 games (the AI took none), now 0; the base offered one whenever a block trigger held the step (the
>   witness shows it on the archive; no such window came up in the 80 base games). The
>   reset is not in `applyDeclareBlocker`: a block is one action of the declaration, and a per-block reset would hand priority around between
>   two blocks of one defender, leave the no-block case without the attacker's window, and still fire the block triggers after it. A state
>   with neither mark (a test built inside the step, an older save) keeps the older shape. The wrong citation on the old `nextStep` comment
>   ("CR 509.4" — a creature put onto the battlefield blocking) is now 509.2a.
> · **Census (AI decisions in declare blockers, the observed runs; base → after).** Attacker windows with blocks declared **13 → 273** (43 with a
>   cast offered), attacker casts there **0 → 6** (the six above); defender casts after its blocks 2 → 2 (game 54's Tamiyo's Safekeeping on
>   Laboratory Maniac now comes after the attacker's pass, same log; game 52's left with that game's divergence; game 43's Tyvar's Stand is new,
>   downstream); during the declaration (after) 1,339 attacker / 1,674 defender / 1,957 other windows, 0 casts offered; the base's attacker
>   windows before any block (1,343, 201 with a cast offered) cast nothing, so no cast was lost. Karametra's Blessing was never offered to an
>   attacker after blocks in the 80 games. Unchanged: first-strike damage step casts 1 → 1, combat damage step 16 → 16.
> · **Steps checked for a missing pass-count reset.** Declare attackers: the active player declares while holding priority with the count at 0
>   and its closing pass counts as its priority (CR 508.2) — correct. Combat damage, first-strike damage, end of combat: `grantPriority`
>   resets — correct. Resolution: `resetPriorityLoop` — correct. Dispatcher handlers: play-land, cast, activate, hand self-put, cycle,
>   discard-ability, plot, turn-face-up, loyalty, companion, suspend reset; the mid-resolution declines (discover, free cast, cascade, cast from
>   among) sit inside a resolution that already reset; **GY-1 / GY-2 graveyard activations and crew do not** (found, not fixed (1)); mana
>   abilities don't (judgment: nothing changes hands, left).
> · **Tests changed with it.** `talonGatesOfMadara.test.js` (the phased-out-blocker case activated Talon Gates for the active player while the
>   declaration was still open — the order this fix forbids; it now passes the declaration lap first, and passes on both trees).

>   empty-stack ticks, 34 raw; after, 32 and 36, one more lap of two passes; 33 is valid on both trees, measured).
> · ⚠️ **Found, not fixed:** (1) `actionDispatcher.applyActivateGyRecursion` (actionDispatcher.js:1339) and `applyActivateGyExile` (:1495) put an
>   ability on the stack without naming the activator the holder or resetting the count, and `applyCrewVehicle` (:1447) neither — and crew
>   resolves at once instead of using the stack (CR 702.122a): after the activator passes, the object can resolve or the step end before every

>   narrator's declare-blockers line ("… chooses which of their untapped creatures block …", narrator.js:114) is the same in the window after

> · **The gap** (opponentAI.selectProfitableAttackers, 79bbb347): the W4 hold sent an attacker only when it was unstoppable or no single eligible blocker killed it for nothing (`attackerDiesForNothingV2`), each judged against every blocker at once; lethality alone overrode it. The racer weighed no crack-back (the brief assumed it did): a creature it held stayed home as a blocker by accident.
> · **The fix** — `opponentAI.outnumberingAttackers` (new), called by `selectProfitableAttackers` after the hold when the swing is not lethal (policy `racer: "v1"` keeps the hold; POLICY_KEYS). The held attackers facing the focused player itself, power above 0, never a land (its permanentValue reads 0; it dies a mana source), sorted cheapest first (`boardEval.permanentValue`, power, id); the group is the cheapest k beside the attackers that go anyway (declared, the racer's safe ones, the creatures that must attack — `requiredAttackerIds`, now read before the racer). Gain = face weight × (unavoidableDamage(group) − unavoidableDamage(the rest)) − LIFE_PER_VALUE × (worstCaseLoss(group) − worstCaseLoss(the rest)): damage with the defender blocking the biggest blockable attackers with every blocker slot (`blockSlots`: one per untapped creature, more under "can block an additional creature" / "any number", `combatEvasion.maxBlocksFor`), loss with its blocks killing the most valuable attackers they can (`worstCaseLoss`: a one-slot matching to the blockers that kill each for nothing, greedy by value — exact, a transversal matroid — and a fractional knapsack of menace / "≥N" attackers over the slots, the smaller kept; CR 509.1a, 702.111b); both worst cases at once, which no single block achieves — conservative. LIFE_PER_VALUE = 4 (evaluateBoard's 0.25 per life point; the walker policy's WALKER_LIFE_PER_VALUE now reads it), the face weight 20 / life below 20 (FACE_URGENCY_LIFE). The best k with gain > 0 whose crack-back is not lethal (`crackBackReader`: each living opponent's creatures that can attack — defender, "can't attack" excepted — blocked biggest-first by the AI's creatures still untapped, an attacker without vigilance staying tapped, CR 508.1f, 702.20b; summed over the opponents) and whose attack taxes the seat can pay with the attackers that go anyway paid first (`attackTaxDetail` at the face, `canAfford` from the sources less the attackers that tap, CR 508.1h, 508.1i). `pickAttackPlan` declares the group last, cheapest first, so each per-tick re-plan counts the declared ones in and reproduces the rest. `blockKillsForNothing` is factored out of `attackerDiesForNothingV2`, unchanged. ENGINE-SCAFFOLD §4.8 names it.
> · **Judgment calls:** the exchange rate is evaluateBoard's, so five Grizzly Bears into one Rumbling Baloth at 40 life stay home (8 damage < a Bear's 12.8) and attack when its controller is at 10; five 2/2 tokens go (a control and two witnesses pin it). A block that kills a bigger attacker while its smaller deathtouch blocker dies too stays "for nothing", as the per-attacker hold counts it. The crack-back guard covers only the added group; the racer's safe attackers keep their old behaviour.
> · ⚠️ **Found, not fixed:** (1) A trade with a smaller deathtouch blocker is valued as a free kill: `blockKillsForNothing` (opponentAI.js:2197) keeps the per-attacker rule, and `worstCaseLoss` credits nothing for the blocker that dies — game 78's Old Gnawbone (9/9), Avenger of Zendikar (5/5) and Apex Devastator (10/10) stayed home against Atraxa (4/4 deathtouch), which dies blocking any of them; valuing it as a trade needs an edge-weighted matching. (2) The planeswalker policy's attacker filter is still per attacker: `planWalkerAttacks`' `safe` (opponentAI.js:2735) asks whether any one of the walker controller's blockers kills it for nothing. (3) Only the focused player's face: `chooseDefender` (opponentAI.js:2544) picks the target first; a group held there is never weighed against an opponent with fewer blockers. (4) The crack-back reads combat damage only — no commander damage, infect, creatures cast or pumped next turn, trample — and assumes every opponent attacks the AI. (5) `boardEval.permanentValue` reads 0 for an animated land (its creature bonus checks the printed type, boardEval.js:65): the group leaves land creatures out, the walker policy and the other readers still see 0. (6) `unavoidableDamage` ignores trample and double strike (an underestimate, as before), and `lethal` still budgets blockers by count where the group budgets multi-block slots.

> · **The reader** (`staticAbilityParser.parseCastCostModifier`, tried at the head of the cost section of `parseClause`; each shape is anchored on a wording no later arm reads, which the static-parse diff confirms). The spell filter (`costSpellSubject`): nothing (every spell), "colorless", one card type or subtype (the existing admissibility test — never a colour, quality, supertype, category or "non-" word), or a pair ("instant and sorcery", "Angel spells and Human") as ONE `subtypes` union, which reduces a spell carrying both words once (Herald of War's ruling: a Human Angel is reduced once per counter).

The bundled rulings witnessed: cumulative (two Helms, one each side: Lava Axe {2}{R}), never below zero, never the coloured part (Shock stays {R}).
> · **Taxes** — `costTaxForSpell(taxers, spell, caster, activePlayer)`: an `exceptCasterTurn` tax (Defense Grid) skips a spell cast on its caster's own turn — the Grid's controller pays it on an opponent's turn too ("each spell"); with no active player named the tax applies (the full cost, never a discount). Its ruling witnessed: a reduction applies to the increased cost (the opponent's Ruby Medallion: Shock {2}{R}). A `cardTypes` tax (Aura of Silence) is one union: Mind Stone {4}, Intangible Virtue {3}{W}, Bident of Thassa {4}{U}{U} — once. Card types only; "Artifact and legendary" stays unread.

Spectacle Mage's ruling witnessed: two Mages make a {4}{U} sorcery {2}{U} — the floor reads the mana value, not the cost.
> · **Scaled reducers** carry `per` with `amount: 0` until stamped, so a reader that never resolves the scale reduces nothing. Per counter on the source (`perCounterOnSource` — "… counter on this creature/artifact", the self-name normalized upstream): `collectCostReducers` stamps it off the permanent's own counters (Animar's ruling witnessed through a real cast: the cost is fixed before its cast trigger adds a counter). Per board count (`perEachCount`): `resolveCastSiteReducers` counts it for the caster through `countForSpec` at the cast site (layer-aware power — a Grizzly Bears with two +1/+1 counters counts for Temur Battlecrier), and drops a `duringYourTurn` reducer on another player's turn. Only `parseCountSource`'s `permanentsYouControl` counts with no `who` and no `excludeSelf` are admitted (the cast site has no source to exclude — "for each other creature you control" stays unread). "<filter> spells you cast have affinity for artifacts" is the same lane over artifacts you control (CR 702.41a; 702.41b — two Samis both apply). Sokka counts himself (his ruling).

> · **The bug** (reproduced on 92356a54). The damage pipeline and the toughness atoms ran `destroyLethalCreatures` (and, for planeswalkers, `destroyZeroLoyaltyPlaneswalkers`) inside the resolution, right after their own step, with the dies triggers queued there: `spellEffects.applyDamageEffect` (spellEffects.js:1846/1849), `dealSimultaneousDamage` (1679), the pump / animate / earthbend / pump-pair / base-P/T atoms (effects/atoms/combat.js:429, 507, 545, 820, 2938, 3003), and the counter, token, manifest, persist, amass and clone entries below. `runEffectProgram` puts an instant or sorcery into its owner's graveyard only after the last atom (`finishSpellResolution`, CR 608.2n), so every death was judged before it — and before every later step. Probed: a 2/3 Tarmogoyf dies to Bolt (ruling: survives as 3/4); Last Gasp kills it (ruling: "or lowers its toughness" — 0/1, survives); Ember Shot at the caster's 3/3 Psychosis Crawler kills it before "Draw a card" makes it 4/4; Marauding Raptor's rider read an empty battlefield after its own damage killed the Dinosaur; Swift Demise's "Then destroy" found nothing to destroy.
> · **The rules** (bundled CR, cited exactly). CR 704.3 / 117.5 — state-based actions are checked whenever a player would receive priority; CR 704.4 — "state-based actions pay no attention to what happens during the resolution of a spell or ability"; CR 608.2n — an instant or sorcery is put into its owner's graveyard as the final part of its resolution; CR 608.2c — the instructions are followed in the order written; CR 704.5f / 704.5g — toughness 0 or less, lethal damage; CR 704.5h / 702.2b — a creature dealt damage by a deathtouch source "since the last time state-based actions were checked" is destroyed; CR 704.5i — a planeswalker with loyalty 0.
> · **The fix** — `gameState.openResolutionWindow` / `closeResolutionWindow` (a transient `resolutionWindow` flag): `resolveTopOfStack` opens it before the resolver runs, `finalizeStackResolution` closes it just before its `checkAllStateBasedActions`. `destroyLethalCreaturesAfterEffect(state, deathtouched, cause)` is the check an effect runs: outside the window it is `destroyLethalCreatures` (unchanged — costs, special actions, combat damage, direct calls, the AI's simulations on a copy of the board such as `triggerTargetRestraint`'s fight read, which runs at the flush after the window closes); inside it destroys nothing and adds the deathtouched creatures to `deathtouchedSinceSba`, which `sba.checkAllStateBasedActions` takes into its lethal pass (CR 704.5h) and clears. `destroyZeroLoyaltyPlaneswalkersAfterEffect` does the same for the damage path's loyalty check. Neither field exists at a priority checkpoint or in a save (no schema change). ENGINE-SCAFFOLD §4.5 names the rule for a new effect.

> · **Reach.** Probed through a real Lightning Bolt cast against each Tarmogoyf-class card with a creature card and a sorcery card in the graveyards (no instant): Tarmogoyf, Polygoyf, Barrowgoyf, Pyrogoyf, The Duke of Midrange and Chimney Goyf die on 92356a54 and survive here as 3/4 (all six sized); Nethergoyf and Consuming Blob count their controller's graveyard, so an opponent's Bolt still kills them (correct — the spell goes to its caster's graveyard); Cognivore and Magnivore change when the spell is an instant / a sorcery (the Cognivore/Shock witness). Beyond the CDAs every death a spell or ability causes now happens after it (log order; by reading, the deaths of several steps of one resolution are now one batch at one check, CR 704.3, so the leaves and dies look-backs of P·34 and 1571b5e4 see one event), and any later step reads the creature still on the battlefield: Swift Demise and Marauding Raptor in the A/B; the hand-count CDAs under a spell that damages then draws (Psychosis Crawler witnessed; Tishana, Voice of Thunder, Body of Knowledge and Maro by the same reading).
> · ⚠️ **Found, not fixed:** (1) **A resolution that pauses on a choice** is finalized as it pauses — `resolveTopOfStack` always ends in `finalizeStackResolution` (gameEngine.js:1250) — so the check runs at the pause (before an instant or sorcery reaches the graveyard) and the atoms after the pause destroy on the spot again; keeping the window open across a pause needs the trigger flush at the pause to read a closed window (the fight restraint simulates on the paused state) and every settle path to finalize — its own slice. (2) The session loop's check also runs while a resolution is paused (learnSession.js:1566, before the pending choice is surfaced), as does its player-loss check. (3) Two state-based actions are still performed at the move inside a resolution: an Aura whose host left goes to the graveyard at once (CR 704.5m, gameState.detachPermanentFromAll, gameState.js:1662) and a token that leaves the battlefield ceases to exist at once (CR 704.5d, gameState.js:926) — a later step of the same resolution that reads them would differ (no case found). (4) **AI decision quality:** the AI's kill read for a damage or shrink spell uses the toughness before the spell's own card joins a graveyard (e.g. opponentAI.js:435, the X-damage picker: `xOf(a) < tou`), so it can now Bolt a 2/3 Tarmogoyf expecting a kill it no longer gets (before, the engine killed it).
