> · **The measurement** (the A/B of record's base, every `pickAttackPlan` call censused through a pure hook in a scratch copy — 80 / 80 byte-identical to the untouched archive): 1,496 combats, 3,125 declarations, **0 combats with an opposing planeswalker offered**, so 0 attacks at one — not the planner: 25 of the batch's 26 planeswalker casts resolved as `spell-unresolved` ("planeswalker (unmodeled static/triggered ability)") and the 26th was countered. With loyalty carried (the supplement's base): 26 combats offered a planeswalker (Tamiyo, Field Researcher 13, Sarkhan, Fireblood 4, Vraska the Unseen 3, Ajani Steadfast 3, Sorin Markov 3, Teferi, Hero of Dominaria 1, Kaya, Orzhov Usurper 1; loyalty 1–10, mostly 4); in 21 the offered attackers could kill one under the worst case, in 10 with the racer's safe attackers only; in 4 a walker could fire its ultimate next turn; in 18 its controller was the focused player, in 5 it had no untapped creature (the only boards the old focus read). The AI attacked a planeswalker in 4.
> · **The gap** (opponentAI.pickAttackPlan, 9a5238ef): PW-3's `chooseWalkerToKill` diverted only when the walker's controller had NO untapped creature, sent the whole chosen swing at the highest-loyalty walker, never used a creature the racer held back from the focused player, never looked at an ultimate, and re-planned each tick from the attackers still undeclared — so a kill needing two attackers lost its second after the first was declared (the supplement's game 20: one Sarkhan attacker declared, the other sent at the player; Sarkhan survived to the next turn). `selectProfitableAttackers` also counted an attack already declared at the focused player's planeswalker toward the player's lethal sum.
> · **The fix** — `opponentAI.planWalkerAttacks` (new), read by `pickAttackPlan` for every offered creature while a planeswalker is offered (pools narrowed by `obeyingAttackOptions` as before — a goaded creature never goes at one while a player other than the goader is free, CR 508.1d, 701.15b). Never while the swing is lethal on the focused player (`faceSwingIsLethal`, swingIsLethalV2 over the creatures that face that player). Per walker: `walkerThreat` — loyalty, value = 4 × `boardEval.permanentValue` (evaluateBoard's 0.25 per life point), the ultimate (the most expensive loyalty cost above the printed starting loyalty) and `ultimateNext` (loyalty already pays for it: its controller fires it on their next turn, CR 606.3, and only damage removes loyalty before then, CR 306.8). Goals: the kill (need = loyalty; worth = value, twice that with the ultimate due) and, with the ultimate due, bringing it below (need = loyalty − ultimate + 1; worth = value). `cheapestReach` picks the attackers giving up the least face damage whose damage connects beside those already declared at the walker when its controller chump-blocks the biggest blockable ones with every untapped creature (`unavoidableDamage`, factored out of swingIsLethalV2 unchanged — block legality, menace and "≥N"); an attacker counts only when that controller's blockers can't kill it for nothing (the racer's `attackerDiesForNothingV2`); its cost is the power it would have dealt the focused player (0 when the racer wasn't sending it), weighted by 20 / life below 20 life. A goal goes ahead when worth > cost and its taxes are paid: every planned attack at a walker pays `attackTaxDetail(state, controller, walkerId)`, summed across walkers and funded by `canAfford` from the seat's sources less the planned attackers without vigilance (CR 508.1f, 508.1i), Phyrexian pips with `lifePaymentContext` as the offer pays them. Greedy by gain across walkers. The walker attacks lead the plan (each pays its tax before a face attack spends the mana); everything else keeps the racer's face target. `selectProfitableAttackers` leaves attacks at the defender's planeswalkers out of its committed lethal sum. Policy key `walker: "v1"` restores the old focus and sum (POLICY_KEYS). ENGINE-SCAFFOLD §4.8 names the policy.
> · **The supplement's three games**: game 20 (turn 17) — both 2-power attackers at Sarkhan, Fireblood (4, no blockers), which dies (base: one, then the other at the player). Game 55 (turn 28) — ai2's 4-power attacker that ai3's one untapped creature can't block kills ai3's Tamiyo, Field Researcher (4), the other attacker goes at the focused ai1 (base: both at ai1; Tamiyo was offered in 7 more combats, to turn 40). Game 78 (turn 36, no blockers) — Omnath's Old Gnawbone (7) at Atraxa's Ajani Steadfast (6) and Omnath (2) + Surrak and Goreclaw (7) at Sorin Markov (9, its −7 due next turn); Maze of Ith untapped Gnawbone and prevented its damage, so Sorin alone died (base: Ajani died, Sorin lived and reached 10).

The same enrichment feeds `/api/learn/start` (route.js:52, :98) — not checked in the running app. Carrying the field (the supplement's patch) lets 12 of 23 casts enter and changes 11 of the 80 games against the untouched base; it is its own change. (2) The racer's per-attacker "dies for nothing" hold ignores that one blocker stops one attacker (`selectProfitableAttackers` / `attackerDiesForNothingV2`, opponentAI.js:2280, :2185): in the supplement Omnath kept 13 creatures (34 power) home on turns 32 and 34 of game 78 against Atraxa's single untapped creature, and the planeswalker policy inherits it — Sorin Markov at 7 with its −7 due went unattacked on turn 34. (3) The goad entry's found-not-fixed (2) stands: a must-attack creature whose face attack is taxed while a planeswalker is free still goes face and pays. (4) Damage short of a kill counts only when it stops a next-turn ultimate; a walker brought out of a non-ultimate minus ability's reach (Liliana of the Veil below −2) is not valued. (5) Two walkers of one controller are each judged against all of its blockers (over-counts blocks; conservative). (6) Mana a walker tax spends is not weighed against a postcombat play (as the face planner pays face taxes). (7) The defending AI never chump-blocks to save its own planeswalker (`pickBlockers` chumps only when face damage is lethal, opponentAI.js:1399). (8) Instant-speed answers (game 78's Maze of Ith) are not anticipated.

> ## 🔧 2026-10-18 — FIX (user-facing): a planeswalker's printed loyalty survives deck enrichment — every planeswalker in a game deck was a no-op cast · **±0**
> Found by the planeswalker-attack slice: in the 80-game A/B batch 25 of 26 planeswalker casts resolved as `spell-unresolved` and the 26th
> was countered. Cause: `learnDeckEnrich.mergeCardData` copied power and toughness from the local index but never `loyalty`, and the
> already-shaped branch (the app's saved-deck snapshot) backfilled only layout and colour identity — so `startingLoyalty` read null,
> `planeswalkerPlayable` refused the card, and actionDispatcher routed the cast to SPELL_NOOP. The same enrichment feeds `/api/learn/start`,
> so the Academy had it too (by reading). Fix: `mergeCardData` carries `loyalty` (a card's own is never overwritten), and the shaped branch
> backfills a missing loyalty on a Planeswalker type line (CR 306.5b). Witness `learnDeckEnrichLoyalty.test.js` (5): the 2 witnesses fail
> on the base on assertions, the 3 controls pass on both; mutants 3/3 (merge drops it, no backfill, overwrite own) each restored
> byte-identical. Not covered: a transforming card whose planeswalker face is the back face (the index's top-level loyalty is the front
> face's; game decks carry no card_faces) — its own slice with the exile-and-return-transformed entry.

> ## 🔧 2026-10-18 — FIX (false positive / rules faithfulness): a creature with a printed `*` toughness whose characteristic-defining ability the engine models dies to lethal damage and to toughness 0 like any other creature (CR 704.5g, 704.5f; CR 208.2, 604.3, 613.4a) — the Apex Altisaur entry's found-not-fixed (1): Lumra, Bellow of the Woods carried 190 damage in that repro and, with no lands, stayed on the battlefield as a 0/0; all 73 sized creatures of the corpus's 184 printed-`*`-toughness creatures (Tarmogoyf, Master of Etherium, Boneyard Wurm, Dakkon Blackblade, Crusader of Odric, Ulvenwald Hydra …) were immortal to damage and -X/-X. The layer engine now says whether it computed a toughness (`toughnessSized` — a printed number, a modeled layer-7a CDA or a layer-7b set; a 7d switch swaps it with power's) and the state-based action skips only the 111 it can't size — none of them credited native · **±0** · snapshot native+land 15,660 unchanged
> Suite **21,461 green (1 skipped) / 1,920 files** under the gate queue (with the rules index built for the run, then deleted) — run 1, the green of record; the docs (this entry, CHANGELOG, ENGINE-SCAFFOLD) were written beside it — no test reads them. Lint 0 (CR citations: 0 of 12,171 name no rule; keyword citations: 0 of 2,477 cite a different keyword). Flip-diff **0 / 0 / RETIERED 0** (34,620 cards; before = an untouched `git archive` of 4f5ccd5e, snapshotted before the first edit; native+land 15,660 of 34,584 snapshot names on both). **Mutants 6/6** on assertions, each restored byte-identical (sha256): the old printed-number guard back (11 tests red), no skip at all (3 — the two unsized controls and the switched Coiling Woodworm), a 7a CDA that doesn't size (10), a 7b set that doesn't size (1), a 7d switch that doesn't swap the sized flags (2), the no-effect fast path always sized (3). Witness `starToughnessSba.test.js` (21), written before the engine change and run on the untouched archive: **14 fail there on assertions, the 7 controls pass on both** (Lumra at 2 damage, Tarmogoyf at 2 damage, an indestructible Darksteel Juggernaut under lethal damage, Boneyard Wurm at 2/2, the unsized Treefolk Seedlings and Souls of the Lost under 1 damage, Grizzly Bears). A/B **80 seeded commander games** (base seed 7, 10 per pod, the 30 profile decks, default AI; base = the untouched 4f5ccd5e archive): **77 byte-identical, 3 change picks**, 1 winner changes — all three in the Shorikai Vehicles pod, all Master of Etherium now destroyed by lethal damage it was dealt (it never died in the 80 base games): game 64 (turn 29, Thrun, Breaker of Silence fights it through Ulvenwald Tracker — winner Shorikai Vehicles → Thrun Voltron), game 68 (turn 23, it blocks a trampler and dies in combat; winner unchanged), game 69 (turn 22, Ancient Animus's fight; winner unchanged); results unchanged (ai-wins 57 / user-wins 23), 0 errors on either tree (236.8 s / 286.5 s). Lumra was not cast in these 80 games. Committed on `day/startough`, not pushed; the release-batch line and the WAKE-REPORT are the integrator's.
> · **The bug** (reproduced on 4f5ccd5e). `destroyLethalCreatures` skipped every printed creature whose printed toughness is not a number (`if (printedCreature && !Number.isFinite(Number(perm.card?.toughness))) continue;`), before both checks. The skip exists because `ptPrimitive` reads a printed `*` as 0: a creature whose CDA is unmodeled would die to a toughness it never had. But it skipped the creatures the layers DO size too. A census over the bundled corpus (each creature on a board with five Forests and a Grizzly Bears, 99 damage marked, the state-based check run): **0 of the 184** printed-`*`-toughness creatures died on base; 72 of the 73 sized ones die after (Darksteel Juggernaut is indestructible), none of the 111 unsized.
> · **The rules** (bundled CR, cited exactly). CR 208.2 / 208.2a — a `*` is set by a characteristic-defining ability; CR 604.3 — a CDA defines power or toughness; CR 613.4a — layer 7a applies it; CR 613.4b — layer 7b sets; CR 613.4d — 7d switches power and toughness; CR 704.5f — toughness 0 or less puts a creature into its owner's graveyard (indestructible doesn't stop it); CR 704.5g — lethal damage destroys it (CR 702.12b — indestructible does).
> · **The fix** — `layers.applyLayer7` tracks `powerSized` / `toughnessSized`: a printed number, a 7a `ptSetDynamicCount` that sets the value, or a 7b set (fixed or counted, gate open); a 7d switch swaps them. `deriveCharacteristics` carries both (the no-effect fast path from the printed value, the empty record false); `permanentToughnessSized(state, id)` reads it. `destroyLethalCreatures` skips a printed creature only while its toughness is unsized; an animated noncreature keeps its derived-value read. A layer-1 copy reads the copiable card for the printed value, as the derive does. ENGINE-SCAFFOLD §4.6 names the signal.
> · **Coverage (CREED).** No card loses credit: all 46 native printed-`*`-toughness creatures are sized (the classifier's static lane credits a clause through `clauseProducesStatic` — the same `parseClause` the layers read), and all 111 unsized ones are body-only. The census places an adventurer by its permanent face (`adventure.permanentFaceCard`, what a cast puts onto the battlefield): Beanstalk Giant and Cruel Somnophage are sized as cast (probed through a real cast). The witness pins the lockstep on seven real cards (five sized-and-native, two unsized-and-not).

The consumers pass it: `legalChoices.canPayAttackTax` (its cache keyed on player vs planeswalker), `applyDeclareAttacker`'s payment, and `attackRequirements.attackCostsNothing` — so `obeyingAttackOptions` and `requiredAttackerIds`, the offer's and the AI planner's one check, see a planeswalker behind Propaganda as free (a taxed option still never raises the bar and stays offered when it ties). The docs (this entry, CHANGELOG, ENGINE-SCAFFOLD) were written beside it — no test reads them. Lint 0 (CR citations: 0 of 12,057 name no rule; keyword citations: 0 of 2,453 cite a different keyword). Flip-diff **0 / 0 / RETIERED 0** (34,620 cards; before = an untouched `git archive` of 68d2a979, snapshotted before the first edit; native+land 15,631 of 34,584 snapshot names on both). **Mutants 8/8** on assertions, each restored byte-identical (sha256): every fight kept (11 tests red), a trade taken (1), a chain step without the fighter's own retrigger (1 — Kogla), an indestructible target counted as killable (1), the chain blind to the fighter's survival (1 — Autochthon Wurm), no synthesized decline under the 64-candidate cap (1), the backstop one resolution late (1), the backstop never preferring a player (3). Witness `optionalFightLoop.test.js` (19): the first 12 written before the engine change and run on the untouched archive — **9 fail there on assertions, the 3 controls pass on both**; the 7 added while building (the Spitemare / Boros Reckoner backstop through the engine, Gigantosaurus, Kogla, Autochthon Wurm) were run on the archive too — 6 fail there, the plain-Spitemare control passes on both (15 / 4 in all; the loop tests run under a resolution budget, so a loop fails an assertion instead of hanging the suite). A/B **80 seeded commander games** (base seed 7, 10 per pod, the 30 profile decks, default AI; base = the untouched 68d2a979 archive): **78 byte-identical, 2 change picks**, no winner changes — game 37 (Jurassic Ramp's Apex Altisaur, turn 35: it kills Neyith of the Dire Hunt and an earthbent Forest as on base, then declines the third fight, which on base killed it along with an earthbent Ba Sing Se) and game 57 (Test Rashmi's Kogla: its enters fight kills a Halfling token, where base fought a creature that killed Kogla and survived); results unchanged (ai-wins 57 / user-wins 23), 0 errors on either tree (374.2 s / 212.3 s). Supplement (not the A/B of record — the goad entry's: the same 80 games with Kardur, Doomscourge, Shiny Impetus, Coercive Impetus and Jeering Homunculus appended to every deck but Atraxa Superfriends): **engine-stuck 1 → 0** — game 37, the repro (Apex Altisaur, put onto the battlefield by Savage Order, fights 22 times — it kills earthbent lands of 2, 21, 30 and 82 toughness, Ancient Greenwarden, a Bear token and Toph, Earthbending Master, and leaves Lumra after two fights: a third is lethal by the rules, but the engine never destroys Lumra — found-not-fixed (1)), game 38 changes picks (the Altisaur declines a fourth fight that on base traded it for Shadow of Mortality; winner unchanged), 78 byte-identical (621.2 s / 315.3 s). Committed on `day/apexloop`, not pushed; the release-batch line and the WAKE-REPORT are the integrator's.
> · **The bug** (re-proved on 68d2a979 by rebuilding the supplement's game 37 alone). The α1 chooser (`gameEngine.chooseTriggerTargets`) takes the first correct-side candidate, and the expander lists an "up to one" decline LAST (targeting.js — "real targets come BEFORE the decline"), so an optional fight was always taken, against the first legal creature. Jurassic Ramp's Apex Altisaur was indestructible there; Earth Bent's Lumra, Bellow of the Woods (23/23, a CDA) took 10 damage a fight and never died — the lethal-damage state-based action skips a printed `*` toughness (found-not-fixed (1)) — each fight dealt the Altisaur 23, its enrage put the fight back on the stack, and the game burned the per-turn raw tick ceiling. Away from loops the same pick lost games: a plain Altisaur fought a 15/15 and died to it; Kogla fought whatever came first.
> · **The rules** (bundled CR, cited exactly). CR 115.6 — an ability that requires targets may allow zero to be chosen; CR 601.2c — a variable number of targets is announced, the choice the ability's controller makes as it goes on the stack (CR 603.3d). CR 701.14a/b — each fighter deals damage equal to its power; nothing fights if either is gone. CR 704.5g / 702.12b — lethal damage destroys, indestructible ignores it. CR 104.4b — "Loops that contain an optional action don't result in a draw"; CR 732.4 — only a loop of mandatory actions is (mandatoryLoop.js: an untargeted LINK chain — this loop is neither); CR 732.3 — in a fragmented loop a player "must then make a different game choice so the loop does not continue"; CR 732.2a — a shortcut names a number of iterations.
> · **The fix** — `triggerTargetRestraint.js` (new; gameState, layers, triggers, triggerRouting, the parser and effects/atoms/combat — no import of gameEngine), two restraints `chooseTriggerTargets` applies to its correct-side candidates. (1) `restrainOptionalFights`: each candidate's source-bound "fights up to one target" (atom `fight` + `optionalTarget`, the enchanted-host form too) is read by `fightWorthTaking`, which resolves the fight on a copy of the board with `fightCreature` itself (so indestructible, deathtouch, protection, prevention, infect, regeneration and the lethal pass all count) — taken when the target leaves and the fighter stays; or, both alive, as a chain step: the fighter was dealt damage, its own self "is dealt damage" trigger fights (routing natively — Apex Altisaur's enrage), the target is not indestructible and still has toughness left, and at this fight's rate it runs out first (an indestructible fighter never does). Every other candidate becomes its decline, synthesized from the first candidate when the expander's 64-candidate cap cut the decline off. Each chain step re-reads the live board, so a chain lasts only while the target's remaining toughness falls (82 toughness, 9 fights). (2) the LOOP BACKSTOP (`loopSpent` / `loopBreakingChoice`): once `abilityResolutionsThisTurn` (the per-turn ledger resolveTopOfStack keeps, keyed by source + sentence) holds `LOOP_ITERATIONS` (300) for the trigger's ability, the next choice declines its optional targets, else takes a candidate aimed only at players. 300 clears the busiest legitimate turn measured (236 resolutions of one ability — the Squirrel turn in learnSession's tick-budget note) and is a few thousand ticks under the 20,000 raw ceiling. ENGINE-SCAFFOLD §4.4 names the module.
> · **The human seat.** A triggered ability has no human target prompt: the chooser targets it for both seats (buildTriggerStack, gameEngine.js:1620–1646), so a person can't decline an "up to one" trigger target themselves (nor choose one) — found-not-fixed (2); with this fix their Apex Altisaur declines the same fights the AI's does.
> · **Reach** (bundled Commander-legal cards whose trigger routes natively): an optional source-bound fight 11 — Apex Altisaur (enters + enrage, the one enrage fighter), Kogla, Pheres-Band Brawler, Mind Meanderer, Wicked Wolf, Gargos, Vicious Watcher, Thorn Mammoth, Markov Enforcer and the Auras Pitiless Fists, Warbriar Blessing, Meltstrider's Resolve; self "is dealt damage" reflectors that can hit a creature 5 — Spitemare, Boros Reckoner, Needletooth Raptor, Red Hulk, Ill-Tempered Loner. Profile decks: Jurassic Ramp (Apex Altisaur), Omnath, Locus of Mana and Test Rashmi (Kogla), Zaxara (Gargos), Wolverine (Meltstrider's Resolve).
> · ⚠️ **Found, not fixed:** (1) **A creature with a printed `*` toughness never dies to lethal damage or to 0 toughness** — `destroyLethalCreatures` skips it before both checks (gameState.js:2926, `if (printedCreature && !Number.isFinite(Number(perm.card?.toughness))) continue;`), even when the layers size it: Lumra (23/23) carried 190 damage in the repro; probed on 68d2a979, Lumra at toughness 3 with 9 damage and at toughness 0 (no lands) both stay on the battlefield. Every */* CDA creature the engine sizes (Lumra, Tarmogoyf, Lhurgoyf, …) is immortal to damage and -X/-X — a false positive; the guard exists because an UNSIZED CDA reads toughness 0, so the fix needs a "sized" signal from layer 7a. (2) No human target prompt for triggered abilities (above). (3) The two-target "target creature you control fights up to one target creature you don't control" triggers (fight-pair — Favored Enemy, Yoshimaru, Amok Time, Arni Slays the Troll, Gimli's Reckless Might, Tolsimir) are not read: the first pair is still taken (no self-retrigger, so no loop). (4) A MANDATORY targeted loop with a single legal target each (two indestructible Needletooth Raptors, nothing else to target) is, by reading, a CR 104.4b draw that `mandatoryLoop.js` misses — its LINK rule takes only untargeted triggers — and the backstop has no different choice there; the tick ceiling still ends it engine-stuck. (5) A "you may" loop (CR 603.5, decided as it resolves — the autopilot takes every "may") is outside the backstop. (6) CR 732.3 names the active player (or the first involved in turn order) as the one to change; the backstop changes whichever ability reaches 300 first. (7) By reading, the expander's 64-candidate cap also drops the "up to one" decline from a person's spell targets (targeting.js:91 `MAX_CAST_EXPANSIONS`, the decline appended last at :462).
> · Witness: `optionalFightLoop.test.js` (19); `fightDamagePipeline.test.js` +1 (the decline) and its Kogla/Dawn Elemental witness re-pointed.

> ## 🔧 2026-10-18 — FIX (false positive / rules faithfulness): a leaves-the-battlefield watcher that leaves in the SAME event as the permanents it watches still triggers for each of them (CR 603.10a, 603.6c) — Marionette Apprentice (EDHREC #566, credited native) wiped together with an Ornithopter drained nothing; every "put into a graveyard from the battlefield" and "leaves the battlefield" watcher (`permanentLeaves` — artifact, creature-or-artifact, any player's artifact, enchantment, land, token, nontoken, "another") now looks back the way the death watchers have since P·34; a flickered watcher's new object no longer sees the leave (CR 400.7 — Ghostly Flicker gave Ninth Bridge Patrol two counters); and the two cards this parked play: Marionette Master (#1567) — "target opponent loses life equal to this creature's power", the power it last had when it left — and Disciple of the Vault (#2482) — "you may have target opponent lose 1 life" (+ Quill-Slinger Boggart) · **+3** · snapshot native+land 15,631 → 15,634

Game 33: the eliminated player's The Ozolith, leaving the game together with that player's creatures (CR 800.4a), now triggers by looking back and is dropped at once as a trigger of a departed player (CR 800.4d — one log line, `trigger-controller-left`); nothing else in the game moves. Game 44 (Halfshell heroes): Game Over destroys Rat King, Tokka & Rahzar and three more of its nontoken creatures — Rat King makes five Rats (one before), Tokka & Rahzar triggers once (a Treasure; its counter has nowhere to go) and latches the other three; 125 later picks move. Committed on `day/gylookback`, not pushed; the release-batch line and the WAKE-REPORT are the integrator's.
> · **The bug.** `checkLeavesTriggers` offered each leave event to the leaving permanent itself and to the battlefield only (triggers.js:8160–8163 at 68d2a979); a watcher that left in the same event was in neither. Measured on the archive: Akroma's Vengeance with Marionette Apprentice and an Ornithopter drains 0 (either battlefield order); Wicked Visitor with a Glorious Anthem 0; Titania with a Dryad Arbor (Day of Judgment) no Elemental; Evacuation with Nadier's Nightblade and two Servos 0; Rat King and a Bears bounced make 1 Rat. The bundled rulings: Marionette Master (2016-09-20) "If Marionette Master and an artifact you control are put into a graveyard at the same time, Marionette Master's ability triggers."; Disciple of the Vault (2020-08-07) — it "triggers for that artifact".
> · **The fix — departed watchers look back** (`triggers.departedLeaveSources` / `departedSaw`, the twin of P·34's `deadLookBackSources`). Each leave in a drain is offered to the drain's departed watchers that SAW it: the watcher was on the battlefield as it left — every leave event now records `boardBeforeIds`, the battlefield immediately before it (`gameState.recordLeaveEvent`, from the `before` board the exit already passes) — or both left in ONE event. The engine moves a wipe's permanents one at a time, so the board a later member left no longer holds an earlier one: `gameState.groupLeaveEvents(state, ids)` marks the members of one event with a shared `group` before the drain — `applyDestroyEffect` (every destroy: wipes, multi-target, Culling Ritual, Blood Money), `applyZoneMove` (mass bounce / exile / tuck), `applyBlink`'s exile, `costSacrifice.sacrificePermanentsTogether` (group sacrifices, Living Death, N-permanent costs) and every `checkDiesTriggers` death batch (SBA lethal damage, combat). A watcher that left in an earlier, separate event never sees a later leave (witnessed both ways with two separate moves). A permanent still on the battlefield stays the sweep's — never twice.
> · **The battlefield sweep is gated the same way:** a watcher not on that board never saw the leave — a flickered permanent is back as a NEW object (CR 400.7). On the archive Ghostly Flicker on Ninth Bridge Patrol and a Bears put two counters on the returned Patrol (it "saw" the Bears and its own old object leave); now the departed Patrol triggers once and its counter has nowhere to go. Emblems, an orphaned Aura's leave and a leave recorded without the board (synthetic test entries) keep the old offer.
> · **Orphaned Auras** (CR 704.5m): the engine moves an Aura whose host left at once; the rules move it as a state-based action AFTER the event. The leave is now marked `orphaned` (gameState.detachPermanentFromAll), and a departed watcher never sees it unless the event moved the Aura itself (Akroma's Vengeance destroys Pacifism too — Wicked Visitor drains for it, either order; Evacuation bounces Wicked Visitor and the Pacified Bears — no drain, either order). > · **The bug** (the value-creature entry's found-not-fixed (2) and (3), re-proved on 6cc20920 through the real offers). `pickAttackPlan`
>   filtered a goaded creature's options by the goader's seat id (`!goaders.has(o.defenderId)`), which keeps a non-goader's planeswalker,
>   and `chooseWalkerToKill` then took it: ai1's Bears wearing the user's Shiny Impetus attacked ai2's Jace (Kardur's rule the same);
>   goaded by every opponent, the filter fell back to every option and the walker kill took Jace again. The requirements lived only in the
>   planner, so the offer gave a person's goaded creature every target (the goader, a planeswalker), the play API accepted the attack at
>   the goader, intermediate difficulty's automatic attack took the first target (the goader), and the declaration could close with a
>   Bloodrock Cyclops or a goaded creature at home. Under Silent Arbiter the planner declared its listed-first creature, the cap closed the
>   declaration, and a must-attack creature never attacked (the A/B's game 62). And the planner forced a must-attack creature whose only
>   attacks were taxed: its controller paid Propaganda's {2} to send a 3/3 into a 6/4.
> · **The rules** (bundled CR and rulings, cited exactly). CR 508.1d — a declaration obeying fewer requirements than the maximum possible
>   without disobeying a restriction is illegal; a player is not required to pay a cost to obey one. Goad is CR 701.15 in the bundled rules
>   (the brief's 701.38b names no goad rule): 701.15b — "attacks each combat if able and attacks a player other than the controller of the
>   permanent, spell, or ability that caused it to be goaded if able"; 701.15c — several goaders, additional requirements; 701.15d — the
>   same player again, none. The goad rulings (Shiny Impetus, Disrupt Decorum, Agitator Ant, 2023-06-30): it must attack a player other
>   than the goader if able, else "a planeswalker an opponent controls, a battle an opponent controls, or a player who goaded it"; goaded
>   by each opponent, "the creature must attack an opponent (rather than a planeswalker or battle)"; a cost to attack a player is never
>   forced. Kardur's ruling (2021-02-05) is the same shape ("it must attack you or an opposing planeswalker").
> · **The fix** — `attackRequirements.js` (new leaf over layers, combatEvasion, attackTax, gameState), the one check: `obeyingAttackOptions`
>   (a creature's defenders narrowed to the ones obeying the most "other than X" requirements among the free options — a planeswalker obeys
>   none; a taxed option never raises the bar, stays offered when it ties), `requiredAttackerIds` (a live "attacks each combat if able" —
>   printed less its unless, the layer-6 grant, a forced-attack turn — and a free offered attack), `attackDeclarationOffer` (under an attack
>   cap with no more slots than owed creatures, only those). `layers.attackOtherThanRequirementsOf` counts the requirements (one per goader,
>   one per `requirementOnly` effect); `goaderControllersOf` reads the same grants, unchanged. legalChoices: every attacker's targets go
>   through `obeyingAttackOptions`, and while `required` is non-empty `legalActionsForPlayer` offers only attacker declarations (the pass,
>   a spell, an ability or a mana tap would each close the declaration). opponentAI: the forced set is `requiredAttackerIds`, the per-creature
>   pools are `obeyingAttackOptions` (a no-op on an offered set), the walker kill counts only creatures that may attack a planeswalker;
>   `selfMustAttack` moved to the leaf (re-exported). ENGINE-SCAFFOLD §4.8 names the module.
> · **Reach** (bundled Commander-legal cards by printed text): goad 82 (17 played natively — Shiny / Coercive / Parasitic Impetus, Jeering
>   Homunculus, Taunting Kobold, Alela, Cunning Conqueror, Redemption Arc, Fast Forward, Coronation of Chaos, Taunting Sliver …), Kardur's
>   rule 1, a self or granted "attacks each combat if able" 99 (53 native), a forced-attack turn 10, an attack cap 3 (Silent Arbiter,
>   Dueling Grounds, Caverns of Despair). Profile decks: Slivers (Bident of Thassa), Veyran Cantrips (Dragon's Rage
>   Channeler), Hulk Smash (Hulk, Brutal Brawler; Hulk, Always Angry), Thrun Voltron (Toski), Halfshell heroes (Fast Forward); caps in
>   Light-Paws Voltron, Nekusar Wheels, Atraxa Superfriends; taxes in Nekusar Wheels and Atraxa Superfriends.
> · ⚠️ **Found, not fixed:** (1) **A "can't attack you" tax is charged on attacks at that player's planeswalkers** — `attackTaxDetail` /
>   `attackTaxToDeclare` (attackTax.js:116, :96) are keyed on the defending player, so Propaganda, Ghostly Prison and Windborn Muse price an
>   attack on their controller's planeswalker as well (legalChoices `canPayAttackTax`, actionDispatcher `applyDeclareAttacker`'s payment);
>   only the "you or planeswalkers you control" printing (Baird, Archon of Absolution, Sphere of Safety) reaches one. The planeswalker
>   attack is withheld when the tax is unaffordable (FN) or charged when it should be free. (2) Per-defender attack caps (Crawlspace) are
>   not modelled (staticAbilityParser.js:3235); if one is, the module's creature-by-creature narrowing (each creature's defender choice

>   costs to attack); the tax is a cost to attack, CR 508.1h (legalChoices.js:43, attackTax.js:2). (6) Pre-existing turn stall, seen only in
>   the supplement (seed 3724842652; Wolverine, claws out! / Jurassic Ramp / Earth Bent / Believe it!), identical on 6cc20920: Jurassic

Murder Investigation's "its" (the enchanted creature) is never rewritten — parked.

The sourcePower reader answered 0 for a source gone while its ability waited — Krenko removed in response made no Goblins. `gameState.stampAbilitySourceLki` now also stamps every stack ability whose program reads sourcePower (`programReadsSourcePower`) and every waiting trigger whose effect clause names "this creature's power", with `power` on the record (`abilitySourceRecord`); `countForSpec` reads it for that id only, after the sacrifice-cost and dies look-backs.
> · **"exile target card from a graveyard", mandatory.** Its target intent was "ambiguous" ("it could be forced onto its own side"), parking every such trigger. Since the forced-target pick (2026-10-16) that is the rule — a mandatory trigger takes a legal target (CR 603.3d) — so the single mandatory form reads "enemy" (programQueries): an opponent's card when there is one, else the forced pick's least valuable card of its controller's (witnessed: the Island before the Grizzly Bears, logged `trigger-target-forced`); every graveyard empty, nothing happens. A multi-target mandatory form stays ambiguous.
> · **"If it was a <type> card" / "If a <type> card is (was) exiled this way".** parseEffectClauseImpl collapses the exile and its payoff into one program: the payoff atoms carry `ifExiledCardType`, and runEffectProgram runs them only when that exile moved a card of the type (read in its owner's exile zone, front face — CR 712.8a; "permanent" is CR 110.4a's six). The payoff must be non-targeting, non-optional and non-pausing and the exile non-optional ("you may exile …" stays unread). Scavenging Ooze's ruling witnessed: the target gone at resolution, no counter and no life (CR 608.2b); two activations on one creature card, only the first does anything. Twins: Diregraf Scavenger, Raven Eagle, Ignis Scientia (and Feral Appetite's, General's Enforcer's, Mastermind Plum's and Graveyard Trespasser's abilities now read — those cards stay parked on other lines).
> · **"another <Subtype> you control dies"** → `otherSubtypeYouControl` on the dies event (the enters scope: the dead creature carries the subtype — a changeling counts —, its controller is the watcher's, and it isn't the watcher). The rulings witnessed: Plague Belcher dying beside another Zombie still triggers for it, once.
> · **Tests changed on purpose (pins graduated / re-pointed):** graveyardExileUpToOne.test.js — "Diregraf Scavenger still parks", "the MANDATORY … stays with the Arbiter", "the mandatory form → ambiguous" now assert native / native / enemy; gyExileOpponent.test.js — "from a graveyard stays AMBIGUOUS" now asserts enemy (and a two-target mandatory form ambiguous); forcedTriggerTarget.test.js — Return to Nature's modal trigger: with only your own artifacts and a Forest in your graveyard the forced pick now exiles the Forest (mana value 0) rather than destroying Sol Ring, and with only the graveyard mode it is forced onto the Forest; the two original assertions ("never the Forest", "the Arbiter no-op") are kept on a modal whose third mode is still ambiguous (Return to Nature's two destroy modes with Vessel of Endless Rest's "put target card from a graveyard on the bottom of its owner's library"); modalChooseOnePartial.test.js — its synthetic ambiguous mode moves from "Exile target card from a graveyard." to the same bottom-of-library instruction (10 lines; Dawnbringer Cleric and Cleanup Crew keep their printed text and stay native). Each graduated assertion fails on the archive on an assertion; the re-pointed ones pass on both.
> · **Programs that move on cards still parked (16):** triggers that now route and run in a game — Brimaz, King of Oreskos and Sigiled Sword of Valeron ("…token with vigilance that's attacking", untapped), Squee, Dubious Monarch, Mastermind Plum's attack trigger, Graveyard Trespasser's, The Great Goblin's dies trigger (another Goblin, Orc or Army); activations now read — Feral Appetite, General's Enforcer; detected but unread (manual, as an undetected trigger was nothing) — Aatchik, Ajani, Nacatl Pariah (a diesBatch with the new scope), Idol of False Gods, Syrix, Wilhelt, Zask; Undercellar Sweep and Battle Cry Goblin parse HIGH but don't route (the defender gate; pack tactics).

(5) The "Otherwise, …" branch after the exiled-type gate is unread (Cling to Dust, Klothys). (6) Faerie Bladecrafter's "each opponent loses X life and you gain X life, where X is its power" (dies) and Rapacious Guest's "loses life equal to its power" (leaves — leave events record no power) unread. > · **The conditional tap augment** (`whenProduces` — staticAbilityParser.parseGlobalTapManaAugment → manaModel.globalTapManaAugment):
>   Forsaken Monument ("Whenever you tap a permanent for {C}, add an additional {C}."), Caged Sun ("Whenever a land's ability causes you to
>   add one or more mana of the chosen color, add an additional one mana of that color.", controller-scoped) and Gauntlet of Power
>   ("Whenever a basic land is tapped for mana of the chosen color, its controller adds an additional one mana of that color.", any player):
>   the extra mana is added only when the tap's own mana includes that colour (Forsaken Monument's rulings: a {T} mana ability only, only if
>   it produces {C}, one additional {C} however many it made). "Chosen" resolves off the carrier's `chosenColor`, only on a card that prints
>   the chooser. manaSources drops the bonus from a record that can't make its colour; planPaymentCore's `tapSource` credits it only when
>   the primary's colour (or a fixed bundle) holds it, and a generic tap's primary prefers a colour that triggers one (Breeding Pool under a
>   green Caged Sun taps {G}{G} for {2}); `manualManaTaps` attaches it per colour; commitManaTap adds exactly the plan's picks. Each new
>   parse arm has its $-anchored line in `stripGlobalTapManaAugment`.

>   adds an additional {G} / {R}"), whatever the land was tapped for (the Gauntlet of Might ruling: a dual with Mountain among its types makes
>   the extra {R} for either colour); Lavaleaper's basic-land Mana Flare line (`basic-land` + sameAsProduced). A fixed bonus that makes the
>   wanted colour now takes it while the primary pays another still-needed colour (`bonusTakesWant`): one Breeding Pool under Vernal Bloom

>   `{ controller, subject, allPlayers, colors, amount, turn }` in `state.tapManaAugmentsEot`; globalTapManaAugment reads only this turn's
>   entries (CR 514.2). Per the rulings, an Island that entered after it resolved counts, and so does any land with the Island type.

>   The draw line's "Spend only mana of the chosen color to activate this ability." is peeled by abilities.js (`spendOnlyChosenColor`, only

> ## 🔧 2026-10-17 — FIX (engine rules): a player leaving a multiplayer game follows CR 800.4a — the control effects giving them control end first (a creature they took with Control Magic, Act of Treason or Sliver Overlord goes to the player beneath; it vanished with them), every object they own leaves the game wherever it is (a creature of theirs another player had stolen, their Aura on another player's creature, a card of theirs another player was casting — all stayed), their abilities, spell copies and waiting triggers cease to exist (CR 800.4d), and what they still control is exiled to its owners' exile (a creature they reanimated from another player's graveyard — it vanished); their Banishing Light returns the card it held (CR 610.3) while an Oblivion Ring's triggered return does not; other players' Equipment and Auras come off their creatures; the monarch passes to the active player (CR 725.4); an extra turn queued for them is skipped (CR 800.4k) · **±0** · snapshot native+land 15,531 unchanged
> Suite **20,880 green (1 skipped) / 1,884 files** under the gate queue (with the rules index built for the run, then deleted). Lint 0
> (CR citations: 0 of 11,727 name no rule; keyword citations: 0 of 2,383 cite a different keyword). Flip-diff **0 / 0 / RETIERED 0**
> (34,620 cards; before = an untouched `git archive` of 80b09e9e, snapshotted before the first edit; native+land 15,531 of 34,584 snapshot
> names on both). **Mutants 6/6** on assertions, each restored byte-identical (sha256): `releaseControlOnLeave` keeping the leaver's own
> stashed home (2 tests red), no `defaultController` stamp in `moveControl` (2), only the leaver's own battlefield leaving (2 — the
> stolen Griffin, the stolen Drone token), stack spells judged by controller alone (2), no CR 800.4d gate in `flushTriggers` (1 — the
> logged drop), the two-trigger detain return handed to a seated player too (1 — Oblivion Ring). Witness `playerLeavesGame.test.js`
> written first: the first 18 run on the untouched 80b09e9e archive — **14 fail on assertions, the 4 controls pass**; with the three added
> while building (the stolen Drone token, the leaver's own Drone token, Oblivion Ring), **16 of the final 21 fail on the archive on
> assertions, the 5 controls pass on both**. A/B **80 seeded commander games** (base seed 7, 10 per pod, the 30 profile decks, default AI;
> base = the untouched 80b09e9e archive): **74 / 80 byte-identical**; the other **6 change no decision** (every row's action, the winner,
> result and turn count identical) — 4 log a dropped leaves trigger of the departed player's own permanent (Watcher for Tomorrow, Cryogen
> Relic, Detention Sphere, Skyclave Apparition; base never recorded the leave, and `orderTriggersAPNAP` would have dropped them silently),
> and in 2 a survivor's Aura on the departed player's creature (Swift Reconfiguration and Detainment Spell; Kenrith's Transformation) goes
> to the graveyard as they leave instead of at the next state-based check (one decision row's `own_permanents` feature differs). 0 errors
> on either tree, results unchanged (ai-wins 60 / user-wins 20), 185 s / 179 s. **158 eliminations** on both trees; **in none was a stolen
> or borrowed object involved** — measured on base with a scratch instrumentation at each elimination (80 / 80 games reproduced): no
> permanent the leaver owned on another battlefield, none another player owned on theirs, no control effect giving them control, no
> cross-owner spell on the stack. No profile deck casts a theft card the engine models (the control-timestamp entry's census).
> Committed on `day/leavegame`, not pushed; the release-batch line and the WAKE-REPORT are the integrator's.
> · **The bug.** `learnSession.removePlayerFromGame` deleted the leaving player's record — their whole battlefield with it — and filtered
>   the stack by controller. Reproduced on 80b09e9e through the session's real elimination (advanceUntilDecision): a creature the leaver
>   held with Control Magic, Act of Treason or Sliver Overlord vanished (CR 800.4a's own examples: it reverts); the leaver's creature
>   another player stole with Mind Control stayed, the Aura on it; the leaver's Pacifism left a dangling id in its host's `attachments`
>   (read by Reyav-style "enchanted or equipped" gates); another player's Bonesplitter on the leaver's creature kept `attachedTo` pointing
>   at nothing and their Pacifism on it stayed on the battlefield until a later check; a card of the leaver's that another player was
>   casting (Ragavan's permission) stayed on the stack, and another player's card the leaver was casting vanished; a creature the leaver
>   reanimated from another player's graveyard vanished (owned by that player: CR 800.4a exiles it); the leaver's waiting trigger stayed
>   queued; a card their Banishing Light held stayed exiled for good; the monarch stayed with the departed seat (nobody could take the
>   crown again); an extra turn queued for them began with them as the active player.
> · **The fix** (`playerLeavesGame.js`, new — learnSession imports it). In CR 800.4a's order: ① the control effects giving the leaver
>   control end first, while they are still seated (`controlMove.releaseControlOnLeave`: the latest remaining effect's controller, else
>   `controlOriginal` unless it is the leaver, else the default controller unless it is the leaver; nobody → it stays for ③). The default
>   controller (CR 110.2) is a new stamp, `defaultController`, that `moveControl` writes on a permanent's first move — the seat it left —
>   so a permanent the leaver controls by default (exiled) is told apart from one an effect gave them (released). Then every permanent the
>   leaver owns, on any battlefield, leaves through `gameState.removePermanentFromGame` (the battlefield exit without a landing: the
>   nonland-left stamp, the trigger look-backs, `detachPermanentFromAll` — attachments fall off, a control Aura releases its host, leave
>   events record so leaves-the-battlefield abilities trigger, CR 603.6c), attachments first; each spell they own leaves the stack. ② Their
>   abilities and spell copies on the stack cease to exist; their waiting and delayed triggers go; `flushTriggers` drops (and logs) any
>   later trigger a departed player would control (CR 800.4d). ③ What they still control is exiled to its owners' exile by the ordinary
>   zone move; a spell they are casting that another player owns goes to its owner's exile. Phased-out permanents: theirs leave every
>   list (CR 702.26k), another player's on their list is exiled. Then the seat (turn order, combat, commander damage — now also from a
>   commander of theirs on another battlefield or the stack — the player-Aura sweep, the monarch via `becomeMonarch`, priority to the next
>   seat in turn order, CR 800.4a). The driver re-runs the SBA check after a removal before anyone gets priority (CR 704.3 — the leave
>   triggers reach the queue first); simultaneous leavers go active player last; `advanceStep` skips an extra turn of a departed player
>   (CR 800.4k). A detainer's return (CR 610.3 — a one-shot, not a trigger) whose controller has left goes to the active player
>   (`checkLeavesTriggers`); the two-trigger printing `foldTwoTriggerDetain` rewrites (Oblivion Ring, Journey to Nowhere) returns with a
>   triggered ability, so it keeps its departed controller and is dropped (`triggers.detainReturnIsTriggered`). A `left-game-objects`
>   log entry names what crossed between players (none in a plain elimination).
> · **Reach.** Every 4-player game with an elimination (158 in the 80 A/B games). The cards whose leave behaviour changes: the 14 control
>   Auras and 15 native threatens of the control-timestamp entry, Sliver Overlord, Hellkite Tyrant, Homeward Path (what they took goes
>   back), every reanimation of another player's creature, every Banishing-Light-style "until" detainer (its card returns) and every
>   leaves-the-battlefield watcher a survivor controls. No tier moves (flip-diff 0).
> · **Tests changed on purpose:** none. Comments updated where they named the old location (`adelineResplendentCathar.test.js`,
>   `ownerZoneRouting.test.js` — its stale-owner board is now built by hand; the fallback it pins stays as the never-throw guard).
> · **Judgement calls:** (1) The leaver's own leave triggers and an Oblivion Ring's return are dropped (CR 800.4d) — the A/B shows
>   `orderTriggersAPNAP` already dropped such triggers silently; the gate makes the drop visible. (2) An attack on the leaver is still
>   removed from combat (base behaviour; CR 800.4e only says no damage is assigned to them). (3) Priority the leaver held passes to the
>   next seat (CR 800.4a); the pass count still restarts, so players who had passed are asked again. (4) The Ragavan permission stamp and
>   a pre-attached Bonesplitter are staged; every other steal, cast and elimination goes through the engine's real entry points. (5) The
>   detain return's stack controller, when its own has left, is the active player (CR 610.3c makes the controller irrelevant to where the
>   card goes). (6) Survivor-controlled leaves triggers of the leaver's objects now fire (the stolen Drone token's drain), per CR 603.6c.
> · ⚠️ **Found, not fixed:** (1) CR 800.4c — a permanent the leaver controlled by default, held by another player's temporary effect when
>   they leave, stays with its holder when that effect ends (`controlMove.endControlEffects`' pinned fallback); the rule exiles it.
>   (2) CR 800.4g — a pending resolution-time choice of the leaver's (`state.pendingDiscover` / `state.pendingChoice`, settled in
>   learnSession.advanceUntilDecision) is not handed to another player; the settlers assume the seat exists. (3) CR 800.4j — the active
>   player leaving still cuts the turn short (`playerLeavesGame.js` active branch, the B3 simplification). (4) CR 800.4m — the leaver's
>   "until your next turn" effects end at once (`gameState.expireDamageReplacementEffects`). (5) Another player's Aura or Equipment that
>   phased out with a leaver's permanent (a CR 702.26g rider) is lost with the leaver's phased-out list (CR 702.26n). (6) The initiative
>   (CR 726.4) is not modelled.
> · Witness: `playerLeavesGame.test.js` (21 — 16 witnesses, 5 controls).

>   pump/grant 539 (355) → 0; tap/untap 555 (255) → 3 (Candelabra of Tawnos ×2, the mana-untap line; Maze of Ith, combat); counters 354
>   (177) → 0; bounce 59 (35) → 0; graveyard 135 (91) → 0; Equip 1,155 → 95 (`pickEquipAction`); other 1,029 (462) → 0. So the reported gap
>   was real for every main-phase kind; the AI already used Equip, combat-role and Candelabra activations.
> · **The policy** — `opponentAI.pickTargetedActivation`, in the ability block after the fetch crack and before the generic picker; own main
>   phase, stack empty (the engine offers non-combat activations there only); the program's one targeted atom read off the parse, its other
>   atoms gains only (gain life, each opponent loses life, draw, scry, surveil, a +1/+1 counter on the source — an "Add" holds). Costs: tap
>   and/or mana; one +1/+1 counter off a source that survives it, for a kill or removal only (Walking Ballista, Steelbane Hydra); a
>   noncreature token whose one activated ability this is, sacrificed for a +1/+1 counter only (Mutagen). Tiers: (4) damage / -N/-N / -1/-1
>   counter that kills an opponent's creature (toughness against the damage marked; an indestructible creature only when its toughness reaches 0) or
>   planeswalker, destroy / exile of an opponent's permanent (no compensating `controllerRider`, no `diesCopyRider`), a fight-pair through
>   the cast path's `chooseDisciplinedVariant` — biggest power, then `permanentValue`; (3) an opponent's graveyard card exiled beside a gain
>   rider; (2) a +1/+1 counter on its own biggest creature, an opponent's graveyard card alone when its owner could use it (a creature card or
>   a graveyard keyword), and in the precombat main haste for its own summoning-sick creature and "can't be blocked" for its own ready
>   attacker while the defender has an untapped creature (the source's tap never costs a bigger attacker); (1.5 / 1) postcombat only, a shot
>   that kills nothing at an opponent's planeswalker, then the living opponent with the least life — a creature source holds it under
>   `LIFE_PRUDENCE_FLOOR` (10) or while `clearlyBehindOnBoard` (the tap costs its blocks until its untap step). Deterministic: tier, value,
>   name, permanent id, ability index, target id. Policy key `target` ("v1" = the old skip) joins POLICY_KEYS.
> · **After (the same 80 games, instrumented):** damage 4 → 15 (Ulvenwald Tracker 7 — its fighter 6/6 to 37/26 against targets of toughness 1–5, each a fight it wins and survives;
>   Walking Ballista 4 — Squirrel, Birds of Paradise, Halfling, Rosie Cotton, the Ballista 4/4 or bigger; Balduvian Trading Post 4),
>   destroy/exile 0 → 6 (Steelbane Hydra: Talisman of Creativity, Mind Stone, Aggravated Assault, Branching Evolution, Everflowing Chalice,
>   Esper Sentinel — the Hydra 2/2 or bigger), counters 0 → 21 (Simic Ascendancy 11 on Ms. Bumbleflower, Mutagen 10), graveyard 0 → 10
>   (Deathrite 9 — drains over Akroma's Will, Three Steps Ahead, Riot Control, Dispel …, gains over Seedborn Muse, Kogla, Spore Frog;
>   Paleontologist 1 — Neyith of the Dire Hunt), pump/grant 0 → 3 (Otepec Huntmaster: Kinjalli's Sunwing, Wayward Swordtooth; Manifold Key:
>   Blightsteel Colossus), tap/untap 3 → 3, Equip 95 → 95, bounce and other 0 → 0. Every new activation landed on the right side (damage,
>   removal and graveyard at an opponent's; counters and grants on its own): 51 new, 0 at its own permanents.
> · ⚠️ **Found, not fixed:** (1) Every non-combat activation is offered in its controller's own main phase only (legalChoices.js:2448
>   `mainWindow`): no end-of-turn ping, no pump after blocks — so the +N/+N and keyword pumps stay skipped (Nylea 15, Kessig Wolf Run 27 on
>   the {X} lane, Hidden Hideout 35, Herd Heirloom 67 own-main offers). (2) Deathrite's mana ability ({T}: exile a land card, add one mana —
>   33 own-main offers) holds: after the casts its mana would empty; the shape is a ramp reading before the casts (activate when its mana
>   casts a held card), as `pickFetchCrack` does for lands. (3) Walking Ballista shoots only to kill (a face ping would spend its body); a
>   counter-rich Ballista's postcombat face ping is the follow-up. (4) Self-sacrifice, life and other costs stay skipped: Haywire Mite,

>   (sacrifice another), Exploding Barrel, Aetherflux Reservoir (50 life), Eriette's Tempting Apple, Atzocan Seer, Grim Hireling (X
>   Treasures). (5) Tap / untap: Thassa, Deep-Dwelling (45) and Staff of Domination (21) could tap the defender's best blocker precombat;
>   the land-untap lines (Deserted Temple, Arbor Elf, Earthcraft, Minamo, Oboro Breezecaller, Formidable Speaker, Manifold Key's untap)
>   need the mana-untap line's reading (manaUntapLine.js reads Candelabra only). (6) Bounce is offered on its own creatures only (Dour

> ## 🔧 2026-10-17 — FIX (false positive): control changes apply in timestamp order (CR 613.1b, 613.7) — Act of Treason then Control Magic keeps the creature under the Aura past cleanup (it went home), Control Magic then a threaten-back returns it to the Control Magic player at cleanup (it went to the owner), Act of Treason then Sliver Overlord keeps it for good (the Hellkite Tyrant entry's found-not-fixed (4)), two control Auras hand the host to the earlier one when the later goes (the pinned simplification), a control Aura destroyed under a live threaten leaves the threatener holding it until cleanup, and Illusory Gains moving onto a new creature (or Codsworth moving a control Aura) releases the creature it held — it stayed stolen for good · **±0** · snapshot native+land 15,531 unchanged

> different keyword). Flip-diff **0 / 0 / RETIERED 0** (34,620 cards; before = an untouched `git archive` of d94d164b, snapshotted before
> the first edit; native+land 15,531 of 34,584 snapshot names on both). **Mutants 6/6** on assertions, each restored byte-identical
> (sha256): the record single-level (6 tests red), an ended effect straight home (9), an indefinite steal keeping the record (4), an
> already-controlling effect never recorded (1), a moved Aura's old effect left in place (2 — Codsworth, Illusory Gains), Homeward Path

> count; the two 127 MB result files differ only in their wall-clock field), 0 errors on either tree, results unchanged (ai-wins 60 / user-wins 20), 176 s / 176 s per batch — no control change happens in
> any of the 80 games (the only theft-text card cast is Eriette's Tempting Apple, games 51 and 59, whose steal is unmodelled).

> · **The bug.** Every control change goes through `controlMove.moveControl`, but the history of WHY a permanent was held was one
>   level deep: `controlOriginal` plus either `controlUntilEndOfTurn: true` (the threaten, 1760fe36) or `controlStolenBy: <Aura>` (the
>   control Auras, 0c19d9c0). The cleanup sweep sent anything flagged straight to `controlOriginal`, the Aura revert likewise, and the
>   indefinite steal and the Aura attach carried the other's flag along untouched. Probed on d94d164b (all through real casts): Act of
>   Treason then Control Magic — at cleanup the creature went home with the Aura still attached (same player or another; the Aura's
>   attach was a no-op for the same player, so the threaten's flag decided); Control Magic then Act of Treason — at cleanup it went to the
>   owner (the sweep sent it to `controlOriginal`, the owner, past the Aura still attached); Act of Treason then Sliver Overlord — the
>   atom skipped an already-controlled target (`from === controller`) or moved it with the flag, and cleanup reverted the permanent
>   steal (the Hellkite Tyrant entry's found-not-fixed (4): effects/atoms/control.js:165); Control Magic, a third player's Act of Treason,
>   the Aura destroyed — the creature went home at once instead of staying with the threatener until cleanup (and the reverse order the
>   same); two control Auras — removing the later sent the host home past the earlier (pinned in controlAura.test.js as a known
>   simplification since 2026-07-29); **Illusory Gains** ("Whenever a creature an opponent controls enters, attach this Aura to that
>   creature.", native-trigger) and a control Aura moved by Codsworth — `attachPermanent` detached the Aura from its old host
>   without ending its effect, so the first creature stayed stolen for good and the second was stolen too.
> · **The fix (CR 613.1b, 613.7).** controlMove.js owns a control-effect record per permanent: `controlEffects` — the temporary effects
>   on it, oldest first, `{to, until: "end-of-turn"}` (a threaten, ends in the cleanup step, CR 514.2) or `{to, aura}` (a control Aura,
>   ends when it stops being attached; a re-attach is a new timestamp, CR 613.7e) — over `controlOriginal` (who controls it once they
>   have all ended). Three writers, nothing else touches the fields: `addControlEffect` (a threaten, an Aura attaching — its player
>   controls it now; not recorded when nothing beneath it can end and its player already has it), `endControlEffects` (the cleanup sweep,
>   an Aura leaving through the battlefield-exit chokepoint, an Aura moved off by `attachPermanent` — the permanent goes to the latest
>   remaining effect's controller, else home; a player who has left is skipped, CR 800.4a; if none is left it stays), and
>   `gainControlIndefinitely` (Sliver Overlord, Hellkite Tyrant, Homeward Path / Trostani Discordant — no duration, CR 611.2a, later
>   than everything on the permanent, so the record is cleared). The single-target atom no longer skips a target it already controls
>   when a temporary effect holds it, and Homeward Path also takes a creature its owner holds only through a temporary effect (an owner
>   who threatened it back from a Control Magic keeps it past cleanup — the base got this right by accident, and the record would
>   otherwise have handed it to the Aura's controller). A pre-record save's `controlUntilEndOfTurn` / `controlStolenBy` is read as the
>   equivalent list (pinned). `playability-sweep.mjs` counts Aura entries instead of `controlStolenBy`.
> · **Reach.** The bundled cards whose modelled control change now behaves differently in these interactions — 34 native: the 15
>   native threatens (Act of Treason, Traitorous Blood, Turn Against, Portent of Betrayal, Vengeful Possession, Pack's Betrayal, Lose
>   Calm, Involuntary Employment, Song-Mad Treachery, Limits of Solidarity, Bloody Betrayal, Twisted Fealty, Press into Service,
>   Tentative Connection, Sarkhan Vol), the 14 control Auras (Control Magic, Mind Control, Treachery, Persuasion, Corrupted Conscience,
>   Mind Harness, Threads of Disloyalty, Yavimaya's Embrace, Spirit Away, Biting Tether, Binding Grasp, Vapor Snare, Mark of the Oni,
>   Illusory Gains) and Hypnotic Siren (bestowed), Sliver Overlord, Hellkite Tyrant (no visible change: its clear already made a later
>   Aura revert a no-op), Homeward Path and Trostani Discordant; plus Codsworth, Handy Helper as the mover. No tier moves (flip-diff 0).
>   Profile decks: The Unbeatable Squirrel Girl holds Homeward Path; Captain America and Light-Paws hold Codsworth but no control Aura;
>   Bumble Flower Combo holds Eriette's Tempting Apple, whose steal is unmodelled (body-only). No theft deck is added (the 08-15 veto).
> · **Tests changed on purpose:** `controlAura.test.js`'s "⚠️ KNOWN SIMPLIFICATION" pin (two Auras → home) now asserts the CR answer (the
>   first Aura's controller, then home when it goes too) — fails on the archive; `threatenControl.test.js`'s stamp assertion reads
>   `controlEffects` instead of `controlUntilEndOfTurn`.
> · **Judgement calls:** (1) Act of Treason stands in for "Threaten" — Threaten's own text ("Untap target creature and gain control of it
>   until end of turn") is not read (arbiter-spell), Act of Treason is the native member. (2) The indefinite single-target steal is
>   witnessed with Sliver Overlord — Agent of Treachery ("gain control of target permanent") is body-only. (3) The pod cases make the
>   casting seat active for its sorcery-speed cast. (4) An effect that gives control to whoever already has it, with nothing beneath it,
>   is not recorded — equivalent at every later point, and it keeps an Aura on its own controller's creature stash-free. (5) The Aura
>   revert no longer asks `isControlAuraPermanent`: only an Aura that took the host has an entry there.
> · ⚠️ **Found, not fixed:** (1) `removePlayerFromGame` (learnSession.js:414) drops the leaving player's whole battlefield — a creature
>   they had stolen vanishes instead of reverting (CR 800.4a's own examples: Mind Control, Act of Treason), and what they OWN under
>   another player's control stays in the game. (2) A control Aura's entry keeps the player who controlled it at attach: if control of
>   the Aura itself changed, the host would not follow (no modelled effect gains control of an Aura today). (3) A bestowed Aura on a host
>   that becomes illegal stays attached (sba.js:77 — CR 702.103f: it becomes unattached), so a bestowed Hypnotic Siren keeps a host that

> · **The bug** (found in the graveyard-exile slice; measured on ee70e7d9). The planner skipped `cost.phyrexian` ("assumed paid with
>   life") and no cast or activation charged the life: Dismember off one Island cost the Island and nothing else, Gitaxian Probe was free,
>   Immolating Souleater pumped for nothing, Lashwrithe equipped for nothing. A hybrid Phyrexian symbol ({G/U/P}) was parsed as plain

>   Noxious Revival, Phyrexian Metamorph, Pith Driller, Porcelain Legionnaire, Slash Panther, Spined Thopter, Tezzeret's Gambit, Thundering

> · **The fix** (manaModel). `planWithPhyrexian` wraps planPayment and canAfford: the fewest symbols in life first (none, one, two … —
>   each set of that size in symbol order), every other symbol turned into its coloured pip (a hybrid one into a hybrid pip), so mana pays
>   whenever it can; the life is a base claim of the payment (consumedClaimsPayable — beside a Mana Confluence's life, at least 1 left; the
>   claims ride the passes into the core and the costed path); it needs the payer's life in the spend context (`lifePaymentContext` —
>   `life`, `lifeLocked`), and with none a symbol needs its mana (never free). The plan's `phyrexianLife` is charged by commitPaymentPlan
>   (loseLife, a `phyrexian-life` log line). payManaCost passes the life and no longer reads a lone {W/P} as an empty cost. parseManaCost
>   keeps a hybrid Phyrexian symbol as one Phyrexian entry ("G/U").
> · **The paths.** The dispatcher's cast and activation (Equip included) pass the payer's life; the attack tax pays Norn's Annex through
>   payManaCost — the second copy (all-mana, else all-life) is gone, and legalChoices withholds on the same planner. The offer's cast and
>   activation contexts carry the life (X spells too); the new last pass `withPhyrexianPayment` prices each Phyrexian cast/activation with
>   the payment's own plan (`offeredPaymentPlan`, shared with withPayableConsumedCosts), drops the unpayable and stamps `phyrexianLife`;
>   the label names it ("pay 4 life for its Phyrexian mana"); opponentAI.pickAction drops a stamped action that would leave it below

>   "at 1 or 2 life withheld; at 3 offered, the attacker goes to 1": the Annex pip now follows the engine's policy for every life payment
>   (paying to exactly 0 is legal, CR 119.4, and loses the game).
> · **Mutants (11/11 on assertions):** the planner skipping the symbols; no life lane; the commit not charging; the life no claim of the
>   payment; the life lock ignored; life paid down to 0; hybrid Phyrexian read as hybrid; the AI paying below the floor; a lone pip read
>   as an empty cost (killed by the Norn's Annex tests); no stamp; life tried before mana.
> · **⚑ Judgment calls.** (1) Mana first, fewest life — the engine never pays life a board could pay in mana; a person who wants to keep a
>   land up can't choose life instead (auto-payment only). (2) The policy keeps 1 life per payment, Phyrexian life included: Dismember
>   off an Island at 4 life is not offered (legal per CR 119.4, but it loses the game). (3) The AI's floor (10) is its existing life floor;
>   at 11 life it holds Vault Skirge off an Island. (4) Compleated (CR 702.150a: two fewer loyalty counters per symbol paid with life) is
>   not modeled — those walkers don't resolve today, so paying their cost with life grants nothing; it must come with their resolution.

>     in 53, 0 errors. Counterfactual: land drops 164 of 1,290 (61 games; 108 fetch/SNC, 56 ordinary), tapped-delivery fetch with another
>     land offered 38 → 11; **searches: 42 of 389 land searches take a different land** (Farseek 9 of 11, Nature's Lore 7 of 15, Cultivate
>     5 of 20, Three Visits 5 of 11, Crop Rotation 4 of 4, Sylvan Scrying 3 of 4, Sowing Mycospawn 3 of 3, Kodama's Reach 2 of 10, Rampant
>     Growth 2 of 14, Everything Pizza 2 of 3), **0 of 137 non-land searches**, and 0 fetch-land searches (they already read this order).
>   · **part 2 on top of part 1:** 55 byte-identical, 25 change picks — every first divergence a search — 7 winners change, 0 errors.
>   · Observed in the batches (not counterfactual): a tapped-delivery fetch played as the land drop 34 (21 with another land offered) → 31
>     (12) → 31 (11); untapped-delivery fetches dropped 179 → 166 → 161; fetch cracks 207 → 189 → 186 (fewer dead fetches played). Results
>     ai-wins 54 → 59 → 60 / user-wins 26 → 21 → 20 (an outcome, not the grade); 171 / 173 / 168 s per batch. No profile deck holds an SNC
>     family land, so its tapped reading is witnessed by the unit tests only. Committed on `day/landseq`, not pushed; the release-batch line
>     and the WAKE-REPORT are the integrator's.
> · **The cause (0e1626b1).** `pickLandAction` ranked untapped first, then the colour gap, then the name — and read every fetch land through
>   `landEntersTapped` (no "enters tapped" text → untapped) and `manaProduction` (no mana ability → no colour): Evolving Wilds was "an
>   untapped land that makes nothing", Polluted Delta at 10 life the same though the AI never cracks it there, Evolving Wilds with no basic
>   left the same. The SNC family land counted its filter's basic types as colours whether or not the library held one, and was
>   deliberately read untapped (its entry: the tapped reading lost to uncracked fetches read untapped — gone now that fetches are read).
> · **Part 1 — what a land drop yields** (`opponentAI.landDropYield`). An activated fetch land that makes no mana yields the land its search
>   would take — `fetchLand.landSearchOrder`, the comparator the search itself resolves in (exported, one place) — untapped only when the
>   search delivers untapped and that land has no enters-tapped text (Bloodstained Mire finding only Savai Triome is tapped); its colours are
>   every land it can find (`fetchableLands`, the search's own filter); a life cost below `LIFE_PRUDENCE_FLOOR` or nothing to find → it yields
>   nothing (pickFetchCrack's own two holds). A Landscape (it taps for {C}, cracked after the casts) yields itself plus the colours it can
>   find. An SNC family land yields a TAPPED basic of a type the library holds; none → nothing. Ranking: **casts now** (`castsOutOfReach` +
>   `landCastsNow`: the land's mana, arriving untapped, pays for a hand or command-zone card the untapped sources can't — printed cost,
>   commander tax, {X} as 1; a hypothetical permanent through `manaSources`, minted with an explicit id so no id counter moves, never written
>   back), then **the colour gap**, then untapped, then makes mana at all, then the name. ⚑ Judgement call: the gap now ranks above
>   "untapped" when no land's mana casts anything this turn — that is what "an untapped dual over a tapped-delivery fetch when it needs to
>   cast this turn; the fetch when it finds a colour it lacks and the dual doesn't" asks, and it applies to every land, not only fetches
>   (the comparison is fair only if it is one rule): the 56 ordinary-land flips are 29 untapped → tapped (a land of a colour already made,
>   or one that makes nothing now — Glacial Chasm, Temple of the False God — giving way to a tapland of the missing colour) and 27 untapped →
>   untapped (Gaea's Cradle with no creatures, a summoning-sick Dryad Arbor, Dark Depths, Serra's Sanctum, Arena giving way to a land whose
>   mana casts now or fills the gap). With nothing to cast and no gap, untapped still goes first (the old tie order — see found-not-fixed).
>   ~71 ms of a 16 s two-game profile is the land drop.
> · **Part 2 — every land search** (`fetchLand.landSearchPickOrder`, replacing the fetch-only `isFetchLandSearch` gate). A tutor-search from
>   the library (Demonic Consultation's name pick is not one) whose every filter alternative names a land ("basic land", "Forest", "Plains,
>   Island, Swamp, or Mountain", "snow land", "land"), to the battlefield, hand or top — not the graveyard — takes `landSearchOrder`: the
>   unmet pips of the hand and command zone in the colours it makes, then all their pips, then the old order. Each pick is read afresh, so
>   Cultivate / Kodama's Reach put the most-needed colour onto the battlefield and the next need into the hand. Kept on the old order: any
>   non-land alternative ("a creature or land card" — Archdruid's Charm, Moonsilver Key), "a card", a graveyard destination, a land put
>   from the hand (Growth Spiral, Uro — the same choice kind, no search).
> · **Tests changed on purpose:** `fetchLandCrack.test.js`'s control "Rampant Growth takes the Forest" is now the witness "takes the Swamp";
>   `sncFetchLands.test.js`'s control "the Overlook over Dimir Guildgate (it is not ranked as the tapped land it becomes)" is now the witness
>   "Dimir Guildgate over the Overlook", and its land-drop fixture's library gained a Swamp (the family land's colours are now the
>   library's — with only a Forest, Maestros Theater finds nothing).
> · ⚠️ **Found, not fixed:** (1) The land-search score weighs colours only: it takes a land that enters tapped over one that doesn't
>   (Nature's Lore: Breeding Pool → Spara's Headquarters; Three Visits → Ketria / Indatha Triome; the fetch's Marsh Flats → Savai Triome),
>   and a colour land over a utility one with every colour already made (Sowing Mycospawn / Crop Rotation: Ancient Tomb → Forest, City of
>   Brass) — fetchLand.js:155 `colourScore`. (2) `landEntersTapped` (opponentAI.js:236) reads shocklands and check lands
>   ("… enters tapped unless …", "If you don't, it enters tapped") as tapped, though the AI's shock policy pays 2 life above 12: such a land
>   never "casts now", and a fetch whose best find is a shock reads tapped (Misty Rainforest → Breeding Pool, both read tapped, decided by
>   name). (3) With nothing to cast this turn and no colour gap, an untapped land still goes ahead of a tapland — the tapland should go
>   first then (the untapped one keeps for a turn that needs it); the old tie order, left for its own slice. (4) "Casts now" checks one card
>   at a time at its printed cost (no reductions, alternative costs, or a second spell the extra mana would add). (5) A land put from the
>   hand (Growth Spiral, Uro, Arboreal Grazer) keeps highest mana value, then name.
> · Witness: `fetchLandDrop.test.js` (27 — 17 witnesses, 10 controls). Updated: `fetchLandCrack.test.js` (25), `sncFetchLands.test.js` (16).

> · **The bug** (found by the opponent-scoped damage slice; reproduced). The {X} lane in `legalChoices.actionsActivateAbility` built its
>   own actions above the shared enumeration and carried only the costs it knew (life, energy, the self-sacrifice / self-exile / counter
>   items, the two discards): "Sacrifice another creature" and "Sacrifice a Clue" rode as `sacCreatureId: null`, and the dispatcher pays
>   only what the action names. Measured on the base engine: Fiend Artisan beside three Swamps and no other creature offered X = 1 and X = 2;
>   with two other creatures it offered one action per X and none named a victim; Phyrexian Altar + the only other creature + one Swamp
>   offered X = 1 (the Altar counted, its only food the Artisan's own victim); Alquist Proft with no Clue offered X = 1. The tap-others,
>   counted-sacrifice, return-a-land and unattach costs were dropped the same way (probe texts — no bundled card carries one beside a
>   modeled {X}), and the exile-from-graveyard cost refused the whole ability. The lane also expanded its targets without the source, so a
>   creature's {X} ability could target a creature with protection from creatures (the printed-cost lane already passed it).
> · **The fix** (legalChoices only; the dispatcher already paid every field). The X choice is one more dimension of the shared lane: the
>   victim pools (sacOther, sacCount, tapCreature, returnLand, unattachEquipment, exileGyCount, the discards) are gathered for an {X}
>   ability as for any other; each per-victim affordability check is a function of the cost it judges — the printed cost, or X = 1
>   (`gateCost`) above the walk, then every X from 1 up to the pool-plus-sources ceiling (X_CHOICE_CAP) per victim set, stopping at the first
>   X that set can't pay (monotonic); the targets are expanded once per X with `{ sourceId, xValue }` (the Candelabra ordering kept) and
>   shared by every victim; one push builds every activation, `xValue` and the "X=N: " text prefix only on the {X} lane. A victim the effect
>   targets is skipped as on the printed-cost lane. Refused, FN-safe, no bundled carrier: an {X} cost with a "Sacrifice X <subtype>" cost
>   (two X choices), and exile-from-graveyard with "Sacrifice X" (the γ1e lane still builds its own action). The victim policy is the
>   printed-cost lane's: one action per legal victim (the player's pick); each victim is its own (an Altar never eats it — the 151790b4
>   reserved set — and a one-shot mana victim such as an Eldrazi Spawn is never also cracked); a repeatable mana creature may tap for mana
>   and then be the victim (Llanowar Elves pays X = 1 and is sacrificed).
> · **Reach** (the engine's own parse over every bundled card): 152 activated abilities with {X} in the cost; 25 parse a modeled cost with a
>   non-mana item, 10 of them modeled (Fiend Artisan — sacrifice another creature; Alquist Proft — sacrifice a Clue; Cackling Witch —
>   discard; Latulla — discard two; Cinder Elemental, Goblin Dynamo, Pain Kami, Mask of the Jadecrafter, Snake Basket, Treasure Vault —

>   vs this tree, over all 24 cards with a modeled {X} ability: **8 change** — Fiend Artisan and Alquist Proft gain their victims (Artisan 9
>   offers → 18, one per creature per X; Alquist 7 → 7, each naming the Clue), Cackling Witch, Cinder Elemental, Goblin Dynamo, Pain Kami,
>   Jiwari and Latulla lose only their Beloved Chaplain targets; the other 16 (Candelabra of Tawnos, Magus of the Candelabra, Kessig Wolf

>   abilities they hold are Candelabra of Tawnos and Magus (cdh), Kessig Wolf Run (Wolverine, Jurassic Ramp) and Treasure Vault (Kinnan).
>   No tier moves: Fiend Artisan and Alquist Proft were credited native off the dropped cost and are now played faithfully, so the credit
>   stands.
