> `fetchLandCrack.test.js` written first: 12 of the first 23 seen to fail on the base engine on assertions (the 11 controls pass on both);
> with the two tests added while building, 13 of the final 25 fail on the untouched 33e3c9c6 archive on assertions, the 12 controls pass on
> both. A/B **80 seeded commander games** (base seed 7, 10 per pod, the 30 profile decks, default AI; base = the untouched 33e3c9c6 archive):
> fetch activations **0 → 207** (172 life paid; every search found a land), **11 byte-identical, 69 change picks — every first divergence is a
> fetch crack**, 29 winners change, turn counts move in 57, 0 errors on either tree (80 / 80 completed), results ai-wins 57 → 54 / user-wins
> 23 → 26 (an outcome, not the grade); 180 s / 331 s per batch (the after batch ran beside the lint; an identical instrumented rerun took
> 196 s). Committed on `day/fetchcrack`, not pushed; the release-batch line and the WAKE-REPORT are the integrator's.
> · **The cause (probed on 33e3c9c6).** `pickSafeAbilityActivation` (opponentAI.js:1582 at the base) skips every activation with `sacSelf`
>   or a life cost, and nothing else in `pickAction` took a fetch: with Evolving Wilds and a basic in the library the AI passed. At scale, the
>   base batch: 0 fetch activations in 80 games while the AI played 207 fetch lands as land drops (the land drop reads one as an untapped land).
> · **The timing the engine allows.** Every activated ability is offered on its controller's own main phase only (legalChoices.js
>   `actionsActivateAbility`, `mainWindow`; the combat and stack windows admit only combat-role and stack-copy abilities), so there is no
>   opponent's-end-step crack to choose: the AI cracks in its own main phase.
> · **The policy** — `fetchLand.js` (new, a leaf over the parser, the tutor filter and manaModel) + `opponentAI.pickFetchCrack`. A fetch land
>   is an offered activation of a land on the battlefield that taps and sacrifices it, costs no mana and nothing but life, targets nothing,
>   and runs exactly one search for ONE card to the battlefield whose every filter group names a land (`fetchCrackAtom` over the action,
>   `fetchLandAbility` over the card — the parsed ability, never the text). Corpus: 32 lands (the Zendikar / Onslaught ten and Prismatic
>   Vista, the five Mirage fetches, the ten MH3 Landscapes, Evolving Wilds, Terramorphic Expanse, Fabled Passage, Escape Tunnel, Hobbit
>   Hole, Vibrant Cityscape); every other sacrifice-self ability stays skipped (Sakura-Tribe Elder, Mind Stone, the Panoramas, Terminal
>   Moraine — pinned). Cracked only in the AI's own main phase with the stack empty; only while the library holds a land the search finds
>   (the search's own `cardMatchesTutorFilter`); and a life cost only when it leaves the AI at `LIFE_PRUDENCE_FLOOR` (10) or more — the floor
>   Castle Locthwain's loss and the alternative-cost life payments use (life 11 pays, life 10 holds). A fetch land that makes no mana of its
>   own is cracked right after the land drop and BEFORE the casts (an untapped fetched land pays for this turn's spells; a tapped one costs
>   nothing to fetch now); one that taps for mana (the Landscapes' "{T}: Add {C}.") only from the ability block, after the casts, while it
>   is untapped, and only when it finds a colour the hand needs and no battlefield source makes. Deterministic: untapped delivery first, then
>   name, then id. The policy key `fetch` ("v1" = the old hold) joins POLICY_KEYS.
> · **The search** — `runProgram.autoPickTutorCandidate` asks `fetchLand.fetchedLandScore`, which answers only for a fetch land's own search
>   (a one-card search to the battlefield, resumed from an ability whose program is a fetch's search, its source — sacrificed to pay for it —
>   a fetch land by name in a graveyard or exile): per candidate, the hand's and command zone's pips in the colours it makes (manaProduction)
>   that no battlefield source makes, then all their pips in those colours; the old order (highest mana value, then name, then id) breaks
>   ties. Every other search keeps the old order (Rampant Growth pinned). `colourNeed` is the one reader: `pickLandAction` takes its `needed`
>   set from it, moved byte-identical. In the batch (an instrumented rerun in a scratch copy, its 80 games byte-identical to the after
>   batch): 207 fetch searches, **114 take a different land than the old order** (44 for more unmet pips, 70 for the colour the hand asks
>   most — Marsh Flats: Blood Crypt → Savai Triome; Scalding Tarn: Island → Steam Vents; Misty Rainforest: Forest → Overgrown Tomb;
>   Bloodstained Mire: Mountain → Taiga), 93 the same; held 17 turns at the life floor (life 1–10) and 3 with no findable land left.
> · **Decks** (each holds at least one fetch land; cracks in the batch): Earth Bent 23, Believe it! 15, Halfshell heroes 15, Did you say
>   Dragons? 13, Teval 13, Atraxa Superfriends 13, Shalai and Hallar 12, Killer Turts 10, Captain America 10, cdh 9, Wolverine 8, Vihaan 7,
>   Jurassic Ramp 7, Kinnan 7, Nekusar Wheels 7, Kellan 6, Squirrel Girl 5, Zaxara 5, Otharri 5, Hulk Smash 5, Test Rashmi 5, Veyran 3,
>   Mothman 2, Brago Blink 2 — all 24. Not holding one: Omnath, Locus of Mana, Slivers, Bumble Flower Combo, Shorikai, Thrun, Light-Paws.
> · ⚠️ **Found, not fixed:** (1) The land drop still reads every fetch land as an UNTAPPED land that makes no colour (`pickLandAction`,
>   opponentAI.js:278 — `landEntersTapped`, :236, matches only "enters tapped"; manaProduction reads nothing), so a tapped-delivery fetch
>   (Evolving Wilds, Terramorphic Expanse, Fabled Passage, Escape Tunnel, Vibrant Cityscape) was the land drop 34 times in the after batch,
>   21 of them with another land offered — now cracked for a tapped land, where it was a dead land. Next: read a fetch land as what it
>   fetches (tapped delivery → tapped, its findable colours toward the gap, under the life floor → a land that makes nothing), then give the
>   SNC family its deferred tapped reading (the SNC entry below). (2) Every other land search still takes the highest mana value, then the
>   alphabetically first name (runProgram.js:384) — Rampant Growth, Cultivate, Kodama's Reach, Farseek, Nature's Lore, Three Visits,
>   Sakura-Tribe Elder, Wood Elves, the SNC family's enters trigger; the reader is in place, widening `fetchedLandScore`'s gate is the change,
>   measured on its own. (3) Fetch lands with a mana cost are not cracked — the Panoramas, Promising Vein, Shire Terrace, Terminal Moraine,
>   Warped Landscape, Urza's Cave (each also taps for {C}: cracking trades a source and a mana for a tapped land; a leftover-mana rule like
>   the Landscapes' is the shape), Myriad Landscape and Blighted Woodland (two lands). (4) No instant-speed crack for anyone: the engine offers
>   activated abilities on the controller's own main phase only (legalChoices.js:2447). (5) Fabled Passage's "Then if you control four or

>   (6) The AI can cast an instant while its own fetch ability is on the stack (game 59: Worldly Tutor above its Flooded Strand) —

> ## 🔧 2026-10-17 — FIX (false positive): a reflexive trigger chooses its targets when IT goes on the stack (CR 603.12, 603.3d) — Smoke Bomb (EDHREC #4790, credited native, never did anything: its own "All creatures have shroud" met the follow-up's target at the parent's flush, so the upkeep trigger was removed and the artifact never sacrificed) now sacrifices itself and makes a creature unblockable; Primal Witchstalker and Yathan Roadwatcher mill even with nothing to return and can return what they milled; Dream Eater surveils with no opposing nonland permanent; Faebloom Trick is cast with no opposing creature; Red Hulk's and The Royal Scions' damage become abilities of their own · **±0** · snapshot native 15,518 unchanged
> Suite **20,649 green (1 skipped) / 1,873 files** under the gate queue (with the rules index built for the run and deleted after). Lint 0 (CR citations: 0 of 11,475 name no rule; keyword citations: 0 of 2,374 cite a different keyword). Flip-diff
> **0 / 0 / RETIERED 0** (34,620 cards; before = an untouched `git archive` of 33e3c9c6, snapshotted before the first edit; native+land
> 15,518 of 34,584 snapshot names on both — no tier moved). `program-fingerprint`: 7 cards' parses move, each by the one new
> `reflexiveTrigger` stamp — Smoke Bomb, Primal Witchstalker, Yathan Roadwatcher, Dream Eater, Faebloom Trick, Red Hulk, and The Last
> Ronin's chapter II (body-only; chapter III unread); the loyalty parse, outside the fingerprint, moves The Royal Scions' −8 and Ajani,
> Nacatl Avenger's 0 (body-only) the same way. **Mutants 8/8** on assertions, each restored byte-identical (sha256). Witness
> `reflexiveTriggerTargets.test.js` written first: **13 of its 24 tests fail on the untouched 33e3c9c6 archive on assertions**, the 11
> controls pass on both. A/B **80 seeded commander games** (base seed 7, 10 per pod, the 30 profile decks, default AI; base = the
> untouched 33e3c9c6 archive): **80 / 80 byte-identical** (every decision row, log hash, winner and turn count), 0 errors on either tree,
> results unchanged (ai-wins 57 / user-wins 23) — expected: of the changed cards only Red Hulk sits in a profile deck (Hulk Smash, seated
> in games 40–49), and no game's log names it. The harness sees the engine (hollow-gate check): the same batch with one basic swapped for
> Smoke Bomb in 27 decks — base: cast 46 times, its trigger removed 134 times, never sacrificed, no creature made unblockable; after: 32
> sacrifices by its trigger, 24 creatures made unblockable, 8 reflexives removed for want of a creature; 49 games byte-identical, 31 change
> picks (most first diverge at a priority pass where base took an action — read as the reflexive's own stack window, not traced
> game by game), 7 winners change, 0 errors on either tree. Committed on
> `day/reflextgt`, not pushed; the release-batch line and the WAKE-REPORT are the integrator's.
> · **The bug** (found in the SNC fetch-land slice, reproduced on 33e3c9c6). `parser.matchReflexiveTrigger` folds "<primary>. When you do,
>   <reflexive>." into ONE program, so a targeted reflexive atom was enumerated with the parent's targets — at the parent's flush (or cast,
>   or activation), before the primary's action. A reflexive triggered ability triggers during the resolution, when the action happens
>   (CR 603.12), and is put on the stack the next time a player would receive priority, its targets chosen then (CR 603.3d → 601.2c); the
>   bundled rulings for Smoke Bomb, Yathan Roadwatcher, Faebloom Trick, Dream Eater and Awaken the Honored Dead say so in as many words.
>   Smoke Bomb: no creature can be targeted while it is on the battlefield, so its upkeep trigger was removed (`trigger-removed-no-target`)
>   every turn and it was never sacrificed. Primal Witchstalker / Yathan Roadwatcher: with no land / creature card in the graveyard before
>   the mill, the whole enters trigger was removed — no mill, no return — and a milled card could never be the target. Dream Eater: no
>   opponent nonland permanent → no surveil. Faebloom Trick: not castable without an opposing creature (the spell itself has no target).
> · **The fix — one mechanism, four seams.** (1) `matchReflexiveTrigger` stamps `reflexiveTrigger` on the reflexive's atoms when the
>   reflexive names a chosen target (`programNeedsChosenTarget`) the trigger chooser can place on a side (`programTriggerTargetsResolvable`).
>   (2) `targeting.expandAtoms` skips a stamped atom (keeping its index, as for kicked-only atoms) — so the parent offers / locks no target
>   for it at cast, activation or flush. (3) `runEffectProgram`, reaching the stamped run with its gate open (the `ifSacrificed` gate the
>   SNC slice put on a self-sacrifice primary is checked first), hands the run to `enqueueReflexiveTrigger`: a pending trigger carrying its
>   own program (the atoms, gates spent — it exists only because the action happened), the parent's controller and source (CR 603.7d,
>   603.7e — the spell for a spell, the permanent for an ability) and context, less the parent's per-ability resolution key. (4)
>   `gameEngine.buildTriggerStack` puts it on the stack at the next flush (`buildReflexiveTriggerStack`): the same `expandCastChoices` and
>   `chooseTriggerTargets` every targeted trigger uses, on the board after the action; no legal target → removed and logged. The parent
>   still sees the reflexive's atoms everywhere else (routing, tier, the α1 gate on the whole program), so no tier moves.
> · **Reach** (corpus scan, every bundled card; text from oracle_cards.json). 236 cards print a "When you do" sentence naming a target, 34
>   credited native. Behaviour changes for the 7 natives above (the five fixes; Red Hulk's damage and The Royal Scions' −8 damage now wait
>   on the stack after the counter / the draw — same amount, same chooser, a priority window between). Untouched by design: the 13
>   optional-primary natives (Fireblade Artist, Cornered Crook, Shrapnel Slinger, Selfcraft Mechan, General Traag, Unscrupulous Contractor,
>   Tether Technician, Inti, Kappa Tech-Wrecker, Forgehammer Centurion, Sutina, Awaken the Honored Dead, Generous Plunderer) —
>   below; Undead Butler and Paramecia Coloniex (the optional-exile-self payment wrapper: target at the flush with the
>   exiled card excluded — the same pool the rule gives); Ancient Bronze Dragon (the roll fold upstream; the roll can't change what is
>   legal); Earth Rumble (its fight pair is "ambiguous" to the chooser, so it keeps the cast-time pick it had rather than become a trigger
>   the flush would hand to the Arbiter); the ten conspire / casualty spells (their "When you do, copy …" is the keyword's, read elsewhere).
> · **Judgment calls.** (a) The optional-primary fold ("You may <cost>. When you do, <targeted payoff>", `matchOptionalReflexiveTrigger`)
>   keeps its flush-time target: the AI's optional-effect autopilot always takes the "may" (learnSession's `optionalAutoTakeValue`
>   fallback), so with the target moved after the action it would sacrifice / discard / bounce into a payoff with no legal target —
>   today's flush removes that trigger before the question is asked. Splitting it needs a take/decline read of the payoff's targets first.
>   (b) A human seat no longer picks the target of Faebloom Trick's tap or The Royal Scions' −8 damage at cast / activation: the reflexive
>   is a trigger, and the engine has no interactive trigger-target choice for any seat — `chooseTriggerTargets` picks (enemy-side here),
>   as it does for every other trigger. (c) A source-scoped trigger multiplier (Annie Joins Up, Katara, Cloud) now sees the reflexive as a
>   triggered ability of its source (CR 603.7e) and can multiply it; folded inline it never could. No ruling in the bundled data settles
>   it either way.
> · ⚠️ **Found, not fixed:** (1) the optional-primary reflexives above — Awaken the Honored Dead's chapter III can't return the card it
>   discards (the bundled ruling says it may) and is removed outright when the graveyard holds no creature or land card
>   (parser.js `matchOptionalReflexiveTrigger`, ~line 2172; the autopilot at learnSession.js:1884). (2) The scaled-damage arms take any
>   source phrase (`atoms/stack.js:532` "^.+? deals? damage to (.+?) equal to the number of", `:551` the modern word order), so a
>   conditional lead is swallowed: Ajani, Nacatl Avenger's 0 ("When you do, if you control a red permanent other than Ajani, he deals
>   damage …") parses HIGH with the "if" dropped. The card is body-only; whether the engine offers that loyalty line was not established.
>   (3) Earth Rumble: the earthbent land can't be the fighter, and the spell can't be cast without an opposing creature (cast-time fight
>   targets — the α1 gap above).
> · Witness: `reflexiveTriggerTargets.test.js` (24). Revised: `reflexiveTrigger.test.js` (the fold's target-opponent payoff carries the
>   stamp; Faebloom Trick's tap and Dream Eater's bounce now target from the reflexive ability, after the tokens / the surveil) and
>   `redHulkReflexive.test.js` (the stamp; the "any other target" exclusion read from the reflexive's own program).

> · **The sentence grammar** (`damageReplacements.readDamageSentence`). The consult already modeled the UNSCOPED doublers; its parse was a
>   set of partial regexes, and two of them read sentences wider than printed: "If a source you control would deal damage[^.]*deals double"
>   took Twinflame Tyrant's "… to an opponent or a permanent an opponent controls, it deals double that damage instead" as every source you

>   Anthem of Rakdos' "Hellbent — As long as you have no cards in hand, if a source you control …" without the condition (a body-only card the
>   consult still read off the battlefield). Each static sentence is now read WHOLE: "If <source> would deal [combat|noncombat] damage [to
>   <recipient>], <result>." and the "Double all damage <who> would deal." family, off the face that is up (a Class at its level, no leveler band,
>   no Room door — Torture Pit's door state isn't read), a label stripped only when it has no rules meaning (the shared CR 207.2c list, plus
>   Wolverine's "Unrivaled Lethality"; "Max speed —" is the condition itself, CR 702.178a, so Far Fortune stays unread). New pieces: recipient

>   creature / planeswalker / battle an opponent controls), "you or a permanent you control", "this creature", "equipped creature"; sources

>   vanguard gain the Hellbent condition), 2 one-shot spells no longer read as a permanent's static (Isengard Unleashed, Insult // Injury — the
>   consult reads battlefield permanents only; no tier moved). The coverage strip removes exactly the sentences read.

> · **The bug** (found while building the Gilded Goose slice; reproduced). manaSources gated each sacrifice source on "some other creature /
>   Food exists" alone, and the planner tapped every such record it was handed: two Phyrexian Altars beside one Grizzly Bears planned two
>   mana, canAfford said yes to {2}, and the cast was offered; commitManaTap added each tap's mana FIRST, then looked for a victim, found the
>   second Altar's gone, logged `sacrifice-creature-cost-unpaid` and kept the mana. Measured on the base engine: two Altars + one creature
>   pay {2} (and Grizzly Bears is offered and cast), Phyrexian + Ashnod's Altar + one creature pay {3}, two Gilded Geese + one Food pay {2},
>   two Altars + Gilded Goose + Tough Cookie pay {3} (legal: 2; the commit then threw "Permanent goose not found"), Phyrexian Altar + an
>   Eldrazi Spawn as its only victim pay {2} (the Spawn cracked for itself AND fed to the Altar), Phyrexian Tower's {B}{B} line + Phyrexian
>   Altar + one creature pay {B}{B}{1}, two Altars + one creature fund Simic Signet and still pay {G}{U}{1}, and payGenericMana (the
>   resolution layer) paid {2} off two Altars and one creature. The explicit taps were already right: after one Altar eats the only creature,
>   manaSources offers the other no more (the board is re-read per tap).
> · **The fix** (manaModel). Each sacrifice record carries its eligible victims (`sacVictimIds` — a creature / Food NOW, never the source;
>   main products and extra lines alike; an extra line's `sacrificesFood` now rides its record too). `assignSacVictims` — a distinct victim
>   per cost, depth-first under an augmenting-path bound; a record that leaves as it pays (a self-sacrifice, a depletion land's last counter)
>   takes its permanent out of every list; a source that is another's victim commits first (`sacCommitOrder`: Gilded Goose taps and eats its
>   Food, then Phyrexian Altar eats the Goose — two sources each the other's victim, two Thermopods, have no order). **Planner:**
>   planPaymentCore taps a sacrifice source (or a self-sacrificing one) only while every sacrifice of the payment can still get its own
>   victim (`victimsHold` at the snow, colour and generic picks); activateCostedInOrder's funding, activation and rest calls share one claim
>   list. **Affordability** is the same planner. **Contention retry:** when no plan pays and two sacrifice records share a victim (or a
>   victim sacrifices itself), planPaymentPasses tries once more without each contended record (never nested) — Phyrexian Altar first in
>   board order took the creature, and Ashnod's Altar's {C}{C} from the same creature could no longer pay {2}; a board without contention
>   plans exactly as before. **Commit:** commitPaymentPlan commits every other tap, then assigns the sacrifices on the live board (least
>   valuable first, never `reserved`) and commits them in that order; commitManaTap pays the sacrifice before anything is added, and with no
>   victim it adds, taps and pays nothing (`sacrifice-<kind>-cost-unpaid` logged). The explicit tap keeps its own least-valuable pick.
>   `withoutUnfeedableSacSources` now also narrows each kept source's victims by the reserved permanents.
> · **The action's own cost permanents.** The commit never feeds `reserved` to an Altar, so a planner that counted one left the payment short.
>   Purple Pentapus's "{2}{B}, Tap an untapped creature you control" (graveyard recursion; Otharri the same) was offered, and paid, with
>   Phyrexian Altar eating the very creature the cost taps — phantom mana on base. The offer now checks affordability per tapped creature

>   victims by the emerge victim as castPaymentSources already did (base: Wretched Gryff offered off three Islands + an Altar whose only
>   victim was the emerge sacrifice, then MANA_SHORT on dispatch).
> · **Reach** (manaSources over every bundled card with "sacrifice" and "add" — 894 — on a board with two creatures and two Foods): **7 carry a

>   holds Gilded Goose. So the reach in the profile decks is one Phyrexian Altar, whose single-victim payments

> · **The bug** (found 2026-10-17 in the Brash Taunter slice, probed again on b28acb52). The legacy damage parse
>   (`spellEffects.parseSpellEffect`) read "… damage to target opponent" — and "… to target opponent or planeswalker" — as targetType
>   "player", the every-player pool, and that shape is the fallback every clause reaches through `parser.legacyToAtom`: spells, activated
>   and triggered abilities alike. The counters-put / counters-placed damage sentinels (`atoms/counters.js` — Shalai and Hallar, Casey
>   Jones) emitted "player" too. So Deadeye Duelist's ability was offered at `user` and `ai` both (a "target opponent" is never you — the
>   other player, CR 102.2; in a Free-for-All game every other player, CR 806.1 / 903.2; a target is chosen as the spell or ability is
>   put on the stack, CR 115.1, 601.2c, 602.2b), and so was every cast of Burning Fields, Jeskai Charm's damage mode, Vampiric Touch, and
>   the cast offer of a LOW spell (Stinging Vitriol). Triggers looked safe — the α1 chooser picks an enemy — but with every opponent
>   untargetable (Leyline of Sanctity) it found no correct-side candidate and `pickForcedTriggerCandidate` forced one from the pool: the
>   controller, where CR 603.3d removes the ability (probed: Shocking Sharpshooter, Shalai and Hallar and Casey Jones each dealt their
>   damage to their own controller, `trigger-target-forced: ["user"]`).
> · **The fix.** `parseSpellEffect` maps the printed word: "target opponent" → targetType "opponent" (the enumerator's existing opponent
>   pool, `spellEffects.addOpponents`, which the discard / draw / life / mill / edict arms already use), "target player" → "player" as
>   before; the two counters sentinels emit "opponent". Nothing else needed a change: the cast, activation and trigger-flush offers
>   enumerate the atom's pool (targeting.atomTargetSpec), `atomTargetIntent("opponent")` is enemy, the deal-damage resolver reads
>   `ctx.targets`, and the CR 608.2b re-check judges a recorded target by the same pool — so a stack object whose target is its own
>   controller (a pre-fix record, a saved game) now fizzles instead of dealing the damage (witnessed). The THAT-PLAYER rebind
>   (parser.js — "…deals N damage to target player. That player discards…") accepts the opponent antecedent too, so Carnage (Carnival //
>   Carnage's second half) keeps the HIGH read it had (the card is arbiter-spell, so nothing is offered from it today).
> · **Reach** (the engine's own parse over every bundled card — legacy parse, cast program, activated abilities, triggers — base vs this
>   tree; every changed atom went "player" → "opponent", nothing else moved): **57 cards.** 35 classify native — Aragorn, the Uniter

>   57 print "target opponent or planeswalker". **Profile decks:** Halfshell heroes (Casey Jones) and Shalai and Hallar Test (Shalai and
>   Hallar) — triggers both, so the A/B could not see it: no opponent in those 80 games was untargetable.
> · **The sibling (fixed — a pronoun resolving to the wrong subject).** "It can't be blocked this turn" (atoms/combat.js — the self arm,
>   and its except-by twin; "it becomes colorless until end of turn" is the same shape) parsed as the SOURCE whatever came before it, so
>   Assassin Den's "{3}{U}: Put a +1/+1 counter on target creature you control. It can't be blocked this turn." (native-activated) made
>   the Wall — a defender — unblockable and left the creature that took the counter blockable (probed), and on a spell (no source
>   permanent, atoms/shared.js selfTargets) the rider resolved to nothing. "It" there is the target (CR 608.2c — the rules of English).
>   `parser.bareItAfterTarget`, at sequence assembly: a bare leading "it" with a self referent, right after a clause that targets with

> · **The mechanic.** Spree means "Choose one or more modes. As an additional cost to cast this spell, pay the costs associated with those
>   modes" (CR 702.172a); a mode's cost is paid as the spell is cast when that mode is chosen, every chosen mode's cost (CR 700.2h). No parallel
>   modal path: `textNormalize.readSpree` reads the lead and the "+ {cost} — effect" lines all-or-nothing (the bare keyword, every later line a
>   mode, at least two, plain-mana costs only — hybrid / {X} / Phyrexian read nothing); `parseEffectProgramInner` re-reads the modes as the
>   existing "Choose one or more —" modal (parseModal's `atLeastOne`: every non-empty subset; each mode through the full clause machinery; one
>   unmodeled mode → LOW → the original parse, the card unchanged) and STAMPS `modal.spreeCosts` (printed order). The cast lane
>   (`legalChoices` program lane, `normalCast`, beside strive) charges the base cost — taxed and reduced as computed — plus the chosen modes'
>   costs as the action's own `cost` (CR 601.2f; the dispatcher pays that object, so offer and payment cannot drift), and offers only a set the
>   caster can fund; `expandCastChoices` already drops a mode whose targets can't be chosen (CR 700.2a) and `programAtoms` runs the chosen
>   modes in printed order (CR 608.2c). Mana value stays printed (CR 202.3). Not offered: under a free-cast permission (the dispatcher pays no
>   mana for `freeCast`, so the modes' costs could not be paid — every free-cast window has its own decline), and Fist of Suns' five-pip
>   variant is never twinned onto a cast carrying `spreeCost` (CR 118.9d). A generic reduction the base cost alone can't absorb is not carried
>   onto the modes' costs (an over-charge, never an under-charge).
> · **The AI** (`opponentAI.pickSpreeCast`, new policy key `spree`, 'v1' recovers the whole-card cascade): each chosen MODE is judged by the
>   hold it would face as a spell of its own — a counter mode only at an opponent's spell over the threat bar (`pickCounterCast`), a
>   change-target mode only as `pickChangeTargetCast`'s redirect, a wipe mode only when clearly behind, a team pump only when lethal, a fog only
>   when it saves the game, every target on its atom's side (`atomTargetIntent`; ambiguous never), "each creature target player controls" only
>   on a player with a creature — then the most modes, then the cheapest, then the heaviest permanent targets; none → hold. Placed before the
>   whole-card holds, which read every mode at once (Phantom Interference's counter mode would hold its token mode too).
> · **Three Steps Ahead's copy mode** — new `tokenCopy` arm: "Create a token that's a copy of target artifact or creature you control" →
>   copySource "target" over Teleportation Circle's `artifactOrCreatureYouControl` pool (the types it has now), Sagas kept out as Flash
>   Photography keeps them out (CR 714.3a); that enumeration branch now honours an atom's restrictions (its earlier carriers have none); the
>   atom's side is own (`atomTargetIntent`). A noncreature artifact copies (a Sol Ring token — witnessed).

> later tap-for-mana offers), **5 change picks**, **0 winners change**, 0 errors on either tree, results unchanged (ai-wins 57 / user-wins 23),
> 169 s per batch on both. Rebased onto f71b7e86 (the land lines) mid-slice at the integrator's call. Committed on `day/nykthos`, not pushed;
> the release-batch line and the WAKE-REPORT are the integrator's.
> · **The bug** (the Omnath self-play lane, measured on its deck: Nykthos games net −29 per ~868 vs about −10 expected). 3d121554's generic tap
>   promotes a plain colorless permanent (every record colorless, no rider), and each `planPaymentCore` call judged "plain" from the records it
>   was handed. Three passes hand it a subset: `planPaymentOnce`'s direct pass and `activateCostedInOrder`'s funding and rest calls see only the
>   records without an activation cost; `planPayment`'s pass A holds out the one-shot records; `planPaymentRemovalAware`'s pass A the counter
>   records. So Nykthos, Shrine to Nyx (its devotion line behind {2}) looked like Wastes and spent its tap on one {C} for generic before any
>   land; so did Three Tree City and, since f71b7e86 made their second lines, the filter lands and the "{1}, {T}: any color" lands; Crystal
>   Vein and Phyrexian Tower (their sacrifice line out of pass A — the side effect ebaca087 recorded) and storage lands holding counters.
> · **The fix.** `holdsBack(s)` — a record that is not plain and not spend-restricted. `planPayment` plans with each call's own judgment
>   (plan 1, byte-identical to before: 20,000 random boards, whole plans compared); when some permanent has a plain record beside a holdsBack
>   line (`boardJudgmentCanDiffer`) it plans again counting every holdsBack line on the whole list (plan 2 — the list rides as `board` through
>   the one-shot pass, the storage pass, the direct pass and the funding and rest calls) and returns plan 2 when it pays, else plan 1.
>   `canAfford` runs plan 1 alone. Carried: the planner's record builder is the named `plannerSourceRecord` (moved as is, plus f71b7e86's two
>   fields), `isPlainColorless` at module scope. An order change only (any mana pays generic, CR 107.4b).
> · **Why two plans (measured, not assumed).** The first build used plan 2 alone; a randomized differential (20,000 boards of real mana cards,
>   bundled oracle text, the f71b7e86 land lines included; random pool, cost and spend context) caught it moving affordability: 98 flips — 33
>   payable costs lost (Swamp, Mage-Ring Network, Simic Signet paying {U}{B}{G}: the funding call took the Swamp and stranded the {B}) and 65
>   found that the old order misses. The costed pass is greedy, and what its funding call taps decides the colors left for the rest. Shipped
>   planner: 0 of 20,000 disagree, 3,063 plans differ, 0 plans fail pool + taps − spend ≥ 0. The 65 boards stay unpayable on purpose (a safe
>   false negative kept, not a new offer; pinned: Selesnya Signet, Swamp, Cascading Cataracts can't pay {2}{C}).
> · **⚑ Judgment call — spend-restricted lines left as 3d121554 judged them (open question for Colton / Omnath).** The second build held them
>   back too (Cavern of Souls, Secluded Courtyard, Unclaimed Territory, Plaza of Heroes, Eldrazi Temple, Mech Hangar and 21 more lands). Its A/B
>   on the same 80 games lost a pick: game 63, Shorikai Vehicles paid Emry, Lurker of the Loch with its Plains and kept Mech Hangar, and next
>   turn could not cast Dovin's Veto ({W}{U}); base paid with Cavern's and Mech Hangar's {C} and kept Plains + Tundra (verified by an exact
>   replay, log hashes matching the batch). A restricted line pays a narrow set of spells where a basic's color pays any, and 3d121554 judged
>   it per payment on purpose ("Eldrazi Temple, for an Eldrazi"), so `holdsBack` excludes it. Whether Cavern of Souls should be kept up in a
>   tribal deck is a play question this slice does not decide.
> · **Reach** (manaSources over every bundled mana-producing permanent — 1,832 — on a bare and a rich board, base vs this planner on Grizzly
>   Bears' {1}{G} with the card third): **55 change.** Costed 48 — Nykthos (#163), Three Tree City (#177), Cabal Stronghold (#970) and Baldur's
>   Gate (#2566) once their count is positive; the filter lands Rugged Prairie (#282), Cascade Bluffs (#291), Flooded Grove (#301), Fetid Heath
>   (#334), Twilight Mire (#355), Graven Cairns (#553), Mystic Gate (#839), Sunken Ruins (#950), Fire-Lit Thicket (#1186), Wooded Bastion
>   (#2018); the "{1}, {T}: any color" lands Talon Gates of Madara (#570), The Mycosynth Gardens (#853), Conduit Pylons, Hidden Grotto, Planar
>   Nexus, Crystal Grotto, Rumble Arena, Capital City, Unknown Shores, Artifact Unknown Shores and kin; Cascading Cataracts (#1217), Abstergo
>   Entertainment, Heap Gate, Daily Bugle Building, White Lotus Hideout, Hall of Oracles, Crystal Quarry, Captivating Cave, Hall of Tagsin,
>   Painted Bluffs, Baxter Building, Cave of Temptation, Surveillance Room, Guildmages' Forum, Crypt of the Eternals, Shimmering Grotto, Castle
>   Sengir, Henge of Ramos, School of the Unseen, An-Havva Township, Wizards' School, Aysen Abbey, Koskun Keep, Tarkir Omenpath. One-shot 4 —
>   Phyrexian Tower (#194, with a creature to sacrifice), Crystal Vein (#1488), Lazotep Quarry (#1870, with a creature), Archaeological Dig.
>   Counter 3 (holding counters) — Mage-Ring Network, Tendo Ice Bridge, Mirrodin's Core. Unchanged: the 27 restricted-line lands; Apprentice
>   Wizard. Profile decks holding a changed card: Omnath and Light-Paws (Nykthos), Vihaan, Slivers, Zaxara, Kellan, Veyran, Test Rashmi (filter
>   lands; Kellan's Planar Nexus), cdh / Otharri / Teval (Talon Gates), Earth Bent (Rumble Arena), Kinnan (The Mycosynth Gardens), Killer Turts
>   (Crystal Vein).
> · **A/B detail — the Omnath games** (pod 1, games 0–9; pod 8, games 70–79): 14 byte-identical, 3 offered-set only (3, 7, 74), 3 change picks.
>   Game 78: base paid Bear Umbra with Forest ×3 + Nykthos' {C}; now Forest ×3 + Boseiju, and Nykthos' devotion casts Avenger of Zendikar the
>   same turn — Omnath wins in 47 turns (51); Omnath wins 5 of these 20 on both trees. Game 73: the Selvala payment tapped Fanatic of Rhonas (board order) where base promoted Nykthos, so
>   the Fanatic didn't attack — turns 31 → 55, Vihaan wins both (found-not-fixed (2)). Game 9: the trees part at Vihaan's untapped lands on turn
>   21, Slivers' attack differs on turn 23 — Slivers wins both, 37 → 40. Games 73 and 78 verified by exact replays (log hashes match the batch on
>   both trees). Other pick changes: 49 (Halfshell heroes' pod), 53 (Bumble Flower's pod) — winners and turns unchanged.
> · Witness **`genericTapWholeBoard.test.js`** (15), through `legalActionsForPlayer` + `dispatchAction` on bundled oracle text unless said:
>   Nykthos beside Forests keeps its tap and then pays Rumbling Baloth off devotion; beside Sol Ring the Ring covers the {1}; Three Tree City
>   likewise; Graven Cairns filters the spare Mountain into {B}{B} for Hymn to Tourach; Unknown Shores turns it into {G} for Llanowar Elves; the
>   funding call (Coiling Oracle through Simic Signet) and the rest call (planPayment) keep Nykthos; Crystal Vein and Mage-Ring Network keep
>   their tap; affordability pins (planPayment + canAfford): the plan-1 fallback, the kept false negative; controls — Wastes, Sol Ring beside
>   Mountains, Eldrazi Temple's {C} for a non-Eldrazi (restricted, unchanged), Nykthos at devotion 0 (no devotion record — still first).
> · **Found, not fixed:** (1) Nykthos at devotion 0 and Three Tree City with no creature of its type offer no costed record, so they are still
>   promoted (judged by records). (2) The board-order tier taps a mana creature as readily as a land — game 73 above; 3d121554's found-not-fixed
>   (a dork tapped for another payment loses its attack), now reached by the lands that left the promotion. (3) A permanent with another line
>   goes in board order, not last: Nykthos on the battlefield before the basics is still tapped first for generic (only the promotion changed).
>   (4) The costed pass's greedy order misses payable costs: plan 2 finds 65 of 20,000 random boards that plan 1 can't pay (a planner-completeness
>   slice). (5) The restricted-line question above.

>   `TRIGGERING_LKI_CLAUSE_RE`). Recipients read: target opponent (the enumerator's opponent pool), any target, target player, each

> ## 🧹 2026-10-17 — HYGIENE: the silent try/catch around parseAuraBonus is gone (CLAUDE.md §1.2) · **±0**
> `auraEntry.bonusSide` caught any parseAuraBonus throw and returned null (the AI then held the Aura). A probe ran parseAuraBonus over all

> · **The bug (AI).** Since 7263caa3 every body-only Aura is cast targeting a host and the AI places it by `auraEntry.auraCastIntent` —
>   `parseAuraBonus`'s descriptors, all-or-nothing: one line about the host it doesn't model ("When enchanted creature dies, return this card
>   to its owner's hand", "has protection from the chosen color", "loses all other abilities") empties the parse and the AI HOLDS the card.
>   Only 49 of the 623 readable body-only Auras read a side (34 own, 15 enemy); 445 of the 1,274 Aura faces in all. Light-Paws Voltron held
>   11 of its 34 Auras (its A/B lost 3 games in 7263caa3).
> · **The fix (AI)** — `auraPrintedSide.js` (new, leaf: faceUp + staticAbilityParser.auraEnchantSubject); `auraCastIntent` = control → enemy,
>   untap lock → enemy, the bonus parse's side, else `printedAuraSide`. The face being cast, reminder text and ability-word labels gone, its
>   own name read as "this aura", split quote-aware into sentences; each sentence is OWN (+N/+N incl. per-count and game-conditioned, a
>   keyword or protection, "can't be blocked", "can't be the target of spells", a granted activated ability — optional for its controller,
>   CR 602.1 —, a granted trigger whose effect is plainly a gain, umbra armor, its card returning when it dies, an extra mana or draw for its
>   controller, a +1/+1 counter or untap on it, an Aura-own activation that pumps or regenerates it, cost reductions for spells targeting it,
>   a land animated), ENEMY (−N/−N, can't attack / block / crew, abilities locked or costlier, doesn't untap, can't become untapped, loses
>   abilities / keywords / card types, defender, goad, attacks each combat, its controller losing life, dealt damage or sacrificing it,
>   destroyed / exiled for being damaged, targeted, tapped or blocking, tapped as the Aura enters, "you control enchanted …", a type set that
>   replaces its card types), NEUTRAL (the Aura's own business: Enchant, Flash, split second, cycling, vanishing / fading / cumulative upkeep
>   on the Aura, channel / forecast, a colour chosen, an enters draw / scry / life / investigate / exile or destroy of an opponent's
>   permanent, the Aura returning to hand, an upkeep cost), else UNKNOWN. Consensus: any UNKNOWN, or OWN beside ENEMY → null (hold); all
>   NEUTRAL → the side the Enchant line names ("… you control" own, "… an opponent controls" / "you don't control" enemy), else null. Two
>   rules above single clauses: a restriction beside a buff is MIXED here (the bonus reading calls it the buff's drawback — this reader never
>   trades a hold for a guess); a TRANSFORMATION ("loses all [other] abilities" / "all other card types") is ENEMY as a whole — the
>   abilities, base P/T and types the same sentence gives are the new body (Darksteel Mutation's indestructible 0/1, Kenrith's
>   Transformation's 3/3 Elk, Swift Reconfiguration's crew-5 Vehicle); a P/T change in it still counts. A condition on the host itself ("as
>   long as enchanted creature is white", "as long as it's a Human") is UNKNOWN. Cached per printed card. No tier, offer or resolution reads
>   it; the non-cast entry (`auraEntryIntent` → `chooseAuraEntryHost`, and the AI's flicker gain) reads the same answer, as designed.

> · **The bug** (found 10-17 by the mana-honesty slice; every text from the bundled oracle). `manaProductionImpl`'s last arm made `{C}` for
>   any land whose text says "add" but whose line didn't parse; `coverage.landFullyCovered` reads each line through the same parser, so every
>   unreadable line counted as modelled. `parseAddClause` also gives up on the WHOLE text when an arm matches a line it can't price (a count
>   it can't read, an any-combination line behind a mana cost), so a land's plain line beside it was lost and the fallback answered.
> · **The fix, in order.** (1) The readable lines made explicit: `landLineMana(card, line)` (manaModel) is the land gate's per-line read —
>   the card's extra records, the line alone, or the chosen-colour line of a chosen-colour main (alone it has no chooser beside it; every
>   chosen-colour land — Night Market, Big Apple, 3 a.m., Valgavoth's Lair … — was credited through the fallback). Count readers:
>   `basicSubtypeYouControl` (Cabal Stronghold — the basic supertype, CR 205.4c), `creatureCardsOfColorInGraveyard` (Crypt; front face, CR
>   712.8a, 202.2), "<land type> land(s) you control" (Urza's Workshop), "other <subtype>s you control" (Baldur's Gate, excludeSelf), "storage
>   counter on this land" (City of Shadows), "any type that a <land type> you control could produce" (Plaza of Harmony, `landsCouldProduce`'s
>   `subtype`). Extra records: `COSTED_COUNT_MANA_LINE_RE` (the count / X / any-combination line behind its mana cost, an ability word and an
>   "Activate only if" gate allowed — the cost rides as `activationCost`) and `DEVOTION_TO_CHOSEN_MANA_LINE_RE` (Nykthos: five records, one
>   per colour, each its devotion, CR 700.5; land only — Nyx Lotus has no main product, parked). On a land a plain line is the main product
>   beside a count line (`honestMultiLineMain`: Crypt's explicit tap offers {B} with an empty graveyard; Workshop's gate isn't lost). (2) The
>   fallback removed: a land whose whole-card parse fails reads its plain line alone, else its basic land types (CR 305.6), else nothing.
>   (3) Planner: a permanent's several costed records are tried best first and each alternative retried (`costedActivationOrders`), and the
>   generic tap takes a permanent's biggest plain colourless line when nothing covers the cost (Workshop's metalcraft count).
> · **Every land whose mana or tier moved** (17; before → after): Nykthos {C} → {C}, + {2}: devotion to a chosen colour · Cabal Stronghold

>   Workshop {C} → {C}, + metalcraft {C} per Urza's land · Baldur's Gate {C} → {C}, + {2}: X of one colour, X = other Gates · Baxter Building
>   (land-partial) {C} → {C}, + {4}: four of one colour · Mage-Ring Network {C} → {C} (its plain line now, `requiresTap`; storage line

>   unchanged, land → land-partial. No nonland read changes.
> · **Open, not closed here:** a line that parses alone but that the whole card never makes is still credited through the single-line read —

>   null). "…is an Insect artifact creature with base power and toughness 0/1 and has indestructible, and it loses all other
>   abilities, card types, and creature types." The types (CR 613.1d) and the base 0/1 (CR 613.4b) have layer ops; "loses all other
>   abilities" (CR 613.1f) has none, and faking it would play the card wrong: (1) every reader of a permanent's abilities reads
>   `perm.card` text directly — detectTriggers, parseActivatedAbilities, parseStaticAbilities, manaProduction, combatEvasion's text
>   reads, ~200 call sites — so the only chokepoint is swapping the permanent's card, which acts ahead of EVERY continuous effect
>   (like layer 1): an Equipment's flying / lifelink / protection granted before Mutation must be lost and an earlier P/T set or type
>   add overwritten (the bundled rulings), and the swap leaks into copies (a Clone must copy the original, CR 707.2), zone moves and
>   token copies unless each is re-pointed; (2) layer 6's keyword vocabulary mixes real abilities with rules-effect pseudo-keywords
>   (cantBlock, cantAttack, unblockable, goaded, mustAttack, activatedAbilitiesLocked, attacksIgnoringDefender …) with no record of
>   "has <ability>" versus "can't …" — Mutation removes the first and must keep the second (a Pacifism beside it still binds), so
>   it needs an emitter-by-emitter audit first; (3) keyword counters (layer 6, timestamp-ordered) carry no timestamp, and the
>   name-keyed registries (layers STATIC_REGISTRY, cardEffects REGISTRY, manaModel KNOWN_ROCKS) bypass the text; (4) the
>   recursion-free partial layer readers (effectiveTypeIdentity, copyBaseOf, boardCountColors) would each need the new type-setting
>   op. The shape of the real fix: a layer-6 `loseAllAbilities` op honoured at `layers.effectAffects` (earlier ability grants stop
>   applying) and in the keyword seeds, an ability-vs-effect flag on every layer-6 emitter, and an abilities view of the permanent
>   that every text reader takes — its own program, not a card slice.

> ## 🔧 2026-10-17 — FIX: the ITERATED edict chain chooses, then acts together, one round at a time — Torment of Hailfire's rounds, Braids, Arisen Nightmare's opponents (CR 101.4); the opponents asked in APNAP order · **±0** · corpus 15,494
> Suite **19,823** green (1 skipped) / 1,827 files under the gate queue. Lint 0 (CR citations: 0 of 10,788 name no rule). Flip-diff **0 / 0 / 0**
> (34,620 cards; before = 56ed652e's code from an untouched git-archive copy, after = this tree), so every coverage count is unchanged. **Mutants 15/15** on assertions, restore
> byte-identical (sha256 of each mutated file compared after each). Runtime only.
> · **The bug** (found 10-17 by the edict slice, "still one at a time"; re-proved on 56ed652e — every text from the bundled oracle
>   index). **`iteratedEdict.advanceEdictChain`** carried each opponent's answer out AS IT WAS CHOSEN. Torment of Hailfire, X = 2, in
>   a pod with two opponents sacrificing creatures each round: Great Fierce Bee ("Whenever one or more other creatures die") ×4, one
>   per opponent per round (FALSE POSITIVE; ×2, one per round, CR 603.2c); Braids with two answering opponents: Bee ×3 (×2: one for
>   the controller's own sacrifice, one for the opponents' batch). A later opponent chose after an earlier one's permanent had left;
>   what an answer saw depended on seat order — a forced life loss or a discard carried out before a later opponent sacrificed
>   Exquisite Blood / Megrim fired it (false triggers), and a discard carried out after another opponent had already sacrificed Rest
>   in Peace went to the graveyard; and the opponents were asked in seat order from the first seat (`opponentsOf`), not from the
>   active player (ai2's Torment asked user → ai1 → ai3; CR 101.4: ai3 → user → ai1). The bundled Torment rulings (2017-07-14) state
>   the model: "each opponent in turn order makes their choice once, then all of the actions occur simultaneously, then they repeat
>   this process", and "Each repetition through this process is done separately" (CR 608.2c — each round is the next instruction).
> · **The fix — the edict chain's choose-then-batch, per round.** Queue entries carry `round` (Torment 0..X−1; Braids one round, 0),
>   ordered by **`removal.apnapOrder`** (now exported). Each answer is locked in — **`lockInEdictPick`** replaces `applyEdictMode`
>   (a stale / illegal pick is still the mandatory life loss) — a forced "life" too; the pause carries them as
>   `pendingChoice.chosen`, and `runProgram.resolveEdictModeChoice` locks the answer in (logged `edict-mode-chosen`: a sacrifice names
>   its permanent, CR 101.4b; a discard never names its card, CR 101.4a) and re-enters. When a round's last opponent has chosen,
>   **`settleEdictRound`** carries it out: the discarded cards move first (every permanent chosen for sacrifice still on the
>   battlefield, so a graveyard replacement of one of them still applies, CR 614.1a); the sacrifices as ONE event
>   (**`removal.sacrificeChosen`**, now exported — one is the single sacrifice, more `sacrificeCreaturesTogether`); then the discard
>   watchers and the life losses (Braids's draws with them) — after the sacrifices, so a permanent that left in the round never sees
>   them (only leaves-the-battlefield abilities look back, CR 603.10a); Braids's life loss and draw are its next sentence anyway. A
>   round is carried out before the next round's first choice. A queue entry with no `round` (a pause saved before this change) is
>   its own round, so an old save settles answer by answer as it did.
> · **Found, not fixed:** a life-loss REPLACEMENT on a permanent sacrificed in the same round would no longer apply to that round's
>   life losses (they go after the sacrifices, which is what keeps Exquisite Blood / Mindcrank from seeing them); no card of that
>   shape was found in the profile decks. Several players' discards are separate `checkDiscardTriggers` calls, one per player, as
>   before.
> · **AI / self-play** (the profile decks in AppData, read for these cards; no seeded batch was run). **Zaxara kinda X'ish** holds
>   Torment of Hailfire; no profile deck holds Braids, Arisen Nightmare or a "one or more … die" watcher, so no trigger COUNT changes
>   in profile pods. What can change: each round's sacrifices leave as one batch and the round's life losses land after them, so the
>   round's triggers queue in a different order (Vihaan's Blood Artist, Zulaport Cutthroat, Pitiless Plunderer, Mayhem Devil — still
>   once per creature / sacrifice); a Mindcrank (Mothman Cometh) sacrificed to Torment no longer mills for another opponent's life
>   loss in that round; when Zaxara sits in a seat other than the first, the opponents are asked in APNAP order. `autoPickEdictMode`
>   reads only the chooser's own life, hand and board, so AI answers are unchanged; a pilot that reads the state at its pause sees
>   the round's earlier answers locked in, not carried out. Seeded games with Torment can diverge.
> · Witness **`iteratedEdictTogether.test.js`** (14; 11 red at 56ed652e, every one an AssertionError; 3 controls pass on both):
>   Torment X = 2 in a pod through the real cast (Bee ×2, Blood Artist ×4, two batches, ai3's 6 life), nothing leaving mid-round and
>   the round's permanents gone before round two's choice, mixed answers (a sacrifice, a discard and a life loss all held to the last
>   choice), Exquisite Blood sacrificed in the round not seeing a forced life loss, Rest in Peace sacrificed in the round exiling the
>   discarded card in both seatings, Megrim sacrificed in the round not seeing the discard, APNAP order for ai2's Torment, the
>   chosen-log (discard face down, sacrifice named), a human opponent asked through the session driver after two AI answers were
>   locked in (then one batch of three), Braids with two answering opponents (one batch; Bee ×2 with the controller's own
>   sacrifice), ai2's Braids asking in APNAP order; controls: one opponent (two single sacrifices), every opponent losing life, a

> · **The decisions** (the 10-16 forced-pick slice's found-not-fixed (1) and (2), and the untap-lock Auras). Since 10-16 a mandatory
>   trigger with no correct-side target takes a legal one (CR 603.3d — `pickForcedTriggerCandidate`). That is the rule, and it
>   exposed `opponentAI.pickCastAction`, which never read a permanent's own enters trigger: it cast Man-o'-War with no opposing
>   creature (bouncing its own creature or itself), flashed Mystic Snake in over its own spell (countering it), cast Flametongue
>   Kavu with only its own creatures to burn. And `auraEntry.auraCastIntent` had no reading for "doesn't untap during its
>   controller's untap step" (the lock `gameState.untapAll` enforces; `parseAttachedBonus` skips the line), so the AI held Ice
>   Over, Coma Veil, Claustrophobia and their kin forever.
> · **Rule 1 — the cast-time hold** (`gameEngine.entersTriggerRemovesOwn`, called from `pickCastAction`, policy key `etbHold`):
>   the permanent goes on a COPY of the board (the stack as it stands — its own spell has resolved off it), its enters triggers
>   fire through `checkEnterTriggers` (Torpor Orb / Elesh Norn / Panharmonicon count as they would), and each is routed and
>   targeted by `buildTriggerStack` + `chooseTriggerTargets` — the flush's own code. The card is HELD when a trigger comes back
>   `forced` and would REMOVE one of the AI's own permanents or spells: destroy, exile, bounce, tuck, Venser's union bounce, a
>   counter, or damage / an until-end-of-turn -X/-X / -1/-1 counters it does not survive. A correct-side target, no legal target
>   (removed), an optional ability (declined, CR 603.5), an intervening-if that isn't met, or a forced harm its target survives
>   (Farbog Boneflinger's -2/-2 on the AI's own 6/4) casts as before. Auras keep their lane. Nothing is minted (fixed preview id),
>   nothing logged, `state` never written (witnessed). Cheap gate first: no self enters trigger that targets → no board built.
> · **Rule 2 — the forced pick prefers a harm its target survives** (`forcedHarmSurvived`, both seats): the cost is now
>   [lethal, harmed, value, power]. Among wrong-side permanents of a damage or -X/-X atom, one that survives (a FIXED amount below
>   toughness minus damage marked, CR 704.5g, from a source on the battlefield without deathtouch, CR 702.2b; an until-end-of-turn
>   -X/-X leaving toughness above 0 and above the damage, CR 704.5f — both end at cleanup, CR 514.2) ranks before every one that
>   dies; a plain tap of an already-tapped permanent costs nothing (CR 701.26a). Every other harm keeps the plain value order.
>   NOT done: "a nontoken for bounce" — bouncing a token loses it (CR 704.5d) but bouncing a nontoken costs its mana value again,
>   and mana value can't say which is worse (a Treasure vs Man-o'-War itself); that needs a token valuation, so the value order
>   stands. -1/-1 counters are not read as survived either (a 6/4 left a permanent 3/1 vs a dead 2/2 is not clear).
> · **Rule 3 — the untap lock is a curse** (`auraEntry.isUntapLockAura`): "Enchanted creature/permanent/artifact doesn't untap

>   whose mana cost names two halves rode the generic builder as one object at the summed cost: Marang River Regent // Coil and Catch
>   for ten (and on an opponent's turn, off "Instant — Omen"), Bottomless Pool // Locker Room for {U} + {4}{U}, Adventurous Eater //
>   Have a Bite for {2}{B} + {B}.
> · **The rules** (bundled CR, cited exactly). CR 709.3 / 709.3a: the half is chosen before the card goes on the stack and only it is
>   evaluated; CR 709.3b: "While on the stack, only the characteristics of the half being cast exist"; CR 709.4b: the combined colours
>   everywhere else; CR 715.3b: an Adventure on the stack "has only its alternative characteristics"; CR 202.2 / 202.2d: an object is
>   the colour of its mana symbols, a hybrid symbol each of its colours. A fused split spell has the combined characteristics (CR
>   702.102b, 709.4d) — fuse is not offered. Rooms are split cards; casting a door unlocks it (CR 709.5d) and a locked door is unlocked
>   by a special action (CR 709.5e). OMEN cards are CR 720 (cast normally or as an Omen, 720.3; normal characteristics everywhere but
>   the stack as an Omen, 720.4; the Omen shuffles into its owner's library, 720.3d); PREPARATION cards are CR 722 (the inset can't be
>   cast at all, 722.3; it defines a prepared permanent's copy, 722.3c; normal characteristics in every zone, 722.4).
> · **The change.** `splitCard.splitFaceCards` and `adventure.adventureFaceCard` set the face's `colors` from the half's own block
>   (`staticAbilityParser.colorsOfSpell` — the derivation modalDfc's faces already use; its import closure holds no shape module, so the
>   edges are acyclic). `permanentFaceCard` keeps the card's colours (they ARE the normal half's — corpus check below). Every colour reader
>   takes the stack object's `source`, so nothing else changed: the counter filters and Pyroblast/Hydroblast's restricted twins
>   (`spellOnStack.counterColorsOf`), the cast watchers (`triggers` via `layers.colorsOf`, and `recordSpellCast`'s colours), the cast
>   offer's protection read (`colorsOf(face)` into `expandCastChoices` / `enumerateTargets`) and the CR 608.2b re-check
>   (`resolutionSourceColors`). `legalChoices.castActionsFromZone`: any card whose mana cost holds "//" is skipped (a projected face never
>   does). New pure shape module `omenPrepare.js` (an omen by its inset's spell type, CR 205.3k; a preparation card by the Scryfall layout
>   "prepare" — its inset names nothing); `actionsCastNormalFaceFromHand` and an `actionsCastCommander` branch offer the NORMAL face —
>   the creature at its own cost and timing, entering with the whole card as printedCard — the adventurer's permanent-half posture, not
>   tier-gated. The Omen and the prepare copy are never offered.
> · **Corpus checks** (bundled data, this tree): the union of each split card's two half colours equals Scryfall's combined colours on all
>   103 split cards; 68 of them (136 halves) change colour on the stack, 26 offered natively (Fire // Ice, Consign // Oblivion, Order //
>   Chaos, Far // Away …). 36 Adventure halves change colour, 13 on native cards (Blow Off Steam, Steam Clean, Can't Wake Up, Scan the
>   Clouds, Seek the Heart, Overture …). An adventurer's top-level colours equal its permanent half's mana symbols on 148 of 149 (the
>   playtest Keeper of the Crown's {L}, coloured green by the data, is the exception — kept). The 86 omen and preparation cards' top-level
>   colours equal their normal half's. No split or adventure face carries a colour indicator or Devoid.
> · **Every card shape that still got a combined cast** (a census of all 884 "//" cards in the index, cast offers from hand on a board with
>   six of each basic, before vs after): **119 change, 0 two-half combined casts remain.** 16 OMEN → the creature at its own cost
>   (Marang River Regent, Whirlwing Stormbrood with its own flash, Stonehide Ancient, Scavenger Regent …; Runescale, Disruptive and Twinmaw
>   Stormbrood were offered nothing — the combined card read as an Omen spell — and now cast as the creature). 70 PREPARATION → the
>   creature (Adventurous Eater, Emeritus of Truce, Abigale, Poet Laureate and the five other legendaries also from the command zone). 30
>   ROOMS → nothing (no door / unlock model — CR 709.5d's per-door cast is not offered: FN). 2 three-half split cards (Smelt // Herd //
>   Saw, There // They're // Their) and Twice Upon a Time (a sorcery normal half outside the Adventure lane, with a cast restriction) →
>   nothing. Unchanged and out of scope (none pays two halves): 390 transform DFCs, 21 flip cards and 37 non-native spell // spell modal
>   DFCs still cast as the combined object at the front face's cost (see ⚠️).
> · **Witnesses.** `splitHalfColors.test.js` (17): Gainsay / Pyroblast / Hydroblast against Fire, Ice, Blow Off Steam, Steam Clean;
>   Gainsay resolving against Ice (the whole card to the graveyard); Kor Firewalker on Ice (no trigger), Fire, Blow Off Steam (trigger);
>   Ice may tap Kor Firewalker, Fire and Blow Off Steam may not target it, Steam Clean may; the face colours (Response // Resurgence's
>   hybrid half). Controls: Frolicking Familiar cast normally (blue), Lightning Bolt, Turn // Burn (fuse never offered; a combined split
>   source reads fail-closed in `counterColorsOf`). `combinedHalvesCast.test.js` (14): the Room, the three-half splits and Twice Upon a
>   Time not offered; Marang River Regent at {4}{U}{U}, resolving as the Dragon with printedCard, not on the opponent's turn; Whirlwing
>   Stormbrood at {4}{U} with its own flash; Runescale Stormbrood; Adventurous Eater at {2}{B} → a 3/2 with no counters; Abigale from the
>   command zone with the tax; the shape reader. Controls: Fire // Ice's two halves, Bonecrusher Giant's creature half, Grizzly Bears.
> · **AI / self-play.** Profile decks holding a changed card: Test Rashmi (Omnath profile — Marang River Regent: was the ten-mana combined
>   cast, now the six-mana Dragon at sorcery speed), Shorikai Vehicles (Emeritus of Truce: now the three-mana creature), Believe it!
>   (Joe — Consign is blue only on the stack, no longer black). Decks whose colour readers now judge halves correctly when an opponent
>   casts one: Killer Turts (Pyroblast, Red Elemental Blast, Veil of Summer), Kinnan, cdh (Veil of Summer), and the protection-from-colour
>   holders (Light-Paws Voltron's Mask of Law and Grace / Shield of Duty and Reason, Captain America's Swords, Akroma's Memorial,
>   Mistcutter Hydra, Archon of Absolution).
> · ⚠️ Found, not fixed: (1) the projected faces still inherit the whole card's `keywords` (Swift End carries Lifelink, Petty Theft
>   Flash and Flying, Yeah Nah split second) — no runtime reader reads a spell face's keyword array except Flash at the timing gate, and
>   no corpus sorcery half inherits Flash, so it is unobservable today; a future spell-lifelink or split-second reader would see it.
>   The faces also keep the whole card's `cmc` (the stack mana-value leaf reads the half's own cost by `layout`) and an Adventure keeps
>   the creature's power/toughness. (2) The 390 transform DFCs, 21 flip cards and 37 non-native spell // spell modal DFCs are cast as the
>   combined object at the front face's (legal) cost, the other face's text riding along. (3) Rooms need a door model (CR 709.5) before
>   either door is offered; the Omen spell (CR 720.3d shuffle) and the prepared copy (CR 722.3c) are unbuilt; coverage still tiers the
>   omen and preparation cards `arbiter-spell` although the runtime now plays their creature. (4) An omen or preparation card in another
>   cast lane (impulse exile, the top of the library, a graveyard permission, cascade) is not offered — the adventurer's precedent.

> ## 🔧 2026-10-17 — FIX: the edict chain CHOOSES, THEN SACRIFICES TOGETHER — each-player / each-opponent edicts (CR 101.4's own example), annihilator N one event per trigger, Planar Engineering's chosen two lands (it took ONE) · **±0** · corpus 15,494
> Suite **19,745** green (1 skipped) / 1,824 files under the gate queue. Lint 0 (CR citations: 0 of 10,634 name no rule). Flip-diff **0 / 0 / 0**
> (34,620 cards; before = 6f609d04's code from an untouched git-archive copy, after = this tree), so every coverage count is unchanged.
> **Mutants 13/13** on assertions, restore byte-identical (sha256 of each mutated file compared after each). Runtime only.
> · **The bug** (found 10-17 by the group-sacrifice slice; re-proved on 6f609d04 on real boards — every text from the bundled oracle
>   index). **`removal.advanceSacrificeChain`** sacrificed each pick AS IT WAS MADE, so one instruction's sacrifices were several
>   events. Innocent Blood with Great Fierce Bee ("Whenever one or more other creatures die") on the table: Bee ×2 in a duel, ×3 in a
>   pod (FALSE POSITIVE; one event, CR 603.2c). Ulamog's Crusher's annihilator 2: the defender's Vengeful Townsfolk ×2. A watcher
>   sacrificed early in the chain missed the later victims, and a later chooser chose after the earlier victims had left. CR 101.4's
>   example is this card: "First, the active player chooses a creature they control. Then each of the nonactive players, in turn
>   order, chooses … Then all creatures chosen this way are sacrificed simultaneously." Also: the chain asked the spell's CONTROLLER
>   first (CR 101.4 — the ACTIVE player chooses first), and **Planar Engineering with a real choice sacrificed ONE land**: its pause
>   queued only the n−1 sacrifices after the pick, and `resolveSacrificeChoice` drops the queue's head as the settled pick (probe: five
>   Forests → one in the graveyard, then the search).
> · **The fix — the N-count edict's choose-then-batch, generalized to every pool the chain serves.** `advanceSacrificeChain` takes
>   `chosen` (`[{ playerId, permId, group }]`): a forced pick is locked in, not sacrificed; a permanent already chosen is out of its
>   controller's pool (annihilator's N picks are N permanents); a real choice pauses with `pendingChoice.chosen`, and
>   `runProgram.resolveSacrificeChoice` locks the answer in (logged `sacrifice-chosen`, CR 101.4b) and re-enters. When the
>   instruction's choices are done, `sacrificeChosen` sacrifices them: one → `sacrificeCreatureEffect` (its "sacrifice" entry, the
>   single-victim edict unchanged), more → `sacrificeCreaturesTogether` (one event; every look-back read first, CR 603.10a).
>   `applySacrifice` orders every chain's sacrificers by **`apnapOrder`** (CR 101.4; the N-count path shares it). A queue entry's
>   **`group`** ends one instruction inside one chain: `annihilator.js` pools every attacker's obligation into one chain for the
>   one-pause seam, but each instance is its own trigger (CR 702.86b) — `annihilatorInstances` (parseAnnihilator still sums) gives
>   each its group, and the chain sacrifices a group's permanents before the next group's first choice. `sacLand`'s real choice
>   queues all n sacrifices with this pick at the head. Pools covered: every `what` the chain reads (creature, permanent, the typed
>   pools, nontoken / token creature, planeswalker, creature-or-planeswalker with Flare of Malice's greatest mana value, named-token,
>   subtype), every `who` (target, each player, each opponent, controller, upkeep / damaged / defending player — one-victim forms
>   stay the single sacrifice), annihilator, and Planar Engineering.
> · **The readers.** The batch entry ("sacrifice-together") carries `victims` — each one's controller, card types and last-known
>   power, read before any left (CR 608.2h). **`shared.sacrificesByIn(entry, controller)`** is the one read of "the permanent
>   `controller` sacrificed" in a single or a batch entry, and the three readers the group-sacrifice slice named go through it:
>   `runProgram.realSacrificeIn` ("if you do" — now the program controller's OWN victim: an opponent's victim used to count),
>   `countForSpec`'s `sacrificedThisWayPower` (the controller's victim in the newest sacrifice entry; none or several → 0) and
>   `iteratedEdict.applyEdictSharesType` (Braids's "shares a card type with it"). No printed card puts one of those payoffs after a
>   sacrifice that can batch (Victimize, Disciple of Freyalise and Braids sacrifice their controller's one permanent), so behaviour
>   is unchanged for them; the pins pair a real Innocent Blood resolution with the payoff atom.
> · **Still one at a time (found, not fixed):** the iterated-edict chain (`iteratedEdict.advanceEdictChain` → `applyEdictMode`) —
>   Torment of Hailfire's per-round opponents and Braids, Arisen Nightmare's "each opponent may sacrifice" are CR 101.4 choices too,
>   but each sacrifice goes as it is chosen (its modes mix life loss, a discard and a sacrifice). Nazgûl Battle-Mace's GRANTED
>   annihilator 1 never triggers (`applyAnnihilatorTriggers` reads the attacker's printed oracle); the card is body-only, so no false
>   credit.
> · **AI / self-play** (the profile decks in AppData, read for these cards; no seeded batch was run). **Earth Bent**: Planar
>   Engineering with three or more lands now loses the two lands it picks (it kept one more before) — a real outcome change.
>   **Omnath, Locus of Mana** (Kozilek, annihilator 4), **Vihaan, Goldwaker** (Grave Pact, Dictate of Erebos), **Jurassic Ramp**
>   (Silverclad Ferocidons), **Believe it!** (Flare of Malice): the victims now leave as one batch, so same-controller triggers stack
>   in a different order, and the choosers pick in APNAP order with the earlier picks still on the battlefield (the legacy
>   least-valuable pick reads no board; the policy-eval pick does, so its later picks can differ). No profile deck holds a "one or
>   more … die" watcher (Teval's are graveyard-leave watchers); Dour Port-Mage (Brago Blink) would see a batch only under an exile
>   replacement. Torment of Hailfire (Zaxara) and Tergrid (Nekusar Wheels) are unchanged in count. Seeded games in these decks can diverge.
> · Witness **`edictChainTogether.test.js`** (16; 12 red at 6f609d04, every one an AssertionError; the Braids pin and 3 controls pass on
>   both): Innocent Blood in a pod (Bee ×1, Blood Artist ×3, one batch), the active player choosing first when the controller is not
>   active (ai2 → ai3 → user → ai1, all eight creatures on the battlefield at every pause), a person asked for their victim through the
>   session driver after the AI's pick was locked in but not carried out, Ulamog's Crusher (Townsfolk ×1, Blood Artist ×2), two
>   Crushers (two batches, Townsfolk ×2), a human defender asked twice with nothing gone between, Flare of Malice (forced picks wait
>   for ai3's tie; Bee ×1), Dictate of Erebos (Spectacle of Destruction's two wreck counters, not four), Silverclad Ferocidons enraged
>   by a Bolt (a creature, a creature and a land, one batch), Planar Engineering with five Forests under Living Plane (two lands,
>   Townsfolk ×1, Blood Artist ×2, then the search), and the readers. `sacrificeLandCount.test.js`'s queue pin 1 → 2 (it pinned the bug).

> ## 🔧 2026-10-17 — FIX: a group one instruction removes leaves as ONE event — the minted tokens' end-step sacrifice / exile, a cost of N permanents, Gush's Islands, Cosmic Larva's and Planar Engineering's lands · **±0** · corpus 15,494
> Suite **19,624** green (1 skipped) / 1,819 files. Lint 0 (CR citations: 0 of 10,493 name no rule). Flip-diff **0 / 0 / 0**
> (34,620 cards; before = ca3d9822's code from an untouched git-archive copy, after = this tree), so every coverage count is
> unchanged. **Mutants 9/9** on assertions, restore byte-identical (sha256 of each mutated file compared after each). Runtime only.
> · **The bug** (probed 10-17 by the death-sites slice, re-proved on ca3d9822 on a real board — Kiki-Jiki activated with
>   `legalActionsForPlayer` + `dispatchAction`, the turn stepped to its end step, the delayed leave resolved; every text from the bundled
>   oracle index). **`removal.applyMintedLeave`** — the delayed "Sacrifice it / Exile that token at the beginning of the next end step"
>   bound to the tokens a token copy made (Kiki-Jiki, Tempestra, Orthion, The Fire Crystal, Stormsplitter) — took the tokens one at a
>   time. Each `sacrificeCreatureEffect` drains its own leave event and fires its own dies batch, so beside a doubler Vengeful
>   Townsfolk ("Whenever one or more other creatures you control die") triggered twice instead of once (FALSE POSITIVE; Orthion's five
>   copies: five times), and under Rest in Peace Dour Port-Mage ("leave the battlefield without dying") drew twice. "Sacrifice them" is
>   one instruction, one event: CR 603.2c ("it can trigger repeatedly if one event contains multiple occurrences" — its example is one
>   spell destroying all lands); CR 101.4's example says the same of an each-player sacrifice; Kiki-Jiki's bundled ruling: "you'll
>   sacrifice each of them". The exile branch already drained its leave events as one batch (nothing drains between the moves), but
>   made one zone move and one exile log per token.
> · **The fix.** The batch sequence moves verbatim from `removal.sacrificeCreaturesTogether` to **`costSacrifice.sacrificePermanentsTogether`**
>   (every look-back read first — CR 603.10a — one dies batch, one leave drain, the graveyard-replacement carriers last, a planeswalker to
>   its dispatch, then each sacrifice's watchers); `sacrificeCreaturesTogether` now wraps it with its "sacrifice-together" log, and
>   **`costSacrifice.sacrificePermanentsForCost`** is the cost of N permanents (one victim stays `sacrificePermanentForCost`; the same
>   permanent twice throws). costSacrifice imports only gameState / layers / triggers, so removal → costSacrifice adds no cycle.
>   `applyMintedLeave` sacrifices two or more live tokens the delayed ability's controller still controls through
>   `sacrificeCreaturesTogether` (one stays the single sacrifice, byte-identical) and exiles every live token in ONE `applyZoneMove`.
> · **The audit — every loop that removes a group one at a time** (`sacrificeCreatureEffect` / `sacrificePermanentForCost` /
>   `moveCardToZone` from the battlefield over a list). FIXED, same bug: the AC-1 additional cost of N creatures (Bankrupt in Blood),
>   the activated "Sacrifice N …" list (`sacCountIds` — SAC-N-CLASS Tooth and Claw / Sai / Mondrak / Zopandrel / Bolas's Citadel, γ1d
>   Treasures / Foods, γ1e "Sacrifice X") and the sacrifice-lands alternative cost (Pulverize, Fireblast, Mogg Alarm) → one
>   `sacrificePermanentsForCost`; Gush's return-lands alternative cost drained the leave events after each Island → one drain after the
>   moves; the sac-unless payment of two lands (Cosmic Larva) and Planar Engineering's forced "Sacrifice two lands" →
>   `sacrificeCreaturesTogether`. ALREADY ONE EVENT: mobilize (`applyMobilizeSac`), Living Death, the N-count edict
>   (`advanceCreatureBatchSacrifice`), the mass zone moves (`applyZoneMove`, `applyBlink`), the destroy effect, every SBA sweep.
>   SEPARATE EVENTS BY RULE (unchanged): the end-of-combat queue (each entry its own delayed ability — Mardu Blazebringer, Basilisk
>   Touch), Fading / Vanishing (each permanent's own upkeep trigger). OPEN (found, not fixed — not a local swap):
>   **`advanceSacrificeChain` sacrifices each pick as it is made** — each-player / each-opponent edicts (Innocent Blood, Dictate of
>   Erebos, Silverclad Ferocidons, Flare of Malice — CR 101.4's own example), annihilator N (Kozilek, Nazgûl Battle-Mace), Planar
>   Engineering with a real choice. A "one or more die" watcher fires per pick, and a watcher sacrificed earlier in the chain misses
>   the later victims. The fix is the N-count edict's choose-then-batch generalized to every `what` pool, with the readers of the
>   "sacrifice" log entry (`realSacrificeIn`, `sacrificedThisWayPower`, iteratedEdict) taught the batch's entry. Also open:
>   `zones.applyExileUntilLeaves` / `applyDelayedBlink` skip applyZoneMove's up-front LKI stamp (no trigger count changes — their leave
>   events still drain as one batch), and Ghostway's "return those cards" schedules one delayed return per card (a group RETURN as
>   separate enter events).
> · **Citations.** Mobilize was still cited as CR 702.174 (Gift) in coverage.js, triggers.js (twice) and mobilizeKeyword.test.js →
>   702.181a; offspring as 702.174 in coverage.js → 702.175 (the bundled CR's Offspring — the brief named 702.175 as the stale one;
>   702.175 IS Offspring, the stale number was 702.174). ENGINE-SCAFFOLD §4.7 names the batch and the open chain.
> · **AI / self-play** (the 30 profile decks in AppData, read for these cards; no seeded batch was run). No profile deck holds a
>   "one or more … die" watcher; Dour Port-Mage (Brago Blink) is the only "one or more … leave" watcher, and nothing fixed here can
>   reach it in that deck. The minted leave changes nothing in a profile game: Tempestra (Halfshell heroes) is the only minted-leave
>   card, and Donatello's extra Mutagen is not one of the copy's tokens (one copy → the single sacrifice, byte-identical). A cost of N
>   now stacks its triggers as one batch — every victim's dies triggers, then every sacrifice trigger, instead of interleaved — and
>   reads every victim's look-back before any left: Vihaan, Goldwaker (Mondrak, Olivia, Grim Hireling), Shorikai Vehicles (Sai), Thrun
>   Voltron (Zopandrel), Bumble Flower Combo (Peregrin Took's and Samwise Gamgee's Foods), The Unbeatable Squirrel
>   Girl (Peregrin Took's Foods). Earth Bent's Planar Engineering with two lands or fewer goes as
>   one batch (a land matters only when earthbend has animated it). Gush (Believe it!) is human-only. Trigger counts are unchanged in
>   every one of these decks; only the order of same-controller triggers can move, so seeded games there can diverge.
> · Witness **`groupSacrificeTogether.test.js`** (15; 12 red at ca3d9822, every one an AssertionError; the 3 controls pass on both):

>   PLAY, so a land half is played, never cast (CR 305.1: "it is never a spell"). Playing a land is one special action whatever

>   lands played as special actions", CR 305.2b refuses one past the allowance, CR 305.3 only on the player's own turn. From
>   hand the player chooses normally or as an Adventure (CR 715.3); off the stack only the normal characteristics (CR 715.4).

>   still plays), never `body-only`; a Town flips only when its land face passes `landFullyCovered` like a lone land.

>   noncreature's leave event to the finalizer, and fading.js cannot import removal.js anyway (removal → zones → enterReplacements →
>   fading is a cycle). Each Fading / Vanishing sacrifice is its own event (each permanent's own trigger), read off the live board
>   after a vanishing counter came off; the Saga is re-read live too. ② moves to **`removal.applyMobilizeSac`** (registered in
>   `removalResolvers`; tokens.js keeps the mint half and the sentinel parser — tokens cannot import removal, removal imports tokens):
>   the delayed trigger resolves inside a resolution, and "sacrifice them" is ONE event, so **`sacrificeCreaturesTogether`** — each

> · **Every battlefield → graveyard move in the engine (the audit — `moveCardToZone` from "battlefield" toward "graveyard", plus every
>   `checkDiesTriggers` input):** the cost sacrifice (costSacrifice.js), the single and batch effect sacrifices (removal.js), the
